title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午秋天下復當鄉試應
天府臣預疏請
上命臣自强臣大臨往典試事翌日
陛辭
上賜之酒饌臣自惟庸下往三分校
禮闈今荷
===
皇上拔之
經筵列之史局玆又承乏之輟
講纂膺是役視昔益專以重懼無
以稱任使也行則相與慄慄然
旣至見同考知縣臣世武臣戴
臣成位學正臣祥麟教諭臣啓
明臣肇梓臣用懋臣學成臣秉
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午秋，天下復當鄉試，應天府臣預疏請，上命臣自强、臣大臨往典試事。翌日陛辭，上賜之酒饌。臣自惟庸下，往三分校禮闈，今荷皇上拔之經筵，列之史局，玆又承乏之輟講纂，膺是役，視昔益專以重，懼無以稱任使也。行則相與慄慄然。旣至，見同考知縣臣世武、臣戴、臣成位，學正臣祥麟，教諭臣啓明、臣肇梓、臣用懋、臣學成、臣秉
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the gengwu year of the Longqing reign [1570], the Provincial Examination was once again due throughout the empire. Your servant Yu of Yingtian Prefecture submitted a memorial requesting action, and His Majesty ordered your servants Ziqiang and Dalin to go and preside over the examination. The following day, we took leave at court, and His Majesty bestowed wine and food upon us. I reflected that, mediocre and unworthy as I am, I had previously served three times as an Associate Examiner in the Metropolitan Examination. Now His Majesty has graciously selected me to serve at the Classics Colloquium and placed me in the historiographical office. Once again called upon to fill a vacancy, I have suspended my lecturing and compilation duties to undertake this assignment. Compared with my earlier duties, this charge carries greater individual responsibility and weight, and I feared that I could not prove equal to the trust placed in me. As we set out, we shared a sense of trembling apprehension. Upon arrival, we met the Associate Examiners: the District Magistrates, your servants Shiwu, Dai, and Chengwei; the School Instructor, your servant Xianglin; and the School Instructors, your servants Qiming, Zha梓 [Zhaozi], Yongmao, Xuecheng, and Bing…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
〔臣日宣臣良貴兩〕翼翼然提調
府丞臣有嵩兢兢然監試御史
〔臣嘉賓臣龍〕肅肅然百執事秩
秩然臣則又率簾以內諸臣誓
竭公慎而奉例增設防檢於外
御史臣王〔謠臣余一龍〕毖毖然
蓋罔不精白祇事云先是
===
皇上御極
命天下拔士之秀者府二人衛州
縣各一人貢之太學曰恩貢至
是青衿之士充滿賢關又
俞禮部尚書臣殷〔士儋〕覆國子監
祭酒臣孫〔鋌〕之請兩京增額各
十五人蓋一時
punctuated:
〔臣日宣臣良貴兩〕翼翼然；提調府丞臣有嵩兢兢然；監試御史〔臣嘉賓臣龍〕肅肅然；百執事秩秩然。臣則又率簾以內諸臣，誓竭公慎，而奉例增設防檢於外，御史臣王〔謠臣余一龍〕毖毖然。蓋罔不精白祇事云。先是，
皇上御極，命天下拔士之秀者，府二人，衛州縣各一人，貢之太學，曰恩貢。至是，青衿之士充滿賢關。又俞禮部尚書臣殷〔士儋〕覆國子監祭酒臣孫〔鋌〕之請，兩京增額各十五人，蓋一時
translation_en:
… Your servants Rixuan and Lianggui [the character 兩 is doubtful here: ?] were reverently attentive; the Proctor, Vice Prefect Your servant Yousong, was conscientious; the Censors supervising the examination, Your servants Jiabin and Long, were solemn; and all the functionaries conducted their duties in good order. I further led all the officials within the examination curtain in pledging the utmost impartiality and care. In accordance with the regulations, additional security and inspection arrangements were established outside, where the Censors Your servants Wang Yao [?] and Yu Yilong exercised constant vigilance. Thus all purified their intentions and reverently attended to their duties.
Previously, when His Majesty ascended the throne, he commanded that outstanding students throughout the realm be selected—two from each prefecture and one from each guard, subprefecture, and county—and sent to the Imperial University. These were called “tribute students by imperial grace.” By this time, students in blue collars filled that gateway to worthiness. His Majesty also approved the response of the Minister of Rites, Your servant Yin Shidan, endorsing the request of the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, Your servant Sun Ting, to increase the examination quota in each of the two capitals by fifteen. These were, for that occasion, …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
特典也於是諸曹六館所選士加
昔暨提學御史臣鍾〔繼英〕所選
士合之共四千三百有奇三試
之乃復嚴加校閱遵
恩制錄儁者百五十人并其文之
優者以
獻臣當錄之成而且
===
獻也與諸同事喜而嘆曰於休哉
東南之勝鍾阜龍蟠石頭虎踞
山若彼其奇也江淮外連湖海
內控水若彼其秀也其精英所
鍾毓與所興感多士之文如雲
擁山間風行水上又若此其麗
也而臣等得以縱觀其闓牧山
punctuated: 特典也。於是諸曹六館所選士加昔，暨提學御史臣鍾〔繼英〕所選士，合之共四千三百有奇。三試之，乃復嚴加校閱，遵恩制錄儁者百五十人，并其文之優者以獻。臣當錄之成而且獻也，與諸同事喜而嘆曰：「於休哉！東南之勝，鍾阜龍蟠，石頭虎踞，山若彼其奇也；江淮外連，湖海內控，水若彼其秀也。其精英所鍾毓與所興感，多士之文，如雲擁山間，風行水上，又若此其麗也。而臣等得以縱觀其闓牧山
translation_en:
…an exceptional act of favor. Thus the candidates selected by the various offices and the six colleges exceeded former numbers; together with those selected by your servant Zhong Jiying, Censor for the Supervision of Education, they totaled more than four thousand three hundred. After examining them in three sessions, we again subjected their work to rigorous scrutiny. In obedience to the gracious imperial decree, we selected one hundred and fifty outstanding candidates and gathered the finest of their compositions for presentation to the throne.
As this record was completed and about to be presented, I rejoiced with my colleagues and exclaimed: “How glorious! Among the scenic wonders of the southeast, Zhongfu coils like a dragon and Shitou crouches like a tiger: such is the extraordinary character of its mountains. The Yangzi and Huai link it to the outer regions, while lakes and seas command its interior: such is the beauty of its waters. Nurtured by the concentrated essence of these landscapes and stirred by their inspiration, the compositions of these many scholars resemble clouds massing among mountains and wind moving over water: such, too, is their splendor. And we, your servants, have been able to survey fully their [?], the mountains…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
水之精英曁四方精英之來萃
者爲
主上獻東南之大觀備而涓埃之微
效伸矣斯不亦有厚幸乎雖然
臣尤有欲言者臣竊惟金陵爲
聖祖定鼎之地開科取士寔玆焉始
乃其
===
制監于前代罷愽學宏詞詩賦諸
科以爲虛文不足以得士而純
用經術于其時制錄所錄率沉
浸經旨意顯語質如太羮玄酒
疏越朱絃味若音固有不盡者
存也漸涵百餘年以迄弘治正
德之間質文益茂發奥衍之英
punctuated: 水之精英曁四方精英之來萃者，爲主上獻東南之大觀備，而涓埃之微效伸矣。斯不亦有厚幸乎？雖然，臣尤有欲言者。臣竊惟金陵爲聖祖定鼎之地，開科取士寔玆焉始。乃其制監于前代，罷愽學宏詞、詩賦諸科，以爲虛文不足以得士，而純用經術。于其時，制錄所錄，率沉浸經旨，意顯語質，如太羮玄酒、疏越朱絃，味若音固有不盡者存也。漸涵百餘年，以迄弘治、正德之間，質文益茂，發奥衍之英
translation_en:
…the finest essence of the waters, together with outstanding talents from every quarter who have gathered here, presenting to His Majesty a complete panorama of the southeast’s magnificence; thus our service, slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust, has found expression. Is this not an extraordinary good fortune? Nevertheless, your servant has something further to say.

Your servant humbly reflects that Jinling was the place where the Sage Progenitor established his capital, and that it was here that the recruitment of men through examinations first began. His system drew lessons from preceding dynasties: he abolished the special examinations in Broad Learning and Grand Eloquence and in poetry and rhapsody, judging empty literary ornament insufficient for selecting worthy men, and relied exclusively on learning in the Classics. At that time, the writings included in the examination records were generally steeped in the meaning of the Classics, their ideas clear and their language plain. They resembled the unseasoned broth and plain water of ritual offerings, or instruments with open sound holes and vermilion strings: their flavors and sounds retained something inexhaustible. Cultivated over more than a hundred years, down to the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns, substance and literary refinement flourished ever more richly, bringing forth the splendor of profound and expansive learning…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
華含精光於渾厚郁郁彬彬盛
矣夷考其人多嚅咀道真敦行
彝教淹貫深而藴藉厚故其發
爲文詞則美文詞隨所任使則
勝任使如此而謂經術取士勝
於博學宏詞詩賦諸科也不亶
其然乎惟我
===
世宗皇帝入纘鴻圖作人化久我
皇上嗣承熈運文教維新宜士之應
化教而興者益雲烝霞變也顧
文勝之極其勢必至於沒質其
間豪傑之士以明道立言自許
者固有而溺於記誦徇枝葉而
志本根者尤往往見之甚且崇
punctuated:
華，含精光於渾厚，郁郁彬彬，盛矣！夷考其人，多嚅咀道真，敦行彝教，淹貫深而藴藉厚，故其發爲文詞則美文詞，隨所任使則勝任使。如此而謂經術取士勝於博學宏詞詩賦諸科也，不亶其然乎？
惟我世宗皇帝入纘鴻圖，作人化久。我皇上嗣承熈運，文教維新，宜士之應化教而興者益雲烝霞變也。顧文勝之極，其勢必至於沒質。其間豪傑之士以明道立言自許者固有，而溺於記誦、徇枝葉而志本根者，尤往往見之，甚且崇
translation_en:
…brilliance, holding a pure radiance within substantial depth: richly cultivated and harmoniously balanced—how flourishing it was! Examining these men dispassionately, we find that most savored the truth of the Way and earnestly practiced the enduring teachings. Their learning was profound and comprehensive, and their inner resources abundant. Thus, when they expressed themselves in writing, their compositions were excellent; whatever duties they were assigned, they fulfilled them capably. Given this, is it not indeed true that selecting men through classical learning surpasses the various examination categories of Broad Learning and Grand Eloquence, poetry, and rhapsody?
Our Emperor Shizong succeeded to the great imperial enterprise and long exercised his transforming influence in nurturing talent. Our reigning emperor has inherited this glorious destiny and renewed literary culture and education. Scholars rising in response to this transforming instruction should therefore flourish ever more abundantly, like gathering clouds and changing rosy hues. Yet when literary refinement predominates to excess, it inevitably submerges substance. Among them there certainly are outstanding scholars who aspire to elucidate the Way and establish enduring teachings through their writings. But especially common are those immersed in memorization and recitation, pursuing branches and leaves while neglecting the roots [?]. Some even go so far as to exalt…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
飾詖淫闒略踐履雖正文體端
士習之
德意屢釐而釁校之陋風猶故也
夫康莊坦夷而人爭趨徑者貪
其捷也正學淵源而士爭剿說
者利其便也彼博學宏詞詩賦
誠虛文由後世觀之猶不失爲
===
學之博也詞之宏也詩詩而賦
賦也今之舉業半支詞蔓語耳
在今日且敝帚視之後世謂何
故臣校諸士之文於據理敷章
氣偉而釆奇者亟取之其次則
詞約而精者其次則情辨以澤
者而支蔓叛經即湊泊爛錦弗
punctuated: 飾詖淫，闒略踐履，雖正文體、端士習之德意屢釐，而釁校之陋風猶故也。夫康莊坦夷而人爭趨徑者，貪其捷也；正學淵源而士爭剿說者，利其便也。彼博學宏詞、詩賦，誠虛文，由後世觀之，猶不失爲學之博也，詞之宏也，詩詩而賦賦也。今之舉業，半支詞蔓語耳，在今日且敝帚視之，後世謂何？故臣校諸士之文，於據理敷章、氣偉而釆奇者亟取之；其次則詞約而精者，其次則情辨以澤者；而支蔓叛經，即湊泊爛錦弗
translation_en:
…embellishing biased and extravagant statements while neglecting actual practice [?]. Although the gracious imperial intention to rectify literary style and set scholars’ habits aright has repeatedly been made manifest, the debased practices of the examination schools [?] remain as before. The broad highway is level and smooth, yet people vie to take bypaths because they covet a shortcut; orthodox learning has deep sources, yet scholars vie to plagiarize others’ explanations because they find it convenient. The examinations in Broad Learning and Grand Eloquence, and in poetry and rhapsodies, admittedly concerned empty literary accomplishments. Yet viewed by later generations, their learning would still count as broad, their eloquence as grand, their poetry as poetry, and their rhapsodies as rhapsodies. Today’s examination compositions are half digressive phrases and rambling verbiage. Even today they are regarded as worn-out brooms; what will later generations say of them?
Thus, when your servant assessed the candidates’ compositions, I readily selected those that developed their arguments on the basis of principle, with majestic spirit and striking literary brilliance. Next came those whose language was concise and refined, and next those whose sentiments were clearly articulated and richly expressed [?]. As for those that rambled and departed from the Classics, even if they pieced together resplendent brocade, I would not…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
顧矣誠欲因文占藴取學有本
源者以追復弘正之風也顧一
日之長詎敢以盡信其行乎期
得其近似者而相與勉之焉耳
夫修詞之與修行其難易未可
同語也何者文雖末技胥發性
靈其爲之也必收視反聽馳精
===
於輪扁所不能語耽思於鬼神
所或可通務淵岳其心求麟鳳
其采至於含毫損神輟篇驚夢
然而工拙竟判於才殊若此者
難乎易耶至於行則道在日用
易知簡能實心事父則爲孝子
實心事君則爲忠臣實不取則
punctuated:
顧矣。誠欲因文占藴，取學有本源者，以追復弘正之風也。顧一日之長，詎敢以盡信其行乎？期得其近似者，而相與勉之焉耳。
夫修詞之與修行，其難易未可同語也。何者？文雖末技，胥發性靈，其爲之也，必收視反聽，馳精於輪扁所不能語，耽思於鬼神所或可通，務淵岳其心，求麟鳳其采，至於含毫損神，輟篇驚夢。然而工拙竟判於才，殊若此者，難乎易耶？至於行，則道在日用，易知簡能。實心事父，則爲孝子；實心事君，則爲忠臣；實不取，則
translation_en:
…I give them no consideration. My genuine desire is to discern a candidate’s inner resources through his writing and select those whose learning has firm foundations, thereby recovering the ethos of the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns. Yet, with merely the advantage of a little greater experience, how could I dare place complete confidence in their conduct on this basis? I hope only to find those who approach this ideal and join them in striving toward it.
As for cultivating literary expression and cultivating conduct, their respective difficulty and ease cannot be discussed on the same terms. Why is this? Although writing is a minor art, it springs entirely from one’s innate sensibility. To practise it, one must withdraw one’s gaze and turn one’s hearing inward, direct one’s concentrated spirit toward what Wheelwright Bian could not put into words, and immerse one’s thought in what might communicate with ghosts and spirits. One strives to make the mind deep as an abyss and lofty as a mountain, and seeks literary brilliance like that of the qilin and phoenix. One may go so far as to hold the brush poised until the spirit is exhausted, or interrupt a composition and start awake from dreams. Yet excellence and ineptitude are ultimately determined by talent. With differences such as these, is this difficult or easy? As for conduct, the Way lies in daily life: it is easy to understand and simple to practise. Serve one’s father with a sincere heart, and one becomes a filial son; serve one’s ruler with a sincere heart, and one becomes a loyal minister; truly refrain from taking, and then…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
爲廉士實能愛則爲仁人故行
堯則堯堯爲舜則舜舜百鈞能舉卽
烏獲同稱矣若此者易乎難耶
乃士顧爲彼不爲此此臣所未
解者也夫惟能爲也而爲不
爲也而世罕可見之行是以曰
非言之艱行之惟艱矣而行豈
===
誠艱哉蓋艱在不爲也今觀多
士之文於難而勞心苦思者亦
旣習而能之矣於易而可心怡
日休者顧難之耶是故臣願與
多士勉之也夫
豐芑舊邦文獻淵藪四方操觚者
且望風思效矣而謂正文體端
punctuated:
爲廉士，實能愛則爲仁人。故行堯則堯堯，爲舜則舜舜，百鈞能舉，卽烏獲同稱矣。若此者，易乎難耶？乃士顧爲彼不爲此，此臣所未解者也。夫惟能爲也，而爲不爲也，而世罕可見之行，是以曰：「非言之艱，行之惟艱矣。」而行豈誠艱哉？蓋艱在不爲也。今觀多士之文，於難而勞心苦思者，亦旣習而能之矣；於易而可心怡日休者，顧難之耶？是故臣願與多士勉之也。
夫豐芑舊邦，文獻淵藪，四方操觚者且望風思效矣，而謂正文體、端
translation_en:
…one becomes a man of integrity; if one sincerely loves others, one becomes a benevolent man. Thus, act as Yao did and one becomes Yao; act as Shun did and one becomes Shun [?]. If one can lift a hundred jun, one earns the same acclaim as Wu Huo. Is this easy or difficult? Yet scholars undertake the former and neglect the latter. This is what your servant cannot understand. They are capable of acting, yet fail to act [?], and conduct worthy of notice is seldom seen in the world. Hence the saying: “It is not speaking that is difficult; it is putting words into practice that is difficult.” But is acting truly difficult? The difficulty lies in failing to act. Looking now at these scholars’ compositions, we see that through practice they have already mastered what is difficult and requires strenuous thought. Yet do they regard as difficult what is easy and can bring contentment to the heart and daily improvement? Your servant therefore wishes to strive toward this together with these scholars.
This ancient realm, where talent is nurtured like luxuriant millet, is a gathering place of cultural learning and worthy men. Writers throughout the land will look to its example and seek to emulate it. Can it then be said that rectifying literary style and setting right…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
士習不當自茲地始乎多士文
己入式誠於其所言者而實心
行之以措諸事業以要諸久遠
使今日東南山川之勝不徒為
虛文之鍾毓與感豈惟復還弘
正之風卽古之所稱不朽者可
媲美矣多士皆以豪傑自期待
===
豪傑之士雖無聖人猶興況
聖人在上而臣猶亹亹者慮多士之
興於文而未盡興於行也夫順
風而呼則其聲加疾而及者遠
金陵首善之地囦曩時聲教之
所由四達者也故臣以此風多
士冀多士之嚮風也且因之以
punctuated:
士習，不當自茲地始乎？多士文己入式，誠於其所言者，而實心行之，以措諸事業，以要諸久遠，使今日東南山川之勝不徒為虛文之鍾毓與感，豈惟復還弘正之風？卽古之所稱不朽者，可媲美矣。多士皆以豪傑自期待。
豪傑之士，雖無聖人猶興，況聖人在上！而臣猶亹亹者，慮多士之興於文而未盡興於行也。夫順風而呼，則其聲加疾，而及者遠。金陵首善之地，囦曩時聲教之所由四達者也，故臣以此風多士，冀多士之嚮風也，且因之以
translation_en:
…the conduct of scholars: should this not begin here? Your compositions, scholars, already conform to the prescribed standards. Be sincere in what you say and put it into practice wholeheartedly, realizing it in your undertakings and seeking results that endure. Let the scenic excellence of the southeastern mountains and rivers today nurture more than empty literary ornament [?]. Would this merely restore the spirit of the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns? You could rival even those whom the ancients called immortal. All you scholars aspire to become men of outstanding talent and resolve.
Men of outstanding talent and resolve rise to action even without a sage; how much more so when a sage reigns above! Yet your servant continues to exhort you tirelessly because he fears that you scholars have risen to achievement in writing but have not fully done so in conduct. When one calls with the wind, the voice carries more forcefully and reaches farther. Jinling is the foremost seat of moral exemplarity, the place from which imperial instruction formerly spread in all directions [?]. Thus your servant offers these words to inspire you scholars, hoping that you will respond to this influence, and thereby to …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子謀道不謀食耕也餒在其中矣學也
祿在其中矣君子憂道不憂貧
道也者不可須臾離也可離非道也是故
君子戒慎乎其所不睹恐懼乎其所不
聞
責難於君謂之恭陳善閉邪謂之敬
易
===
以祉元吉中以行願也
九五甘節吉往有尚象曰甘節之吉居位
中也
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉
潤萬物者莫潤乎水
書
克明俊德以親九族九族既睦平章百姓
百姓昭明恊和萬邦黎民於變時雍
導河積石至于龍門南至于華陰東至于
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

君子謀道不謀食。耕也，餒在其中矣；學也，祿在其中矣。君子憂道不憂貧。

道也者，不可須臾離也；可離，非道也。是故君子戒慎乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所不聞。

責難於君謂之恭，陳善閉邪謂之敬。

易

以祉元吉，中以行願也。

九五：甘節，吉，往有尚。象曰：「甘節之吉，居位中也。」

夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。

潤萬物者莫潤乎水。

書

克明俊德，以親九族。九族既睦，平章百姓。百姓昭明，恊和萬邦。黎民於變時雍。

導河積石，至于龍門，南至于華陰，東至于
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The gentleman seeks the Way, not food. In plowing, hunger may be found; in learning, an official stipend may be found. The gentleman is concerned about the Way, not poverty.

The Way cannot be departed from for even a moment. If it could be departed from, it would not be the Way. Therefore the gentleman is watchful and cautious concerning what he does not see, and fearful and apprehensive concerning what he does not hear.

To demand difficult things of one's ruler is called deference; to set forth what is good and bar what is depraved is called reverence.

Book of Changes

“Blessings bring supreme good fortune”: through centrality, one carries out one's aspirations.

Nine in the fifth place: Sweet moderation. Good fortune. Going forward brings esteem. The Image says: “The good fortune of sweet moderation comes from occupying the central position.”

Qian, in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct. Thus it brings forth greatness.

Among things that moisten the myriad beings, nothing does so more than water.

Book of Documents

He was able to make manifest his eminent virtue and thereby bring affection to the nine degrees of kinship. Once these were harmonious, he distinguished and ordered the hundred clans. Once the hundred clans were enlightened, he brought the myriad states into harmony. The common people were thereby transformed and became harmonious.

He traced the Yellow River from Jishi to Longmen, southward to Huayin, and eastward to …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
底柱又東至于孟津東過洛汭至于大
伾北過洚水至于大陸又北播爲九河
同爲逆河入于海
所寶惟賢則邇人安
哲人惟刑無疆之辭屬于五極咸中有慶
詩
蠶月條桑取彼斧斨以伐遠揚猗彼女桑
七月鳴鵙八月載績載玄載黃我朱孔
陽爲公子裳四月秀葽五月鳴蜩八月
其穫十月隕蘀一之日于貉取彼狐狸
爲公子裘
===
彼交匪紓天子所予
其詩孔碩其風肆好
龍旂十乘大糦是承邦畿千里維民所止
肇域彼四海四海來假來假祁祁景員
維河
春秋
六月齊侯來獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕
punctuated:
底柱，又東至于孟津，東過洛汭，至于大伾，北過洚水，至于大陸，又北播爲九河，同爲逆河，入于海。
所寶惟賢，則邇人安。
哲人惟刑，無疆之辭，屬于五極，咸中有慶。
詩
蠶月條桑，取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚，猗彼女桑。七月鳴鵙，八月載績，載玄載黃，我朱孔陽，爲公子裳。四月秀葽，五月鳴蜩，八月其穫，十月隕蘀。一之日于貉，取彼狐狸，爲公子裘。
彼交匪紓，天子所予。
其詩孔碩，其風肆好。
龍旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，維民所止。肇域彼四海，四海來假。來假祁祁，景員維河。
春秋
六月，齊侯來獻戎捷。〔莊公三十有一年〕
translation_en:
…Dizhu; then eastward to Mengjin, eastward past the mouth of the Luo to Dapi, northward past the Jiang River to Dalu, and farther north, branching into the Nine Rivers. These unite as the Ni River and enter the sea.
If those whom you treasure are the worthy, the people nearby will be at peace.
The wise adjudicate the countless pleas, referring them to the five standards of punishment. When all judgments strike the proper mean, blessings follow.
Book of Odes
In the silkworm month, we prune the mulberries. Taking axes and hatchets, we cut off the high, spreading branches and bend down the young mulberry trees. In the seventh month the shrike calls; in the eighth month we begin spinning. We dye the cloth black and yellow; our vermilion is brilliantly bright, for the young lord’s lower garments. In the fourth month the yao plant flowers; in the fifth month the cicadas call. In the eighth month comes the harvest; in the tenth month the leaves fall. In the first month we hunt badgers, taking foxes and wildcats to make fur robes for the young lord.
Those who are unremitting in their attendance receive gifts from the Son of Heaven.
His poem is truly grand; its airs are most fine.
Ten chariots bear dragon banners, presenting great offerings of sacrificial grain. The royal domain extends a thousand li: here the people dwell. He first established the bounds of the lands within the Four Seas, and from the Four Seas they come. They come in great multitudes; the vast surrounding territory reaches the Yellow River [?].
Spring and Autumn Annals
In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present the spoils of victory over the Rong. 〔Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang.〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
月癸丑公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯
衛子莒子盟于踐土〔僖公二十有八年〕
六月癸酉季孫行父臧孫許叔孫僑如
公孫嬰齊帥師會晉郤克衛孫良夫曹
公子首及齊侯戰于鞌齊師敗績〔成公〕
二年
冬十月不雨〔僖公二年〕春王正月不雨夏
四月不雨　六月雨〔僖公三年〕
夏五月公自京師遂會晉侯齊侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯邾人滕人伐秦〔成公十有〕
三年
===
冬楚公子結帥師伐陳吳救陳〔哀公十年〕
禮記
知其義而敬守之天子之所以治天下也
天下大定然後正六律和五聲弦歌詩頌
此之謂德音德音之謂樂
百官得其宜萬事得其序
溫良者仁之本也敬慎者仁之地也寬裕
punctuated:
月癸丑，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子，盟于踐土〔僖公二十有八年〕。
六月癸酉，季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌，齊師敗績〔成公〕二年。
冬十月，不雨〔僖公二年〕。春王正月，不雨；夏四月，不雨；六月，雨〔僖公三年〕。
夏五月，公自京師遂會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人、滕人伐秦〔成公十有〕三年。
冬，楚公子結帥師伐陳，吳救陳〔哀公十年〕。
禮記
知其義而敬守之，天子之所以治天下也。
天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌，此之謂德音。德音之謂樂。
百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
溫良者，仁之本也；敬慎者，仁之地也；寬裕
translation_en:
… month, on the guichou day, the Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju to conclude a covenant at Jiantu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕

In the sixth month, on the guiyou day, Jisun Xingfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led an army and joined forces with Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Prince Shou of Cao. They fought the Marquis of Qi at An, and the army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Duke Cheng,〕 second year.

In winter, in the tenth month, there was no rain. 〔Second year of Duke Xi.〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, there was no rain; in summer, in the fourth month, there was no rain; in the sixth month, it rained. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕

In summer, in the fifth month, the Duke proceeded from the royal capital to join the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu and Teng in attacking Qin. 〔Duke Cheng, thirteenth〕 year.

In winter, Prince Jie of Chu led an army to attack Chen. Wu came to Chen’s aid. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ai.〕

Record of Rites (Liji)

To understand its meaning and reverently observe it is the means by which the Son of Heaven governs all under Heaven.

Only after all under Heaven is firmly settled are the six pitch standards rectified, the five tones harmonized, and the poems and hymns sung to string accompaniment. This is called the sound of virtue. The sound of virtue is what is called music.

The hundred officials each find their proper place, and the myriad affairs attain their proper order.

Warmth and goodness are the root of benevolence; reverence and caution are the ground of benevolence; magnanimity and generosity …

之和也分散者仁之施也儒皆兼此而

translation_en:
…are the expression of benevolence; receiving others with humility is the capacity of benevolence; ritual propriety is the outward appearance of benevolence; speech and conversation are the refinement of benevolence; singing and music are the harmony of benevolence; distributing one's resources is the bestowal of benevolence. Second Session
Discourse
The hearts of Yao and Shun endure to this day.
Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question from among these [?]; the transcription reads 內科一道.〕
Compose, as if for the Han court, an edict establishing provisions for relieving the destitute and supporting the aged. 〔First year of Emperor Wen's reign.〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
縱放軍人歇役
官司出入人罪
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問易稱主器者莫若長子而記著禁於未
發之謂豫之文三代所以有道之長以
其豫建元良諭教於早焉爾於稽其制
莫備於周公所以教成王者可得而言
其詳歟漢臣賈誼嘗以周制爲文帝告
見采納矣迺以景方成終有慙德何也
嗣是若帝範若戒子篇若承華要略諸
書代有作者不知與周之制誼之言有
相契合發明者否歟我
===
太祖高皇帝締造鴻業首建大本堂以爲
東宮育德之所
成祖文皇帝則又輯古之嘉言善行爲
文華寶鑑一書以授
皇太子
punctuated:
縱放軍人歇役。
官司出入人罪。
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：易稱「主器者莫若長子」，而記著「禁於未發之謂豫」之文。三代所以有道之長，以其豫建元良，諭教於早焉爾。於稽其制，莫備於周公所以教成王者，可得而言其詳歟？漢臣賈誼嘗以周制爲文帝告，見采納矣，迺以景方成，終有慙德，何也？嗣是，若《帝範》，若《戒子篇》，若《承華要略》諸書，代有作者，不知與周之制、誼之言有相契合發明者否歟？我太祖高皇帝締造鴻業，首建大本堂，以爲東宮育德之所。成祖文皇帝則又輯古之嘉言善行，爲《文華寶鑑》一書，以授皇太子。
translation_en:
Permitting soldiers to leave their duties without authorization.
Judicial authorities wrongfully imposing or remitting criminal liability.
Third Session
Policy questions〔Five questions〕
Question: The Book of Changes states, “For presiding over the sacred vessels, none is better suited than the eldest son,” while the Book of Rites contains the words, “Checking wrongdoing before it arises is called prevention.” The Three Dynasties long maintained good government because they established the heir apparent in advance and instructed him from an early age. Examining their institutions, none was more fully developed than the means by which the Duke of Zhou educated King Cheng. Can you explain these in detail? Jia Yi, a minister of the Han, once presented the Zhou institutions to Emperor Wen, who adopted his recommendations. Yet when Emperor Jing reached maturity [?], his conduct ultimately gave cause for shame. Why was this? Thereafter, works such as the Model for Emperors (Di fan), Admonitions to a Son (Jie zi pian), and Essentials for the Heir Apparent (Chenghua yaolüe) appeared in successive ages. Do they accord with and elucidate the institutions of Zhou and the words of Jia Yi?
When our Emperor Taizu Gao founded his great enterprise, he first established the Hall of the Great Foundation (Daben tang) as a place for the crown prince to cultivate virtue. Emperor Chengzu Wen subsequently compiled exemplary sayings and good deeds from antiquity into a book entitled Precious Mirror of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua baojian), which he bestowed upon the crown prince.

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
二祖所以垂裕後昆意至深遠矣至于
敷言貽訓見于
諭太子及
諭宮臣梁賢解縉蹇義等之詞與夫
建極叙倫章之爲身敎者皆足爲
聖子
神孫萬世楷式亦可得而揚厲之歟我
皇上踐祚之二年卽崇建
儲宮以定大本
===
聖度宏曠超越前代帝王遠甚茲
睿齡漸茂四海之內日喁喁徯其
出閣開講筵也則
二祖燕翼弘規正
今所當繹思而率由矣不知所以爲
儲宮燕閒緝熈之助者尙有可言者歟此天
下之大計臣子深願所汲汲也諸生誠
有賈生之見有司者將藉以轉
聞焉
punctuated: 二祖所以垂裕後昆，意至深遠矣。至于敷言貽訓，見于《諭太子》及《諭宮臣梁賢解縉蹇義等》之詞，與夫《建極叙倫章》之爲身敎者，皆足爲聖子神孫萬世楷式，亦可得而揚厲之歟？我皇上踐祚之二年，卽崇建儲宮，以定大本。聖度宏曠，超越前代帝王遠甚。茲睿齡漸茂，四海之內日喁喁徯其出閣開講筵也，則二祖燕翼弘規，正今所當繹思而率由矣。不知所以爲儲宮燕閒緝熈之助者，尙有可言者歟？此天下之大計，臣子深願所汲汲也。諸生誠有賈生之見，有司者將藉以轉聞焉。
translation_en: The two founding emperors’ intention in providing abundantly for their descendants was profoundly farsighted. As for their pronouncements bequeathing instruction, found in the Admonition to the Crown Prince and the Admonition to the Palace Officials Liang Xian [?], Xie Jin, Jian Yi, and Others, together with the example of personal conduct set forth in the Chapter on Establishing the Supreme Standard and Ordering Human Relationships, all are sufficient to serve as models for their sagely sons and divine grandsons for ten thousand generations. Might their significance also be further expounded and celebrated? In the second year after ascending the throne, our reigning emperor solemnly established the heir apparent, thereby securing the great foundation of the state. His sagely breadth of vision far surpasses that of emperors of earlier dynasties. Now that the crown prince is growing older, all within the four seas eagerly await, day after day, his coming forth from the inner palace to begin formal lectures. Thus the two founding emperors’ grand plans for the welfare of their descendants are precisely what should now be pondered carefully and followed. Are there further proposals for helping the crown prince continually advance in enlightened learning during his hours of leisure? This is a matter of great consequence for the realm, something that we, his subjects and servants, deeply desire and urgently pursue. If you students truly possess insights like those of Master Jia, the responsible officials will draw upon them to submit a report to the throne.

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
問孔子曰邦有道危言危行宋儒朱氏釋
之曰危高峻也夫君子之行之高峻固
無時而改矣言與行宜相顧者也奚獨
至有道之時始危其言乎且既曰有道
則君明臣良靡可指議士生其時鋪張
盛美可矣言又何危耶古稱有道若舜
禹湯武盛矣其繼體之君莫若太甲高
宗成王考之當時諸臣之所告戒類皆
警怠荒而憂危亂即中才之主所不足
===
慮而乃以言於明聖之君極治之世何
歟自漢而下固不得比於三代方其盛
時亦庶幾乎有道矣乃賈誼魏徵張昇
輩其言憂憤激切若過於事情而其君
用之不以爲怪及其後也治日以不逮
而憂憤激切之言卒不得聞然則有道
之世危言固不可少歟抑言之危乃所
以成其有道歟夫願治之君孰不欲聽
言以自廣也顧言有當不當耳即未嘗
punctuated: 問：孔子曰：「邦有道，危言危行。」宋儒朱氏釋之曰：「危，高峻也。」夫君子之行之高峻，固無時而改矣。言與行宜相顧者也，奚獨至有道之時始危其言乎？且既曰有道，則君明臣良，靡可指議，士生其時，鋪張盛美可矣，言又何危耶？古稱有道，若舜、禹、湯、武盛矣。其繼體之君，莫若太甲、高宗、成王。考之當時諸臣之所告戒，類皆警怠荒而憂危亂，即中才之主所不足慮，而乃以言於明聖之君、極治之世，何歟？自漢而下，固不得比於三代，方其盛時，亦庶幾乎有道矣。乃賈誼、魏徵、張昇輩，其言憂憤激切，若過於事情，而其君用之，不以爲怪。及其後也，治日以不逮，而憂憤激切之言卒不得聞。然則有道之世，危言固不可少歟？抑言之危，乃所以成其有道歟？夫願治之君，孰不欲聽言以自廣也？顧言有當不當耳，即未嘗
translation_en:
Question: Confucius said, “When the state possesses the Way, be upright in speech and upright in conduct.” The Song Confucian scholar Zhu explained: “Wei means lofty and stern.” Surely the lofty sternness of a gentleman’s conduct should never change with the times. Speech and conduct ought to accord with one another: why, then, should he speak uprightly only when the state possesses the Way? Moreover, if it possesses the Way, its ruler must be enlightened and its ministers worthy, with nothing to criticize. A scholar living at such a time need only expound its abundant glories. Why should his speech also be stern?

Among those of antiquity said to possess the Way, Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wu were outstanding. Among the rulers who succeeded to their heritage, none surpassed Tai Jia, Gaozong, and King Cheng. Yet if we examine the admonitions their ministers offered at the time, these generally warned against negligence and dissipation and expressed anxiety over peril and disorder. These were matters that even a ruler of middling ability need scarcely have feared; why, then, were they raised before enlightened and sagely rulers in an age of consummate order?

From the Han onward, government certainly could not compare with that of the Three Dynasties; nevertheless, at its height it came close to possessing the Way. Yet men such as Jia Yi, Wei Zheng, and Zhang Sheng spoke with anxiety and indignation, urgently and vehemently, seemingly exceeding what the circumstances warranted. Their rulers nonetheless acted upon their words without finding them strange. In later times, government daily fell further short, yet words of anxiety and indignation, urgency and vehemence, were ultimately no longer heard. Does this mean that stern speech is indispensable in an age possessing the Way? Or is sternness of speech precisely what enables it to possess the Way?

What ruler who desires good government does not wish to hear counsel and thereby broaden his understanding? The question is simply whether the counsel is appropriate or not. Even if it has never been…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
當亦可謂之危言歟抑所謂危言者必
期於當而進言者固自有道也諸生幸
生有道之時行將以言揚矣其明著于
篇毋讓
問經術者學問之本原節義者士人之高
蹈敎若無尚於此矣古之敎莫備於周
攷其制顧無所謂經術節義之名稱何
歟後世漢去周最近或以經術節義歸
之矣又皆卒不免訾議豈周之敎有尚
於此者而漢未之及歟不然何若是謬
盭也我
===
朝
聖相承敦崇敎化於學校至
加意矣百餘年閒士罔不殫力稽古雅志好
修以經術節義著見如萃於名臣錄者
槩可睹識類多兼長而尤有褎然特出
者過兩漢遠甚可謂盛矣何漸至於今
又多不類經術則安於淺陋節義則流
punctuated:
當，亦可謂之危言歟？抑所謂危言者，必期於當，而進言者固自有道也？諸生幸生有道之時，行將以言揚矣，其明著于篇，毋讓。
問：經術者，學問之本原；節義者，士人之高蹈。敎若無尚於此矣。古之敎莫備於周，攷其制，顧無所謂經術節義之名稱，何歟？後世漢去周最近，或以經術節義歸之矣，又皆卒不免訾議。豈周之敎有尚於此者，而漢未之及歟？不然，何若是謬盭也？我朝聖相承，敦崇敎化，於學校至加意矣。百餘年閒，士罔不殫力稽古，雅志好修，以經術節義著見，如萃於《名臣錄》者，槩可睹識。類多兼長，而尤有褎然特出者，過兩漢遠甚，可謂盛矣。何漸至於今，又多不類？經術則安於淺陋，節義則流
translation_en:
…appropriate, can it nevertheless be called forthright speech? Or must what is called forthright speech necessarily aim to be appropriate, so that those who offer counsel indeed have a proper way of doing so? You candidates are fortunate to live in an age when the Way prevails, and will soon gain advancement through your words. Set forth your views clearly in your essays, without holding back.
Question: Classical learning is the foundation of scholarship; moral integrity and righteousness are the lofty attainments of scholars. It would seem that education has nothing higher than these. No education in antiquity was more comprehensive than that of the Zhou. Yet when we examine its institutions, we find no designations corresponding to “classical learning” and “moral integrity and righteousness.” Why is this? Among subsequent dynasties, the Han was closest in time to the Zhou, and some have credited it with classical learning and moral integrity and righteousness. Yet these, too, ultimately failed to escape criticism. Could Zhou education have possessed something higher than these, which the Han failed to attain? If not, why was there such a discrepancy?
In our dynasty, sage rulers have succeeded one another, earnestly promoting moral instruction and devoting the utmost attention to schools. For more than a hundred years, scholars have all exerted themselves in studying antiquity and cherished noble aspirations toward self-cultivation. Those distinguished for classical learning and moral integrity and righteousness, such as those assembled in the Record of Eminent Ministers, can generally be identified and known. Most excelled in both, and among them were men of outstanding distinction, far surpassing those of the Western and Eastern Han. This may indeed be called a flourishing age. Why, as we have gradually come down to the present, do so many no longer measure up? In classical learning, they rest content with superficiality and ignorance; in moral integrity and righteousness, they drift toward…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於萎靡豈氣化之不逮前歟抑士之所
以自待者卑歟宋李復劉光祖嘗疏於
政和紹熈間矣不知其說於今有足鏡
者否歟夫經術以適治節義以維風關
於世道非眇小矣而流弊若茲識治者
能無憂乎茲欲使豐亨之間易淺陋爲
愽綜化萎靡爲耿介而德一俗同厥道
何在幸諸士究言之且將觀所以自養
者
===
問明體所以適用學術事功自昔相表裏
矣先儒乃謂志伊尹之志學顔子之學
若岐而言之何歟攷其所志與其所學
同乎否歟後世有志於事功者或日夜
興致太平或決策以安社稷或萬口稱
賢相或田野知姓名雖不得比隆伊尹
乃其樹立亦卓然偉矣而不以理學稱
豈無得於學而能然歟抑亦有所本歟
其潛心於理學者或會道有元或聞道
punctuated:
於萎靡，豈氣化之不逮前歟？抑士之所以自待者卑歟？宋李復、劉光祖嘗疏於政和、紹熈間矣，不知其說於今有足鏡者否歟？夫經術以適治，節義以維風，關於世道非眇小矣，而流弊若茲，識治者能無憂乎？茲欲使豐亨之間，易淺陋爲愽綜，化萎靡爲耿介，而德一俗同，厥道何在？幸諸士究言之，且將觀所以自養者。

問：明體所以適用，學術、事功自昔相表裏矣。先儒乃謂志伊尹之志，學顔子之學，若岐而言之，何歟？攷其所志與其所學，同乎否歟？後世有志於事功者，或日夜興致太平，或決策以安社稷，或萬口稱賢相，或田野知姓名，雖不得比隆伊尹，乃其樹立亦卓然偉矣，而不以理學稱，豈無得於學而能然歟？抑亦有所本歟？其潛心於理學者，或會道有元，或聞道
translation_en:
…into enervation. Is this because the transforming influence of cosmic vital energy no longer equals that of earlier times? Or because scholars set too low a standard for themselves? Li Fu and Liu Guangzu of the Song submitted memorials during the Zhenghe and Shaoxi eras. Might their arguments still offer a useful mirror for the present? Classical learning serves the work of government, while integrity and righteousness sustain moral customs: their bearing on the moral order of the world is far from slight. With abuses developing to this extent, how could those who understand government remain unconcerned? Amid our present prosperity, we wish to replace shallow learning with broad and comprehensive understanding, transform enervation into upright independence, and bring virtue and customs into accord. By what means can this be achieved? Let you scholars discuss this thoroughly; we shall also thereby observe how you cultivate yourselves.

Question: Clarifying fundamental substance enables practical application; learning and achievement in public affairs have complemented each other since antiquity. Yet an earlier Confucian said that one should aspire to Yi Yin’s aspirations and study what Master Yan studied, seemingly speaking of these as separate paths. Why is this? If we examine their aspirations and their learning, were they the same or different? Among later men who aspired to achievement in public affairs, some worked day and night to bring about supreme peace [?]; some settled policies that secured the state; some were acclaimed by all as worthy chief councilors; and some had names known even in the countryside. Although they could not equal Yi Yin in eminence, their accomplishments were nevertheless outstanding and great. Yet they were not renowned for the Learning of Principle. Could they have achieved this without gaining anything from learning? Or did they too have a foundation on which they drew? Among those who devoted themselves to the Learning of Principle, some apprehended the Way as having a source [?], while others heard the Way…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
甚早或學本至誠或精思力踐或窮理
以致知反躬以踐實亦庶幾從事於顏
子之學矣乃用之不異究焉豈其所學
不適於用歟抑固有遇不遇歟孟子論
伊尹愼取與於一介孔子語顏淵非禮
勿視聽言動焉則進德修業不可以泛
求而諸君子之事功學術亦必有要矣
諸士景行往哲將何所實用其力歟願
質言之毋徒以空辭相眩爲也
===
問陸贄有言克敵之要在乎將得其人馭
將之方在乎操得其柄夫被廬之謀帥
蘭陵之論將以禮樂仁義爲尚乃後世
有雅歌臨戎輕裘布信者亦有夷都坑
降見雄料敵吹簫敗繒起佐興運者王
在得人固不能盡如晉楚所云無容議
矣至於馭將之方蓋嘗歷覽古昔求所
謂操得其柄者竊有惑焉試與諸生商
之爵以正功也亡於治粟都尉者因漢
punctuated:
甚早，或學本至誠，或精思力踐，或窮理以致知、反躬以踐實，亦庶幾從事於顏子之學矣。乃用之不異究焉，豈其所學不適於用歟？抑固有遇不遇歟？孟子論伊尹，愼取與於一介；孔子語顏淵，非禮勿視聽言動焉。則進德修業，不可以泛求，而諸君子之事功學術，亦必有要矣。諸士景行往哲，將何所實用其力歟？願質言之，毋徒以空辭相眩爲也。

問：陸贄有言：「克敵之要，在乎將得其人；馭將之方，在乎操得其柄。」夫被廬之謀帥、蘭陵之論將，以禮樂仁義爲尚。乃後世有雅歌臨戎、輕裘布信者，亦有夷都坑降、見雄料敵、吹簫敗繒、起佐興運者。王在得人，固不能盡如晉楚所云，無容議矣。至於馭將之方，蓋嘗歷覽古昔，求所謂操得其柄者，竊有惑焉。試與諸生商之。爵以正功也，亡於治粟都尉者，因漢
translation_en:
…very early; some grounded their learning in utmost sincerity; some reflected deeply and practiced strenuously; others investigated principles to attain knowledge and examined themselves to put it into practice. They, too, came close to pursuing the learning of Master Yan. Yet when their learning was applied, its outcome was no different [?]. Was their learning unsuited to practical application? Or does success indeed depend upon encountering, or failing to encounter, the right opportunity? In discussing Yi Yin, Mengzi spoke of his care in accepting or giving even the smallest thing. Confucius told Yan Yuan neither to look, listen, speak, nor act contrary to ritual propriety. Thus, advancing in virtue and cultivating one’s undertakings cannot be pursued in vague generalities; the achievements and learning of these gentlemen must likewise have had their essential points. You candidates look up to the worthy philosophers of the past: where will you actually apply your efforts? Please speak plainly, rather than merely dazzling one another with empty words.

Question: Lu Zhi said: “The key to defeating the enemy lies in finding the right man to command; the way to control commanders lies in holding the proper means of control.” In the deliberations over choosing a commander at Beilu and the discussion of generalship by the Master of Lanling, ritual, music, benevolence, and righteousness were held supreme. Yet in later ages there were men who sang refined songs as they faced battle or wore light fur robes and inspired trust. There were also men who razed capitals and buried surrendered soldiers alive, displayed prowess in assessing the enemy, or rose from flute-playing and damaged silk [?] to assist the rise of a dynasty. For a ruler, the matter lies in obtaining capable men [?]; these men certainly could not all conform to what was said in Jin and Chu. There is no need to debate this further. As for the means of controlling commanders, however, I have surveyed the past in search of what is meant by “holding the proper means of control,” and privately find myself perplexed. Let me discuss this with you candidates. Rank serves to accord proper recognition to merit. The man who fled while serving as Commandant for Grain, on account of Han…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中片語而登壇倚爲北道主人者待庥
下數言而佩印何遲速之不等歟罰以
正法也戮僨帥於一敗者欲以謝申息
之老用纍臣於再衄者卒以啓西戎之
霸何操縱之殊科歟大將拜於入塞明
天寵也乃有剋敵斬使相之授者不幾
於有司歟嚚將斬於河陽肅軍令也乃
有臨陣徇司隸之請者不幾於無紀歟
同於被訟也或責其人而諭之改或送
===
其人而令之誅何待之異歟均於屯邊
也或士卒大樂乎簡易或軍吏殊苦其
擾煩何用之同歟若是乎馭之無定術
也果孰爲操得其柄耶夫執古可以御
今今南北多虞時務所急宜莫如馭將
者故願諸生以往事明之也
punctuated: 中片語而登壇，倚爲北道主人者待庥下數言而佩印，何遲速之不等歟？罰以正法也，戮僨帥於一敗者欲以謝申息之老，用纍臣於再衄者卒以啓西戎之霸，何操縱之殊科歟？大將拜於入塞，明天寵也，乃有剋敵斬使相之授者，不幾於有司歟？嚚將斬於河陽，肅軍令也，乃有臨陣徇司隸之請者，不幾於無紀歟？同於被訟也，或責其人而諭之改，或送其人而令之誅，何待之異歟？均於屯邊也，或士卒大樂乎簡易，或軍吏殊苦其擾煩，何用之同歟？若是乎馭之無定術也，果孰爲操得其柄耶？夫執古可以御今，今南北多虞，時務所急宜莫如馭將者，故願諸生以往事明之也。
translation_en:
…a few words at Hanzhong brought him onto the platform to receive his command; the man relied upon as master of the northern route had to await a few words beneath the shade [?] before wearing the seal of office. Why did their appointments differ so in speed?

Punishment serves to uphold the law. One ruler executed a defeated commander after a single defeat, intending thereby to make amends to the elders of Shen and Xi; another employed an imprisoned minister after two defeats and ultimately established hegemony over the western Rong. Why were restraint and latitude applied by such different standards?

Appointing a general-in-chief upon his return within the frontier passes displayed imperial favor. Yet there was also the case of defeating the enemy, beheading an envoy, and conferring a chief ministership [?]. Did this not approach the conduct of a mere functionary? Executing an insubordinate general at Heyang enforced military discipline. Yet there was also someone who, on the eve of battle, acceded to the request of the Metropolitan Commandant. Did this not approach a complete lack of discipline?

Both men faced accusations: in one case the ruler reproached the man and instructed him to reform; in another he sent the man away with orders that he be executed. Why were they treated differently? Both men commanded frontier garrisons: under one, the soldiers greatly enjoyed the simplicity and ease of his administration; under the other, military officers suffered greatly from its burdensome interference. Why were they employed alike?

Was the management of generals so devoid of any settled method? Who, then, truly held the means of controlling them? Understanding antiquity enables one to govern the present. Now that troubles abound in both north and south, surely no urgent task of government surpasses the management of generals. I therefore ask you candidates to illuminate this matter through past events.

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人一百五十名
第一名吳汝倫　無錫縣學生　書
第二名陸檄　蘇州府學生　易
第三名武尚耕　溧水縣人監生　詩
第四名陳有則　蘇州府學增廣生　春秋
第五名魏良靜　江西寧都縣人監生　禮記
第六名吳中英　全椒縣學生　詩
第七名王守素　溧水縣學附學生　易
===
第八名甘一驥　江西南昌縣人監生　詩
第九名葉汝華　太倉州學附學生　書
第十名夏思　廣德州人監生　易
第十一名金從洋　華亭縣學附學生　詩
第十二名方楊　歙縣學生　書

text:

四書
君子謀道不謀食耕也餒在其中矣學也
祿在其中矣君子憂道不憂貧

translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“The gentleman seeks the Way, not food. In plowing, hunger may still be found; in learning, official emoluments may be found. The gentleman worries about the Way, not poverty.”

Lu Ji 陸檝

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “Most writers on this topic cannot connect its parts into a coherent whole. This composition refines its ideas and fashions its language with exceptional precision and close integration, yet expresses everything naturally. Only someone deeply accomplished in self-cultivation could achieve this. It certainly deserves a high recommendation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The conception is subtle and precise; the language and tone are serene and harmonious.”

Comments by Associate Examiner Xu, District Magistrate: “The form is a seamless whole, and the writing vigorous and strong.” “The idea concerning serving one’s ruler and putting remuneration last is especially good [?]. This shows an understanding of how to seek the Way.” “It should be regarded as more than merely a composition in the current fashion; it should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting: “The form is concise and disciplined; the meaning is rich and enduring.”

Comment by Examiner Ma, Librarian: “The language and ideas are rounded and harmonious.”

In discussing the learning through which the gentleman attains the Way, the Sage describes a mind entirely free of ulterior purpose. For the gentleman studies in order to realize his Way. Although he may thereby obtain official emoluments, could his heart be set on these? It is fitting that the Master spoke these words as a warning to those who seek emoluments. It is as though he were saying: in learning, nothing takes precedence over distinguishing righteousness from profit. What makes the gentleman’s learning different from that of others lies precisely in having…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
得乎此而已何則君子以明道自期吾見其孳
孳以求道之能知矣乃若食雖養所必資何嘗
或計焉以行道自任吾見其汲汲以求道之能
體矣乃若食雖人所同欲何嘗或圖焉夫君子
固不謀食矣其究未必不得食也如以食爲謀
者其究又未必得食也農夫之耕非志於求食
者乎然而餒在其中求之有不得矣君子之學
固惟以謀道焉耳然而祿在其中不求可自致
矣是君子雖謀道也而食未嘗不寓者也顧其
===
志道之初心則又不若是其幾也惟以道不能
知吾憂之道知而憂斯釋矣豈其貧之不能安
也而假此以爲謀利之階哉道不能體吾憂之
道體而憂斯釋矣豈其貧之不能樂也而藉此
以爲欲富之地哉故祿之得也若固有之也即
未之得也若將終身也蓋所憂者非貧也觀其
憂不憂而其謀不謀益可知矣君子之學蓋如
此此其所以不可及乎抑道高矣遠矣君子必
有深造之者乃夫子獨言其不謀食何蓋義利
punctuated: 得乎此而已。何則？君子以明道自期，吾見其孳孳以求道之能知矣。乃若食，雖養所必資，何嘗或計焉？以行道自任，吾見其汲汲以求道之能體矣。乃若食，雖人所同欲，何嘗或圖焉？夫君子固不謀食矣，其究未必不得食也。如以食爲謀者，其究又未必得食也。農夫之耕，非志於求食者乎？然而餒在其中，求之有不得矣。君子之學，固惟以謀道焉耳；然而祿在其中，不求可自致矣。是君子雖謀道也，而食未嘗不寓者也。顧其志道之初心，則又不若是其幾也。惟以道不能知，吾憂之；道知而憂斯釋矣。豈其貧之不能安也，而假此以爲謀利之階哉？道不能體，吾憂之；道體而憂斯釋矣。豈其貧之不能樂也，而藉此以爲欲富之地哉？故祿之得也，若固有之也；即未之得也，若將終身也。蓋所憂者非貧也。觀其憂不憂，而其謀不謀益可知矣。君子之學蓋如此，此其所以不可及乎？抑道高矣，遠矣，君子必有深造之者，乃夫子獨言其不謀食，何？蓋義利
translation_en:
…having attained an understanding of this, and nothing more. Why is this so? The gentleman sets himself the goal of illuminating the Way: I see him diligently seeking to understand it. As for food, although it is indispensable for sustaining life, when does he ever calculate how to obtain it? He takes practicing the Way as his responsibility: I see him earnestly seeking to embody it. As for food, although everyone desires it, when does he ever scheme to secure it? The gentleman certainly does not seek food, yet in the end he will not necessarily fail to obtain it. Conversely, those who make food their object will not necessarily obtain it in the end. When a farmer tills the soil, is his purpose not to obtain food? Yet hunger may still be his lot: he may seek food without obtaining it. The gentleman’s learning is devoted solely to seeking the Way; yet an official salary may be his lot, coming of itself without being sought. Thus, although the gentleman seeks the Way, provision for food is nevertheless implicit in that pursuit. But his original intention in setting his heart on the Way involves no such expectation.

It is only my inability to understand the Way that troubles me; once the Way is understood, that anxiety is dispelled. Could it be that he cannot rest content in poverty and uses learning as a stepping-stone to profit? It is my inability to embody the Way that troubles me; once the Way is embodied, that anxiety is dispelled. Could it be that he cannot find joy in poverty and uses learning as a means of pursuing wealth? Thus, when he obtains an official salary, he treats it as something naturally his; even when he has not obtained one, he accepts that this may last his whole life. For poverty is not what troubles him. By observing what troubles him and what does not, we can understand still more clearly what he seeks and what he does not. Such is the gentleman’s learning. Is this why others cannot equal him? Yet the Way is lofty and far-reaching, and the gentleman must pursue it deeply. Why, then, does the Master speak only of his not seeking food? It is because righteousness and profit…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之辨不明則體用之間悉謬窮無眞儒淳無善
治皆此之由也故夫子垂訓不爲高遠之論語
爲學惟曰謀道不謀食他日語事君亦惟曰敬
事後其食其詞近其旨深矣噫事君後其食惟
爲學不謀食者能之
道也者不可須臾離也可離非道也是故
君子戒愼乎其所不睹恐懼乎其所不
聞
===

punctuated:
之辨不明，則體用之間悉謬，窮無眞儒，淳無善治，皆此之由也。故夫子垂訓，不爲高遠之論，語爲學惟曰：「謀道不謀食。」他日語事君，亦惟曰：「敬事後其食。」其詞近，其旨深矣。噫！事君後其食，惟爲學不謀食者能之。

道也者，不可須臾離也；可離，非道也。是故君子戒愼乎其所不睹，恐懼乎其所不聞。

translation_en:
…if the distinction [between righteousness and profit] is not clear, then everything concerning substance and function goes astray. That there are no true Confucians in straitened circumstances and no good government in conditions described as chun [?] all stems from this. Thus, in bequeathing his teachings, the Master did not offer lofty and remote pronouncements. Speaking of learning, he said only: “Seek the Way, not sustenance.” On another occasion, speaking of serving a ruler, he likewise said only: “Attend reverently to your duties and put your remuneration afterward.” His words are accessible, but their meaning is profound. Ah! Only those who pursue learning without seeking sustenance can serve a ruler while putting their remuneration afterward.

“The Way cannot be departed from for even an instant. What can be departed from is not the Way. Therefore, the gentleman is watchful and cautious concerning what he does not see, and apprehensive concerning what he does not hear.”

Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor, comments: “The principle underlying the topic is profound and abstruse. Many who write on it in the examination produce tiresome verbosity [?]. This essay is precise in principle and elegant in language; without deep cultivation one could not…” The ending, including the following ‘admiration’ and annotation ‘admiration, reverence,’ is garbled [?].

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Its grasp of principle is precise, and its language is also elegant and pure.”

Wu Shanggeng.

“It is entirely fitting to select this for inclusion as a model for the many candidates.”

Associate Examiner Xu, School Instructor, comments: “The passage stating that the Way cannot be departed from for even an instant contains exceptionally profound implications that are difficult to express. This essay expounds them clearly and penetratingly, while its language is also mature and elegant. Include it.”

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍讀陶　批〔體認親切〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔冲粹古雅之作〕
中庸甚言道不可離而示人以敬畏之密焉夫
道率諸性本不可須臾離也然則君子之敬畏
豈以不睹不聞而遂忽哉子思示人之意若曰
夫人之或離乎道也其亦未知斯道之甚切乎
夫道曰率性而性命於天則是道也者根本於
天命人心之正而貫徹於日用常行之間語其
統體無物不有自吾心之所具以至吾身之所
===
接須臾離之不得其理矣不可也語其流行無
時不然自思慮之未起以至應感之無窮須臾
離之不得其理矣不可也使或可離於須臾而
無所闕於得失則是外鑠之物耳而豈率性之
謂哉君子知其不可離如此是故欽翼之忱常
存於宥密寅畏之念無間於斯須囿嘗嚴乎其
所睹矣雖時乎不睹而尤深致其戒慎焉蓋誠
慮夫至靜之中一息少懈則一息或離乎道而
惺惺者罔敢懈也不睹尚爾又焉往而不戒慎
punctuated:
考試官侍讀陶，批〔體認親切〕
考試官洗馬馬，批〔冲粹古雅之作〕
《中庸》甚言道不可離，而示人以敬畏之密焉。夫道率諸性，本不可須臾離也。然則君子之敬畏，豈以不睹不聞而遂忽哉？子思示人之意若曰：夫人之或離乎道也，其亦未知斯道之甚切乎？夫道曰率性，而性命於天，則是道也者，根本於天命人心之正，而貫徹於日用常行之間。語其統體，無物不有，自吾心之所具，以至吾身之所接，須臾離之，不得其理矣，不可也。語其流行，無時不然，自思慮之未起，以至應感之無窮，須臾離之，不得其理矣，不可也。使或可離於須臾，而無所闕於得失，則是外鑠之物耳，而豈率性之謂哉？君子知其不可離如此，是故欽翼之忱常存於宥密，寅畏之念無間於斯須。囿嘗嚴乎其所睹矣，雖時乎不睹，而尤深致其戒慎焉。蓋誠慮夫至靜之中，一息少懈，則一息或離乎道，而惺惺者罔敢懈也。不睹尚爾，又焉往而不戒慎
translation_en:
Examiner Tao, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔An intimate and thorough understanding.〕
Examiner Ma, Librarian, comments: 〔A work of serene purity and classical elegance.〕
The Doctrine of the Mean emphatically declares that the Way cannot be departed from, thereby showing people how exacting their reverence and awe must be. The Way follows our nature and fundamentally cannot be departed from even for an instant. How, then, could the gentleman neglect reverence and awe merely because he neither sees nor hears anything? What Zisi means to teach people is as follows: If people sometimes depart from the Way, is it perhaps because they have not understood how immediately it concerns them?
The Way is called following one's nature, and that nature is ordained by Heaven. Thus the Way is rooted in the rectitude of the human heart as ordained by Heaven and pervades everyday activities and ordinary conduct. Speaking of its all-embracing substance, there is nothing in which it is not present: from what is inherent in my heart to everything with which my person comes into contact. To depart from it even for an instant is to fail to grasp its principle; this cannot be done. Speaking of its ongoing operation, there is no time when it is not so: from before thoughts arise to the endless responses to things that affect us. To depart from it even for an instant is to fail to grasp its principle; this cannot be done. If one could depart from it for an instant without any deficiency in what one gains or loses, it would merely be something imposed from outside. How could it then be called following one's nature?
The gentleman understands that the Way cannot be departed from in this manner. Hence his sincere reverence and circumspection remain constantly present in the deepest stillness, and his thoughts of reverent awe never lapse for an instant. He has already been scrupulous about what he sees [?]; even when he sees nothing, he applies himself still more deeply to vigilance and caution. For he truly fears that, amid utter stillness, the slightest slackening for a single breath might mean departing from the Way for that breath. Thus, ever alert, he dares not relax. If he is like this even when he sees nothing, where could he go without vigilance and caution…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
哉固當謹乎其所聞矣雖時乎不聞而尤深致
其恐懼焉蓋誠慮夫無感之際一念少弛則一
念或離乎道而兢兢者罔敢弛也不聞尚爾又
焉往而不恐懼哉吁君子之敬畏若此此其心
之所以常存性之所以常定而不至離道於須
臾也由教入道者其亦是務哉抑論中庸首章
首言斯道之大原終言神化之極致而其用功
之密乃在於戒慎恐懼則戒慎恐懼固性命所
由盡而聖神功化所由始歟時雍風動本於兢
===
業之懷而小心翼翼實所以事上帝而受方國
也有志於位育之化者不可不知
責難於君謂之恭陳善閉邪謂之敬
吴汝倫
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔此題作者上下纏擾殊無分析此篇語意超脫發明曲盡宜錄以式〕
同考試官教諭郭　批〔矩矱蒼嚴詞華奇古大方家之作也敬服敬服〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔筆力高古不類衆作〕
punctuated:
哉？固當謹乎其所聞矣，雖時乎不聞，而尤深致其恐懼焉。蓋誠慮夫無感之際，一念少弛，則一念或離乎道，而兢兢者罔敢弛也。不聞尚爾，又焉往而不恐懼哉？吁！君子之敬畏若此，此其心之所以常存、性之所以常定，而不至離道於須臾也。由教入道者，其亦是務哉！抑論《中庸》首章，首言斯道之大原，終言神化之極致，而其用功之密，乃在於戒慎恐懼。則戒慎恐懼，固性命所由盡，而聖神功化所由始歟？時雍風動，本於兢業之懷，而小心翼翼，實所以事上帝而受方國也。有志於位育之化者，不可不知。

責難於君謂之恭，陳善閉邪謂之敬。
吴汝倫
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔此題作者上下纏擾，殊無分析。此篇語意超脫，發明曲盡，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭郭　批〔矩矱蒼嚴，詞華奇古，大方家之作也。敬服！敬服！〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔筆力高古，不類衆作。〕
translation_en:
…? He must certainly be attentive to what he hears; even when he hears nothing, he applies himself still more deeply to apprehension and fear. For he truly fears that, when nothing stirs him, the slightest relaxation in a single thought might cause that thought to depart from the Way; thus, in his vigilance, he dares not relax. If he is like this even when he hears nothing, where could he ever fail to remain apprehensive and fearful? Ah! Such is the noble man’s reverence and awe. This is how his mind remains ever present and his nature ever settled, so that he does not depart from the Way even for an instant. Those who enter the Way through instruction should surely devote themselves to this as well!

Furthermore, the opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean begins by discussing the great source of this Way and ends by discussing the highest attainment of wondrous transformation. Yet the meticulous application of effort lies in watchfulness, caution, apprehension, and fear. Are these not, indeed, the means by which one fully realizes one’s nature and Heaven’s mandate, and the starting point of the transformative achievements of sages and spirits? Harmony throughout the age and transformation spreading like the wind are rooted in a vigilant and conscientious disposition. Being careful and reverent is precisely how one serves the Lord on High and receives dominion over the regional states. Those who aspire to the transformation through which all things find their proper places and flourish must understand this.

“To demand difficult achievements of one’s ruler is called dutiful respect; to set forth what is good and shut out what is evil is called reverence.”

Wu Rulun 吴汝倫

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: 〔Writers on this topic entangle its two clauses and fail to distinguish them clearly. This essay’s language and meaning rise above such constraints, and its exposition exhausts every subtlety. It should be recorded as a model.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor: 〔Its form is mature and rigorous; its literary expression is striking and antique. This is the work of an accomplished master. I admire it! I admire it!〕

Comment by Examiner Tao, Reader-in-waiting: 〔The force of its writing is lofty and antique, unlike the other compositions.〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官洗馬馬　批〔理貫而詞〕〔所〕
大賢指言事君之恭敬所以立臣極也夫恭敬
者人臣事君之道也而知所謂恭敬者鮮矣宜
孟子指責難陳善以示之極乎意豈不曰君之
於臣所需者甚殷臣之事君所務者貴大是故
爲君以堯舜爲極至事莫難焉而爲之則是顧
人臣無以責之耳誠知古今無不同之道責君
以爲堯爲舜之事俾奮然自勵於有爲即道不
易盡而左右夾輔必欲曠世匹休焉若此者何
===
以謂之恭蓋望君不至者薄待其君者也慢孰
甚焉以難責君雖投之艱也實尊以聖也其期
之大有爲皆其心不敢以不足與爲待之者此
其輔相之志與臯夔稷契之贊襄者同矣不謂
之恭而何哉堯舜以仁政成治平道莫善焉而
非是則邪顧人臣無以格之耳誠知理欲有互
勝之機啓君以仁心仁政之說使默然自開其
不仁即機不相入而委曲開導必欲昭德塞違
焉若此者何以謂之敬蓋從君之欲者陷君於
punctuated:
考試官洗馬馬批〔理貫而詞〕〔所〕

大賢指言事君之恭敬，所以立臣極也。夫恭敬者，人臣事君之道也，而知所謂恭敬者鮮矣。宜孟子指責難陳善以示之極乎！意豈不曰：君之於臣，所需者甚殷；臣之事君，所務者貴大。是故爲君以堯舜爲極至，事莫難焉，而爲之則是，顧人臣無以責之耳。誠知古今無不同之道，責君以爲堯爲舜之事，俾奮然自勵於有爲，即道不易盡，而左右夾輔，必欲曠世匹休焉。若此者，何以謂之恭？蓋望君不至者，薄待其君者也，慢孰甚焉？以難責君，雖投之艱也，實尊以聖也。其期之大有爲，皆其心不敢以不足與爲待之者。此其輔相之志，與臯夔稷契之贊襄者同矣，不謂之恭而何哉？堯舜以仁政成治平，道莫善焉，而非是則邪，顧人臣無以格之耳。誠知理欲有互勝之機，啓君以仁心仁政之說，使默然自開其不仁，即機不相入，而委曲開導，必欲昭德塞違焉。若此者，何以謂之敬？蓋從君之欲者，陷君於
translation_en:
Examiner Ma, Librarian of the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔The reasoning runs coherently through it, while the language…〕〔suo (“that which”) [?]〕

The great worthy expressly explained deference and reverence in serving a ruler, thereby establishing the highest standard for ministers. Deference and reverence are the way a minister serves his ruler, yet few understand what they mean. Was it not fitting that Mengzi should point to demanding difficult achievements and presenting what is good, thereby showing this highest standard? Surely his meaning was this: a ruler’s demands upon his ministers are most substantial, and ministers serving their ruler must prize great undertakings.

Thus, for a ruler, Yao and Shun constitute the highest standard. Nothing is harder than their achievements, yet to emulate them is right; it is simply that ministers fail to demand this of their ruler. If a minister truly understands that the Way is the same in ancient and present times, he will demand that his ruler undertake the deeds of Yao and Shun, encouraging him to rouse himself and strive for accomplishment. Even though the Way is not easily realized in full, he will support and assist the ruler on every side, determined that he should equal their excellence across the intervening ages. Why is conduct such as this called deference? To expect less than the utmost from one’s ruler is to hold him in low esteem. What greater disrespect could there be? To demand difficult achievements of a ruler may place him amid hardships, but it truly honors him as a sage. The minister’s expectation that the ruler will accomplish great things springs entirely from a heart that dares not treat him as someone incapable of undertaking such things together with him. His resolve to assist the ruler is thus the same as that of Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie in their service. If this is not called deference, what should it be called?

Yao and Shun achieved orderly and peaceful government through benevolent rule. No way is better; whatever departs from it is deviant. It is simply that ministers fail to bring their ruler into accord with it. If a minister truly understands the workings through which principle and desire alternately gain ascendancy, he will enlighten the ruler with teachings about a benevolent heart and benevolent government, causing him inwardly to free himself from his lack of benevolence [?]. Even if their dispositions do not accord, he will guide and enlighten him with patient attention to every circumstance, determined to make virtue manifest and block wrongdoing. Why is conduct such as this called reverence? For those who follow their ruler’s desires lead their ruler into…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
過者也歟孰甚焉以善格君雖拂其情也實引
之道也其入而盡所言皆其心不敢以不足與
言視之者此其匡救之意與臯夔稷契之謨弼
者同矣不謂之敬而何哉吁人臣而知此可以
語事君矣雖然尤貴於君之知之也君知此之
爲恭敬也則樂於嘉納而恭敬行矣不然將不
以爲苦難逆耳者乎伊尹遇從諫弗咈之聖始
遂堯舜其君之心教其臣卑之無甚高論焉斯
漢之所以雜霸矣故曰俊士俟明主以顯其德
明主者明此者也
===
易
以祉元吉中以行願也
