於易學者宜錄以式
punctuated:
過者也，歟孰甚焉？以善格君，雖拂其情也，實引之道也。其入而盡所言，皆其心不敢以不足與言視之者。此其匡救之意，與臯夔稷契之謨弼者同矣，不謂之敬而何哉？吁！人臣而知此，可以語事君矣。雖然，尤貴於君之知之也。君知此之爲恭敬也，則樂於嘉納而恭敬行矣。不然，將不以爲苦難逆耳者乎？伊尹遇從諫弗咈之聖，始遂堯舜其君之心。教其臣卑之，無甚高論焉，斯漢之所以雜霸矣。故曰：「俊士俟明主以顯其德。」明主者，明此者也。

易
以祉元吉，中以行願也。
陸檝
同考試官教諭蔡 批〔老成莊重，詞復自然。〕深得純心任賢意，可以式矣。
同考試官教諭張 批〔發明人主下賢保泰〕之旨，多用本色語，而精切懇到，迥異衆作，蓋深於易學者，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…into wrongdoing. What could be worse [?]? To correct one’s ruler through goodness may run counter to his feelings, but it truly guides him toward the Way. In coming before him and saying all that must be said, such ministers act from hearts that dare not regard him as unworthy of being addressed. Their intent to correct and rescue him is the same as that behind the counsels and assistance of Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie. How could this not be called reverence? Ah! With ministers who understand this, one can discuss serving a ruler. Yet it is especially important that the ruler himself understand it. If he recognizes this as respect and reverence, he will gladly accept it, and respect and reverence will find expression in practice. Otherwise, will he not consider it distressing, difficult, and offensive to hear? Only upon encountering a sage who followed remonstrance without resisting it could Yi Yin fulfill his wish to make his ruler a Yao or a Shun. To instruct one’s ministers to lower their sights and avoid excessively lofty discourse—this is why Han government mingled the methods of the hegemon with those of the true king. Thus it is said: “Outstanding men await an enlightened ruler in order to manifest their virtue.” An enlightened ruler is one who understands this.

Book of Changes
“Through this comes blessing: supremely auspicious. Through centrality he fulfills his aspiration.”
Lu Ji 陸檝
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔Mature and dignified, with language that is also natural.〕 It profoundly captures the idea of appointing worthy men with a sincere heart and can serve as a model.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔It elucidates the ruler’s humbling himself before worthy men to preserve peace〕 as its central meaning. It mostly uses plain, unaffected language, yet is precise, incisive, earnest, and thorough, far surpassing the other compositions. Its author evidently has a deep understanding of the study of the Changes. It should be included as a model.

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官知縣徐　批〔識精句雅無假雕鏤〕
而理自明暢積學之士也
考試官侍讀陶　批〔明粹可式〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔詞簡而意足錄之〕
象傳於保泰之主而表其下賢之心焉蓋賢者
邦國之楨也人君純心以下賢茲固泰之所由
保與夫子小象之意若謂王者之御世也集維
新之命者易爲力而保盈成之運者難爲功顧
茲卦而曰泰治之盛也爻而至五時之極也物
===
盛則衰時過必返吾方慮其悔咎之不終無矣
乃周公繫其辭曰以祉元吉則又若不虞其往
復之常期而直許以于食之有福者五果何修
而得此哉亦惟中以行願焉耳蓋得賢臣以弘
功業人主孰無此願也第德有未中則淵微所
存既無以端其取人之本而頗僻是累又無以
致其信任之專願之不獲自遂者多矣茲惟六
五柔中虛已下應九二則是帝德罔愆而任賢
爲之弗貳凡名言允出一皆念其邁種之懿也
punctuated:
同考試官知縣徐，批〔識精句雅，無假雕鏤〕而理自明暢，積學之士也。

考試官侍讀陶，批〔明粹可式〕。

考試官洗馬馬，批〔詞簡而意足，錄之〕。

《象傳》於保泰之主，而表其下賢之心焉。蓋賢者，邦國之楨也。人君純心以下賢，茲固泰之所由保與！夫子《小象》之意，若謂王者之御世也，集維新之命者易爲力，而保盈成之運者難爲功。顧茲卦而曰泰，治之盛也；爻而至五，時之極也。物盛則衰，時過必返，吾方慮其悔咎之不終無矣。乃周公繫其辭曰：「以祉元吉。」則又若不虞其往復之常期，而直許以于食之有福者。五果何修而得此哉？亦惟中以行願焉耳。蓋得賢臣以弘功業，人主孰無此願也？第德有未中，則淵微所存，既無以端其取人之本，而頗僻是累，又無以致其信任之專，願之不獲自遂者多矣。茲惟六五柔中，虛已下應九二，則是帝德罔愆，而任賢爲之弗貳。凡名言允出，一皆念其邁種之懿也。
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xu, District Magistrate, comments: 〔“Discerning in understanding and elegant in phrasing, with no need for elaborate ornamentation”〕—yet the principles emerge clearly and fluently of themselves. He is a man of accumulated learning.

Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔“Clear and refined; worthy to serve as a model.”〕

Examiner Ma, Librarian to the Heir Apparent, comments: 〔“Concise in wording yet complete in meaning. Include it.”〕

The Commentary on the Images brings to light the heart of a ruler who preserves Peace (Tai): his humility toward the worthy. For worthy men are the pillars of the state. Surely it is through the ruler’s purity of heart and humility toward the worthy that Peace is preserved! The Master’s meaning in the Lesser Image Commentary seems to be this: when a king governs the world, bringing together the forces of a renewed mandate is relatively easy, but preserving an era of full achievement is difficult. Consider this hexagram, named Peace: it represents government at its height. When its lines reach the fifth, the time has reached its culmination. Things in their fullness decline; times, once past their peak, must turn back. I was just beginning to fear that regret and blame could not remain absent forever. Yet the Duke of Zhou attached these words to the line: “Thereby obtaining blessings: supreme good fortune.” It is as though he were unconcerned about the regular cycle of advance and return, and directly promised blessings in the enjoyment of sustenance [?]. What, then, has the fifth line cultivated to attain this? Only this: “Through centrality, he carries out his wish.”

For what ruler does not wish to obtain worthy ministers to enlarge his achievements? Yet if his virtue falls short of centrality, then, in the profound and subtle recesses of his heart, he lacks the means to set right the foundation of his selection of men. Burdened by partiality and deviation, he also lacks the means to make his trust in them undivided. Thus wishes often fail to find fulfillment. Here, however, the six in the fifth place is yielding and central; emptying himself, he responds below to the nine in the second place. Thus imperial virtue is free from error, and his employment of the worthy admits no wavering. In all nominations and pronouncements sincerely put forth [?], his thoughts dwell wholly upon the excellence of their vigorous cultivation of virtue. …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇極克協而俊民由之用章凡貨色讒邪不能
搖其貴德之誠也由是包荒馮河之嘉猷旣敷
施于有政而輔相裁成之耿烈將永保於無疆
矣辭之所謂以祉元吉不以是耶是可見保泰
非難而得賢爲難得賢非難而能純其心以任
賢之爲難也人主欲守至治而綏景福其尚求
之心乎嗚呼人君一心萬化之原也其大端惟
在於用人所謂中者惟心無偏倚云爾人主心
無偏倚則知人哲舉措當萬化得其理而祉與
===
元吉固其所自至者一有偏倚則用非所用心
愈專治愈遠去祉吉千里矣然則治心之道柰
何亦曰惟精惟一而已
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉
王守素
同考試官教諭蔡　批　〔意義精密文辭典雅〕
善闡天道之與足占素養矣
同考試官教諭張　批　〔通篇整潔純粹而講〕
乾道專直之理更是精緻宜錄以式
punctuated:
皇極克協，而俊民由之用章，凡貨色讒邪不能搖其貴德之誠也。由是包荒馮河之嘉猷旣敷施于有政，而輔相裁成之耿烈將永保於無疆矣。辭之所謂以祉元吉，不以是耶？是可見保泰非難，而得賢爲難；得賢非難，而能純其心以任賢之爲難也。人主欲守至治而綏景福，其尚求之心乎！嗚呼！人君一心，萬化之原也。其大端惟在於用人。所謂中者，惟心無偏倚云爾。人主心無偏倚，則知人哲，舉措當，萬化得其理，而祉與元吉固其所自至者。一有偏倚，則用非所用，心愈專，治愈遠，去祉吉千里矣。然則治心之道柰何？亦曰惟精惟一而已。
夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。
王守素
同考試官教諭蔡批：〔意義精密，文辭典雅〕善闡天道之與，足占素養矣。
同考試官教諭張批：〔通篇整潔純粹，而講〕乾道專直之理，更是精緻，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…The august mean is duly realized, and talented men thereby gain distinction through employment; neither wealth and sensual pleasures nor slander and wickedness can shake his sincerity in honoring virtue. Thus the excellent counsels of embracing the uncultivated and crossing rivers on foot are put into practice in government, while the illustrious achievements of assisting and regulating the transformations of Heaven and Earth will endure without limit. Is this not why the statement speaks of “blessings and supreme good fortune”? From this we can see that preserving Peace is not difficult; obtaining worthy men is difficult. Obtaining worthy men is not difficult; being able to purify one’s heart so as to entrust them with responsibility is difficult. If a ruler wishes to preserve perfect order and enjoy great blessings, should he not seek the means within his own heart? Ah! The ruler’s single heart is the source of all transformations. Its foremost concern lies in employing men. What is called centrality means simply that the heart has no bias or inclination. When the ruler’s heart is without bias, he is discerning in judging men, his appointments and measures are appropriate, and all transformations follow their proper principles; blessings and supreme good fortune then come of themselves. Once there is bias, however, he employs those who should not be employed. The more fixed his purpose, the more distant good government becomes, and blessings and good fortune are a thousand li away. How, then, should one govern the heart? The answer is merely: be discerning and single-minded.
“As for Qian, in stillness it is concentrated, and in movement it is direct; thus it brings forth on a grand scale.”
Wang Shousu
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: 〔The meaning is precise and closely reasoned; the diction is refined and elegant.〕 Its skill in expounding the Way of Heaven [?] is sufficient evidence of sustained cultivation.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔The entire piece is orderly, polished, and pure; its exposition of〕 the principle of concentration and directness in the Way of Qian is especially meticulous. It should be recorded as a model.

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官知縣徐　批〔揣思精微造語雅健〕
〔沛然之中有成法蓋邃於易道者矣〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔說理明順〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔是善言乾之大者〕
大傳即乾道之至健而推其所以大焉蓋專一
直遂天下之至健也乾道之動靜以之而其所
以大也謂不在是乎大傳之意若曰易書之蘊
固極於廣大而廣大之理實本於乾坤今夫乾
其數則一得乎陽之純也其體則實全乎德之
===
易也方其靜與坤別而造化之用以藏斯時也
氣之歛者醇而固理之凝者粹而精蓋至善之
體渾然涵於寂而未有所分也何其專歟及其
動與坤交而造化之仁以顯斯時也歛者以之
而發育凝者以之而流行蓋至健之用沛然妙
於感而莫之能禦也何其直歟夫其靜也正以
豫乎其所動其直也又以出乎其所專乾道之
健如此而大不生於是乎吾見畜之專一則起
知也易而有以宰充周不窮之化發之直遂則
punctuated:
同考試官知縣徐批〔揣思精微，造語雅健〕〔沛然之中有成法，蓋邃於易道者矣〕。
考試官侍讀陶批〔說理明順〕。
考試官洗馬馬批〔是善言乾之大者〕。
大傳即乾道之至健而推其所以大焉。蓋專一直遂，天下之至健也。乾道之動靜以之，而其所以大也，謂不在是乎？大傳之意若曰：易書之蘊，固極於廣大，而廣大之理，實本於乾坤。今夫乾，其數則一，得乎陽之純也；其體則實，全乎德之易也。方其靜，與坤別，而造化之用以藏。斯時也，氣之歛者醇而固，理之凝者粹而精。蓋至善之體，渾然涵於寂，而未有所分也。何其專歟！及其動，與坤交，而造化之仁以顯。斯時也，歛者以之而發育，凝者以之而流行。蓋至健之用，沛然妙於感，而莫之能禦也。何其直歟！夫其靜也，正以豫乎其所動；其直也，又以出乎其所專。乾道之健如此，而大不生於是乎？吾見畜之專一，則起知也易，而有以宰充周不窮之化；發之直遂，則
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xu, District Magistrate, comments: 〔His reflections are subtle and penetrating, his phrasing elegant and vigorous.〕〔Within its abundant flow there is established method: surely he has penetrated deeply into the Way of the Changes.〕
Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔The exposition of principle is clear and coherent.〕
Examiner Ma, Librarian, comments: 〔This is an able account of the greatness of Qian.〕
The Great Commentary proceeds from the utmost vigor of the Way of Qian to infer what makes it great. Single-minded concentration and direct, unimpeded advance constitute the utmost vigor in all under Heaven. The movement and stillness of the Way of Qian depend on these: can one say that its greatness does not lie here? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as if to say: the profundities of the Book of Changes do indeed reach the utmost breadth and greatness, yet the principle of that breadth and greatness is rooted in Qian and Kun. Now Qian has one as its number, possessing the purity of yang; its substance is solid, embodying fully the ease of its virtue. When it is still, it remains distinct from Kun, and the workings of creation are stored within it. At this time, its gathered vital energy is pure and firm, and its concentrated principle is refined and subtle. The substance of utmost goodness is thus held as an undivided whole within stillness, with no differentiation yet arising. How concentrated it is! When it moves, it joins with Kun, and the benevolence of creation becomes manifest. At this time, what was gathered issues forth in generation and nurture, and what was concentrated flows and circulates. The operation of utmost vigor thus responds with abundant and wondrous efficacy, and nothing can resist it. How direct it is! Its stillness precisely prepares for its movement; its directness, in turn, emerges from its concentration. Such is the vigor of the Way of Qian: does not greatness arise from this? I see that when what it stores is concentrated and single, its initiating and directing are effortless [?], enabling it to govern the transformations that fill all things without end; when what it releases advances directly and unimpeded, then …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
擬及也弘而有以成生物不測之功萬物由之
以知始人知乾之大無所不覆矣而不知其所
以覆乎物者惟此徒爲之也無方之神豈物之
所得而踰哉坤道承之以時行人知乾之大無
所不統矣而不知其所以統乎坤者惟此徒爲
之也無涯之氣豈形之所得而限哉吁觀乾之
大而坤之廣從可知矣易固模寫乎乾坤者也
其爲廣大當何如哉抑嘗論之乾天也其道君
道也天之道發見於動而其機則始於靜夫君
道亦猶是耳是故聖人立仁義中正之極必曰
主靜而中和位育之效必自不睹不聞始此又
憲天者之所當知也
===
書
克明俊德以親九族九族既睦平章百姓
百姓昭明協和萬邦黎民於變時雍
吳汝倫
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔常德感應人所易言而功之所至未易形容此作發明精透且援應〕
punctuated:
擬及也弘，而有以成生物不測之功。萬物由之以知始，人知乾之大無所不覆矣，而不知其所以覆乎物者，惟此徒爲之也。無方之神，豈物之所得而踰哉？坤道承之以時行，人知乾之大無所不統矣，而不知其所以統乎坤者，惟此徒爲之也。無涯之氣，豈形之所得而限哉？吁！觀乾之大，而坤之廣從可知矣。易固模寫乎乾坤者也，其爲廣大當何如哉？抑嘗論之：乾，天也；其道，君道也。天之道發見於動，而其機則始於靜。夫君道亦猶是耳。是故聖人立仁義中正之極，必曰主靜；而中和位育之效，必自不睹不聞始。此又憲天者之所當知也。
書
克明俊德，以親九族；九族既睦，平章百姓；百姓昭明，協和萬邦；黎民於變時雍。
吳汝倫
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔常德感應，人所易言，而功之所至，未易形容。此作發明精透，且援應〕
translation_en:
…its reach is broad [?], enabling it to accomplish the unfathomable work of bringing living things into being. Through it, the myriad things receive their beginnings. People know that the greatness of Qian, the Creative, leaves nothing uncovered, yet do not know that what enables it to cover all things is solely this working [?]. How could anything surpass its spiritual efficacy, which is confined to no direction? The way of Kun, the Receptive, receives it and proceeds in accordance with the seasons. People know that the greatness of Qian leaves nothing outside its governance, yet do not know that what enables it to govern Kun is solely this working [?]. How could physical form limit its boundless vital energy? Ah! By observing the greatness of Qian, one can also understand the breadth of Kun. The Book of Changes indeed depicts Qian and Kun: how vast and great, then, must it be!
I have also considered this: Qian is Heaven, and its way is the way of the ruler. Heaven’s way manifests itself in movement, but its incipient impulse begins in stillness. The way of the ruler is likewise. Thus, when the sage establishes the supreme standard of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness, he necessarily speaks of taking stillness as the governing principle. And the effects of equilibrium and harmony—Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and the myriad things being nourished—must begin with what is neither seen nor heard. This, too, is something those who take Heaven as their model should understand.
Book of Documents
“He was able to make manifest his eminent virtue, and thereby bring affection to the nine degrees of kinship. Once the nine degrees of kinship were in accord, he distinguished and ordered the hundred clans. Once the hundred clans had become enlightened, he harmonized the myriad states. The common people were thus transformed and brought into concord.”
Wu Rulun
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: 〔“The stimulus and response of constant virtue [?] are easy for people to speak of, but the full extent of its achievement is not easy to describe. This composition elucidates the matter with precision and penetration; moreover, its supporting references and correspondences …”〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
有體必潛心經學而有得者
同考試官教諭郭　批　此題要見動之放處
感與序意俱非所重此作獨得肯綮而詞復精
明瑩徹足以爲多士式矣
考試官侍讀陶　批　莊重雅潔
考試官洗馬馬　批　庶幾得放動氣象者
史臣詳聖人盛德所及之廣以見放勳之實也
蓋化本於德者也堯之德極其盛矣而化之所
及有不廣者乎史臣贊堯之意若曰大哉堯之
===
爲君也吾固謂其放勳矣而何以見之彼堯也
欽明文思之安安也恭讓之允克也則心法之
虛明者湛然太極之內融身法之著明者昭然
皇極之外煥其俊也固家國天下以爲體而其
明也先家國天下以作則矣俊德之克明如此
而推之有不準者乎故言乎其家有九族也以
是德而親之欲合異分而同情也則見九族反
乎其薄歸乎其厚而藹然自效於親之篤也舉
一家而在帝德聯屬之內矣有不既睦者乎言
punctuated:
有體，必潛心經學而有得者。
同考試官教諭郭批：此題要見動之放處，感與序意俱非所重。此作獨得肯綮，而詞復精明瑩徹，足以爲多士式矣。
考試官侍讀陶批：莊重雅潔。
考試官洗馬馬批：庶幾得放動氣象者。
史臣詳聖人盛德所及之廣，以見放勳之實也。蓋化本於德者也，堯之德極其盛矣，而化之所及有不廣者乎？史臣贊堯之意若曰：大哉，堯之爲君也！吾固謂其放勳矣，而何以見之？彼堯也，欽明文思之安安也，恭讓之允克也，則心法之虛明者，湛然太極之內融；身法之著明者，昭然皇極之外煥。其俊也，固家國天下以爲體；而其明也，先家國天下以作則矣。俊德之克明如此，而推之有不準者乎？故言乎其家，有九族也，以是德而親之，欲合異分而同情也。則見九族反乎其薄，歸乎其厚，而藹然自效於親之篤也。舉一家而在帝德聯屬之內矣，有不既睦者乎？言
translation_en:
…has proper form; its author must be someone who has devoted himself to studying the Classics and gained insight from them.
Associate Examiner Guo, an Instructor, comments: This topic requires bringing out the far-reaching scope of the achievements [?]. Neither influence nor sequence is the principal emphasis. This composition alone grasps the essential point, and its language is also refined, lucid, and perfectly clear. It is worthy to serve as a model for the many candidates.
Examiner Tao, a Reader-in-Waiting, comments: Dignified, elegant, and polished.
Examiner Ma, an Editorial Director, comments: It comes close to capturing the grandeur of far-reaching achievement [?].
The court historian details the broad reach of the sage’s abundant virtue to reveal the substance of his “far-reaching achievement.” Transforming influence is rooted in virtue. Yao’s virtue attained the utmost fullness: could its transforming influence fail to extend widely? The historian’s praise of Yao means something like this: Great indeed was Yao as ruler! I have certainly called his achievement far-reaching, but how can this be demonstrated? Yao was naturally reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful, and truly capable of deference and yielding. Thus, in the empty clarity of his discipline of the mind, the Supreme Ultimate was profoundly integrated within; in the manifest brilliance of his discipline of personal conduct, the Sovereign Ultimate shone resplendently without. His excellence embraced family, state, and all under Heaven as its substance, while his illumination preceded family, state, and all under Heaven in establishing their standard. With his eminent virtue made bright in this way, could its extension fail to furnish a norm?
Thus, speaking of his family, there were the nine degrees of kinship. He drew them close through this virtue, wishing to unite those of differing positions in shared affection. We then see these nine degrees of kinship turn away from coldness and return to generosity of feeling, warmly committing themselves to deep familial affection. His entire family lay within the bonds forged by the emperor’s virtue. Could any fail to be fully harmonious? Speaking of …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乎其國有百姓也以是德而平章之欲均異人
而同德也則見百姓去乎其舊即乎其新而熈
然自敏於光之近也舉一國而在帝德照臨之
下矣有不昭明者乎至於天下有萬邦也以是
德而協和之欲通異地而同風也則見黎民於
變易乎其惡也相忘於不識不知之天遷乎其
善也咸和於大順大化之世舉天下而在帝德
陶鎔之中矣有不時雍者乎夫家國天下盡乎
地與人也而皆堯德之所及四表被上下格矣
===
所謂放勳蓋如此抑堯之及人者曰睦曰明曰
雍雖若不同其實皆明其德耳是之謂明明德
於天下而皆俊德分內事也必如是而後謂俊
德之克明也猶天之覆育萬物而始盡乎其天
也故曰惟天爲大惟堯則之而其要則又在欽
之一言法堯圖治者其亦知所以崇敬哉
所寶惟賢則邇人安
葉汝華
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔講寶賢安民處精切〕
punctuated:
乎其國，有百姓也。以是德而平章之，欲均異人而同德也，則見百姓去乎其舊，即乎其新，而熈然自敏於光之近也。舉一國而在帝德照臨之下矣，有不昭明者乎？至於天下，有萬邦也。以是德而協和之，欲通異地而同風也，則見黎民於變：易乎其惡也，相忘於不識不知之天；遷乎其善也，咸和於大順大化之世。舉天下而在帝德陶鎔之中矣，有不時雍者乎？夫家國天下，盡乎地與人也，而皆堯德之所及，四表被，上下格矣。所謂放勳，蓋如此。抑堯之及人者，曰睦，曰明，曰雍，雖若不同，其實皆明其德耳。是之謂明明德於天下，而皆俊德分內事也。必如是而後謂俊德之克明也，猶天之覆育萬物而始盡乎其天也。故曰：「惟天爲大，惟堯則之。」而其要則又在欽之一言。法堯圖治者，其亦知所以崇敬哉！
所寶惟賢則邇人安
葉汝華
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔講寶賢安民處精切〕
translation_en:
…As for his state, there were the hundred clans. By this virtue he distinguished and regulated them, seeking to bring different people into accord and unite them in virtue. Thus the hundred clans could be seen leaving behind their old ways and embracing the new, joyfully applying themselves to drawing near his light. The entire state lay beneath the illuminating presence of the emperor’s virtue: could any fail to become radiant and enlightened? As for all under Heaven, there were the myriad states. By this virtue he brought them into concord, seeking to connect different lands and unite their customs. Thus the common people were transformed: abandoning their evil ways, they forgot themselves and one another beneath a Heaven whose workings they neither recognized nor knew; advancing toward goodness, they all lived in harmony in an age of great accord and transformation. All under Heaven lay within the shaping and refining influence of the emperor’s virtue: could any fail to attain harmony?
The family, the state, and all under Heaven encompass all lands and people, and all were reached by Yao’s virtue. It extended to the four outer bounds and reached above and below. Such, indeed, was what is meant by “vast achievement.” Moreover, the effects of Yao’s influence upon others are called familial concord, enlightenment, and harmony. Though these may seem different, in truth they all amount to making their virtue bright. This is what is meant by “making bright virtue shine throughout all under Heaven,” and all these things fall within the proper scope of eminent virtue. Only after accomplishing this can one be said to have succeeded in making eminent virtue bright, just as Heaven fulfills its nature as Heaven only by sheltering and nurturing the myriad things. Hence it is said: “Heaven alone is great; Yao alone took it as his model.” Yet the essential point lies in the single word “reverence.” Those who model themselves on Yao in seeking good government should surely understand how to exalt reverence!
“If what he treasures is the worthy, then those nearby will be at peace.”
Ye Ruhua
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: 〔The discussion of treasuring the worthy and bringing peace to the people is precise and incisive.〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
有味錄之不徒以其文也
同考試官教諭郭　批〔好尚得其正故能安民此作發明親切而詞復簡雅一洗浮冗之敝矣宜錄以式〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔得旨〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔明雅〕
大臣勉聖君欲其重賢以成內治也夫君之所
與共治者賢也惟是之重而遠人之安於治也
宜哉召公欲武王無受獒而以此戒勉之若曰
===
人君之好尚天下之安危繫焉不可不慎也不
寶遠物固遠人所由格矣近而求之果何所寶
哉彼國之有賢可以尊主可以庇民寶莫尚焉
者也誠能忘勢而專於樂道不萌夫狎侮之私
賤貨而一於貴德不奪於耳目之玩內之所篤
好曰惟賢也行其諫焉聽其言焉真見其可以
輔吾德而信之罔或貳也外之所崇尚曰惟賢
也隆其禮焉厚其養焉真見其可以裨吾治而
任之罔或忽也如是則好尚克端既有以澄萬
punctuated:
有味，錄之，不徒以其文也。

同考試官教諭郭，批〔好尚得其正，故能安民。此作發明親切，而詞復簡雅，一洗浮冗之敝矣。宜錄以式。〕

考試官侍讀陶，批〔得旨。〕

考試官洗馬馬，批〔明雅。〕

大臣勉聖君，欲其重賢以成內治也。夫君之所與共治者，賢也。惟是之重，而遠人之安於治也，宜哉！召公欲武王無受獒，而以此戒勉之，若曰：

「人君之好尚，天下之安危繫焉，不可不慎也。不寶遠物，固遠人所由格矣。近而求之，果何所寶哉？彼國之有賢，可以尊主，可以庇民，寶莫尚焉者也。誠能忘勢而專於樂道，不萌夫狎侮之私；賤貨而一於貴德，不奪於耳目之玩。內之所篤好，曰惟賢也。行其諫焉，聽其言焉，真見其可以輔吾德，而信之罔或貳也。外之所崇尚，曰惟賢也。隆其禮焉，厚其養焉，真見其可以裨吾治，而任之罔或忽也。如是則好尚克端，既有以澄萬
translation_en:
…has substance; it is selected for more than its literary merit alone.

Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor, comments: 〔When a ruler’s preferences are properly directed, he can bring peace to the people. This essay explains the point aptly and directly, and its language is concise and elegant, thoroughly sweeping away the faults of superficiality and verbosity. It should be selected as a model.〕

Examiner Tao, Reader-in-waiting, comments: 〔Captures the purport.〕

Examiner Ma, Librarian, comments: 〔Clear and elegant.〕

The great minister exhorted the sage ruler, wishing him to value worthy men and thereby establish good government within his realm. Those with whom a ruler shares the work of governing are the worthy. If he values them above all, it is surely fitting that people far away should find peace under his rule! The Duke of Shao wished King Wu not to accept the mastiffs and therefore admonished and encouraged him with these words, as though saying:

“The peace or peril of all under Heaven depends upon the ruler’s preferences: he cannot be incautious about them. Not treasuring objects from distant lands is indeed the means by which people far away are induced to come. But if we look nearer home, what should truly be treasured? The worthy men within the realm can bring honor to their sovereign and protect the people; no treasure surpasses them. If you can truly put aside your exalted position and devote yourself to delighting in the Way, no selfish impulse to treat them with disrespect will arise. If you hold material goods cheap and single-mindedly prize virtue, you will not be diverted by things that delight the eyes and ears. Let those whom you cherish deeply within your heart be the worthy alone. Act upon their remonstrances and heed their words; truly recognize that they can strengthen your virtue, and trust them without wavering. Let those whom you outwardly honor likewise be the worthy alone. Accord them ample ceremonial respect and generous support; truly recognize that they can assist your government, and entrust them with responsibilities without ever neglecting them. In this way your preferences will be properly directed, and you will thereby have the means to purify all…

化之本而能邇之政已立賢才畢輔又有以致
庶績之熙而篤近之效自臻以謨謀於廟堂則
於道無違也臣不咈於將順而凡安其位以自
靖者將和樂於清明之朝矣以敷布于邦國則
於事無擾也民不困於征求而凡安其業以自
力者將順適於寧謐之世矣邇人其有不安者
哉吁一致寶賢之誠遂獲安人之效天下之寶
信無尚於此矣抑論易曰聖人之大寶曰位而
召公乃曰所寶惟賢蓋寶賢固所以寶位也夫
===
武王之世亂臣十人曷常不寶天下大悅奚止
於安即受獒于貢似無損也而召公拳拳戒之
何哉慮夫漸之或長而防之預也武王惟能用
之賢才益附而民益安矣噫此萬世君臣之龜
鑑也
詩
蠶月條桑取彼斧斨以伐遠揚猗彼女桑
七月鳴鵙八月載績載玄載黃我朱孔
陽爲公子裳四月秀葽五月鳴蜩八月
punctuated:
化之本，而能邇之政已立；賢才畢輔，又有以致庶績之熙，而篤近之效自臻。以謨謀於廟堂，則於道無違也；臣不咈於將順，而凡安其位以自靖者，將和樂於清明之朝矣。以敷布于邦國，則於事無擾也；民不困於征求，而凡安其業以自力者，將順適於寧謐之世矣。邇人其有不安者哉？吁！一致寶賢之誠，遂獲安人之效，天下之寶信無尚於此矣。抑論，《易》曰：「聖人之大寶曰位。」而召公乃曰：「所寶惟賢。」蓋寶賢固所以寶位也。夫武王之世，亂臣十人，曷常不寶？天下大悅，奚止於安？即受獒于貢，似無損也，而召公拳拳戒之，何哉？慮夫漸之或長，而防之預也。武王惟能用之，賢才益附，而民益安矣。噫！此萬世君臣之龜鑑也。

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
若曰天下之治觀風俗風俗之美在淳厚不於
我豳民見之乎彼以衣取諸蠶績其事貴預今
歲雖幸成矣而來歲又所當慮也故思於來歲
治蠶之月桑可供蠶則采而兼取乎大小七月
八月鵙鳴麻熟則績而就緒於杼軸於是或爲
之玄或爲之黃而朱則尤極其鮮明焉若此者
亦甚勞矣乃身任其勞也而不以自愛皆獻之
以爲公子裳焉雖裳在公子非無之也而持美
欲效固其忠愛之不容自已者耳蓋必如是而
===
後有衣卒歲之心其慰矣乎又以褐取諸狩獵
其事亦貴預蠶績雖有備矣而禦寒猶恐未周
也故思夫四月葽斯秀五月蜩斯鳴而一陰起
純陽之後八月早禾穫十月草木落而純陰近
大寒之期於是當一陽之月爲于貉之行而狐
狸皆其所利執焉若此者亦甚力矣然力出於
身也而不必爲已皆獻之以爲公子裘焉雖裘
在公子容有之也而獲嘉思奉囧其忠愛之所
欲自盡者耳蓋必如是而後有褐卒歲之意其
punctuated: 若曰：天下之治，觀風俗；風俗之美，在淳厚。不於我豳民見之乎？彼以衣取諸蠶績，其事貴預。今歲雖幸成矣，而來歲又所當慮也。故思於來歲治蠶之月，桑可供蠶，則采而兼取乎大小；七月八月，鵙鳴麻熟，則績而就緒於杼軸。於是或爲之玄，或爲之黃，而朱則尤極其鮮明焉。若此者，亦甚勞矣。乃身任其勞也，而不以自愛，皆獻之以爲公子裳焉。雖裳在公子非無之也，而持美欲效，固其忠愛之不容自已者耳。蓋必如是而後，有衣卒歲之心，其慰矣乎？又以褐取諸狩獵，其事亦貴預。蠶績雖有備矣，而禦寒猶恐未周也。故思夫四月葽斯秀，五月蜩斯鳴，而一陰起純陽之後；八月早禾穫，十月草木落，而純陰近大寒之期。於是當一陽之月，爲于貉之行，而狐狸皆其所利執焉。若此者，亦甚力矣。然力出於身也，而不必爲已，皆獻之以爲公子裘焉。雖裘在公子容有之也，而獲嘉思奉，囧其忠愛之所欲自盡者耳。蓋必如是而後，有褐卒歲之意，其
translation_en:
…as though saying: To judge how well the realm is governed, observe its customs; the excellence of customs lies in their simplicity and sincerity. Can this not be seen among our people of Bin? They obtain clothing through raising silkworms and spinning, work for which advance preparation is essential. Though this year's work has fortunately been accomplished, the coming year must also be considered. Thus they think ahead to the months of tending silkworms next year: when mulberry leaves can feed the silkworms, they gather them from both large and small trees. In the seventh and eighth months, when shrikes call and hemp ripens, they spin and set the work in order upon the loom. They dye some cloth dark and some yellow, while the vermilion is especially brilliant. Such work is indeed arduous. Yet they undertake the toil themselves without sparing themselves, and offer it all to make lower garments for their lord's sons. Although the lord's sons do not lack such garments, the people's wish to present these fine things is simply an irrepressible expression of their loyalty and affection. Surely only after doing this can their concern that there be clothing to last the year find comfort!

They also obtain coarse garments through hunting, work that likewise requires advance preparation. Though silk production and spinning have been provided for, they still fear that protection against the cold may be incomplete. Thus they consider how, in the fourth month, the yao plant flowers, and in the fifth month cicadas call, with the first yin arising after the period of pure yang; how early grain is harvested in the eighth month, and vegetation sheds its leaves in the tenth, when pure yin approaches the season of great cold. Then, in the month when the first yang appears, they undertake the hunt for badgers, seeking also to capture foxes and wildcats. Such work indeed demands great exertion. Yet although the effort comes from their own bodies, it need not be for their own benefit: they offer everything to make fur robes for their lord's sons. Although the lord's sons may already possess fur robes, the people's thought of offering up the fine things they have caught is [?] simply their desire to give the fullest expression to their loyalty and affection. Surely only after doing this can their concern that there be coarse garments to last the year find…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
寧矣乎吁循不忘於嚬戚而義必急乎公家幽
俗之厚有如此夫抑於是而知周公告成王之
微意也觀民俗之厚則先公之德化可知亦可
以見民性之未嘗不善也苟有仇予則非獨民
之過而君亦與有責焉矣知先公之化又知民
之性成王之卒爲有周令主也有以哉
龍旂十乘大糦是承邦畿千里維民所止
肇域彼四海四海來假來假祁祁景員
維河
吳中奭
同考試官教諭崔　批　題意前後重疊而是
作聯絡有法詞復俊雅宜錄以式
同考試官教諭劉　批　修詞古雅析義精瑩
是爲善說詩者允宜高薦
同考試官學正徐　批　鋪叙有體而意味優
揚深得詩人之旨
同考試官知縣李　批　理趣精鑿詞華粹雅
而高古之調殆不可以時義目之者宜用爲式
punctuated:
寧矣乎？吁！循不忘於嚬戚，而義必急乎公家，幽俗之厚有如此夫！抑於是而知周公告成王之微意也。觀民俗之厚，則先公之德化可知，亦可以見民性之未嘗不善也。苟有仇予，則非獨民之過，而君亦與有責焉矣。知先公之化，又知民之性，成王之卒爲有周令主也，有以哉！
龍旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，維民所止。肇域彼四海，四海來假。來假祁祁，景員維河。
吳中奭
同考試官教諭崔批：題意前後重疊，而是作聯絡有法，詞復俊雅，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭劉批：修詞古雅，析義精瑩，是爲善說詩者，允宜高薦。
同考試官學正徐批：鋪叙有體，而意味優揚，深得詩人之旨。
同考試官知縣李批：理趣精鑿，詞華粹雅，而高古之調，殆不可以時義目之者，宜用爲式。
translation_en:
…be at peace? Ah! Even amid distress and sorrow, they do not forget their duties [?], and righteousness requires them to give priority to the ruling house. Such was the generosity of the customs of You [?]! Here, moreover, we discern the subtle intention behind the Duke of Zhou’s admonition to King Cheng. From the generosity of the people’s customs, one can recognize the transforming virtue of the ancestral dukes; one can also see that the people’s nature has never been other than good. If any should “regard me as an enemy,” the fault lies not with the people alone: the ruler, too, bears responsibility. Understanding both the transforming influence of the ancestral dukes and the people’s nature—there was indeed a reason why King Cheng ultimately became a worthy ruler of Zhou!

“Ten chariots with dragon banners bear the great offerings of millet. The royal domain extends a thousand li: here the people dwell. He established the bounds of those lands within the Four Seas, and all within the Four Seas came to pay homage. They came in multitudes; the vast extent was like the River.”

Wu Zhongshi.

Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor, comments: “The theme repeats itself in its earlier and later portions, yet this composition connects them methodically. Its language is also distinguished and elegant. It should be recorded as a model.”

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Its diction is classically elegant, and its analysis of meaning precise and lucid. This is the work of one skilled in expounding the Book of Odes. It certainly merits a strong recommendation.”

Associate Examiner Xu, School Instructor, comments: “Its exposition is well structured, and its meaning and feeling unfold with grace and resonance. It deeply apprehends the poet’s intent.”

Associate Examiner Li, District Magistrate, comments: “Its ideas are penetrating and precise, and its literary expression refined and elegant. Its lofty, antique tone makes it scarcely possible to regard it merely as a contemporary examination essay. It should serve as a model.”

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍讀陶　批〔晉言高宗中興氣象〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔後〕〔殊可誦〕
商人美賢王一統之業而復表其盛焉夫天下
一統賢王中興之業盛矣宜商人頌美之無已
歟想其歌於廟祀者若謂武丁之興也其德旣
視湯而無愧其業亦繼湯而有光是故方命之
初諸侯固咸湯之統御也自表正風微而或不
免於渙矣今則建龍旂以昭物釆聿遵歲事之
修而承大糦以潔粢盛用效精禋之薦王祭所
===
供其罔後也奄有之初疆理固盡湯之版圖也
自撫綏道缺而或不免於析矣今則邦畿之所
止雖儉於千里之規而疆域之所肇實極乎四
海之遠王封所及其罔外也吾于龍旂承糦有
以見人心之齊焉孝享助於一人懽心萃於萬
國四海之內莫非王臣而同執畢至祈祈乎載
道之光矣今之人心其翕然方命之人心乎吾
于邦畿肇域有以見土宇之固焉表景山以爲
鎮環大河以爲疆千里之外莫非王土而丕基
punctuated:
考試官侍讀陶批〔晉言高宗中興氣象〕。
考試官洗馬馬批〔後〕〔殊可誦〕。
商人美賢王一統之業，而復表其盛焉。夫天下一統，賢王中興之業盛矣，宜商人頌美之無已歟！想其歌於廟祀者，若謂武丁之興也，其德旣視湯而無愧，其業亦繼湯而有光。是故方命之初，諸侯固咸湯之統御也，自表正風微，而或不免於渙矣。今則建龍旂以昭物釆，聿遵歲事之修，而承大糦以潔粢盛，用效精禋之薦。王祭所供，其罔後也。奄有之初，疆理固盡湯之版圖也，自撫綏道缺，而或不免於析矣。今則邦畿之所止，雖儉於千里之規，而疆域之所肇，實極乎四海之遠。王封所及，其罔外也。吾于龍旂承糦，有以見人心之齊焉。孝享助於一人，懽心萃於萬國，四海之內莫非王臣，而同執畢至，祈祈乎載道之光矣！今之人心，其翕然方命之人心乎！吾于邦畿肇域，有以見土宇之固焉。表景山以爲鎮，環大河以爲疆，千里之外莫非王土，而丕基
translation_en:
Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔Sets forth [?] the flourishing circumstances of Gaozong’s restoration.〕
Examiner Ma, Librarian, comments: 〔The latter part [?].〕〔Especially worthy of recitation.〕
The people of Shang praised the worthy king’s achievement in unifying the realm and further proclaimed its grandeur. With all under Heaven united, the worthy king’s achievement in restoring the dynasty was indeed magnificent. Was it not fitting that the people of Shang should praise it without end? Imagine their song at the ancestral temple sacrifices, as though saying: When Wu Ding rose to power, his virtue could be compared with Tang’s without shame, and his achievements carried on Tang’s work with added glory. Thus, when Tang first received the mandate, the regional lords were all indeed under his rule. But as the influence of upright leadership weakened, some fragmentation became unavoidable. Now, however, they erect dragon banners to display their ceremonial insignia, duly observe the annual rites, and present great offerings of grain, keeping the sacrificial grain pure and offering it in reverent sacrifice. In supplying the royal sacrifices, none falls behind.
When Tang first possessed the realm, all its demarcated lands lay within his dominion. But as the practice of pacifying and reassuring the people became deficient, some division became unavoidable. Now, although the royal domain is confined within the prescribed thousand li, the boundaries of the territory extend to the farthest reaches of the Four Seas. Wherever the king’s enfeoffments reach, none is left outside. In the dragon banners and the presentation of grain offerings, I can see the unity of people’s hearts. They assist the One Man in his filial offerings, and the joyful allegiance of the myriad states converges upon him. Within the Four Seas, none is other than the king’s subject. All alike bear their offerings and arrive together, proceeding in stately numbers—how splendidly they fill the roads! Are not the hearts of the people today united just as they were when Tang first received the mandate? In the royal domain and the extension of its boundaries, I can see the firmness of the realm. Mount Jing is designated its guardian mountain, and the great Yellow River encircles it as a boundary. Beyond the thousand li, no land is other than the king’s land, and the mighty foundation…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
光宅翼翼乎四方之極矣今之土宇其居然奄
有之土宇乎吁武丁之朝諸侯而有天下如此
振中葉之衰纘先后之緒信乎德之盛而業之
隆矣登歌于廟其可繹思也夫自昔繼世之君
撫有成業以人心土宇爲可恃而不思其本至
於日寖離析又狃於因循而莫之圖也不知土
宇之聯屬在人心之維繫在德或以震疊之
威經營天下則豈武丁之所以爲武者哉殷武
曰不僭不濫不敢怠遑噫其武德固如此
===
春秋
冬十月不雨〔僖公二年〕春王正月不雨夏
四月不雨　六月雨〔僖公三年〕
同考試官教諭葉　批〔同憂同樂俱本詩推〕
陳有則
〔見得旨且詞有操縱通篇明粹讀之灑然可以〕
〔爲經生式矣〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔意精而詞健〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔明切〕
punctuated:
光宅，翼翼乎四方之極矣！今之土宇，其居然奄有之土宇乎？吁！武丁之朝諸侯而有天下如此，振中葉之衰，纘先后之緒，信乎德之盛而業之隆矣！登歌于廟，其可繹思也夫！自昔繼世之君，撫有成業，以人心土宇爲可恃，而不思其本，至於日寖離析，又狃於因循而莫之圖也。不知土宇之聯屬在人心之維繫，在德。或以震疊之威經營天下，則豈武丁之所以爲武者哉？《殷武》曰：「不僭不濫，不敢怠遑。」噫！其武德固如此。

春秋
冬十月，不雨。〔僖公二年〕春王正月，不雨。夏四月，不雨。六月，雨。〔僖公三年〕
同考試官教諭葉，批〔同憂同樂，俱本詩推。〕
陳有則
〔見得旨，且詞有操縱，通篇明粹，讀之灑然，可以〕〔爲經生式矣。〕
考試官侍讀陶，批〔意精而詞健。〕
考試官洗馬馬，批〔明切。〕
translation_en:
…extends its glorious dominion, majestically serving as the standard for the four quarters! Is the territory now held simply territory possessed without effort? Ah! Such was Wu Ding’s reception of the feudal lords at court and his possession of all under Heaven. He reversed the decline of the dynasty’s middle years and continued the legacy of the former sovereigns. Truly, his virtue flourished and his achievements were exalted! Sung in the ancestral temple, these words surely invite sustained reflection. From antiquity, rulers who inherited the throne took possession of an established realm, regarding the people’s allegiance and their territorial holdings as dependable without considering their foundation. When these gradually fell apart, they remained accustomed to following established routines and made no effort to remedy matters. They did not understand that territorial cohesion depends upon maintaining the people’s allegiance, and upon virtue. If someone sought to govern all under Heaven through the force of overwhelming intimidation, could this be what made Wu Ding truly martial? “The Martial Power of Yin” says: “Neither erring nor excessive, he dared not idle or take his ease.” Ah! Such indeed was his martial virtue.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In winter, in the tenth month, there was no rain.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi.〕 “In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, there was no rain. In summer, in the fourth month, there was no rain. In the sixth month, it rained.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕
Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: 〔“Sharing sorrow and sharing joy: both are developed from the Odes.”〕
Chen Youze
〔“He has grasped the purport, and his language displays control and flexibility. The entire piece is lucid and refined; reading it is refreshing. It may〕〔serve as a model for students of the Classics.”〕
Examiner Tao, Expositor-in-waiting, comments: 〔“The ideas are precise and the language vigorous.”〕
Examiner Ma, Library Attendant, comments: 〔“Clear and pertinent.”〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
春秋紀天澤之逆順嘉內君以民事係憂樂也
甚矣君當以民心爲心也僖公閔雨喜雨無不
與民同者此春秋所以嘉之歟僖公二年嘗三
時不雨矣迨六月而雨焉此亦天不可必之常
耳春秋每書不雨又特書雨以爲見僖公與民
同憂樂者何蓋詩稱僖公儉用愛民務農重穀
其賢有足徵者若夫三時不雨則穀有不滋農
無所賴而國用民生俱困矣公也能無憂乎吾
知當不雨之歷三時也必不以饑之在民者諉
===
諸天而惟以災之自天者責諸已其修省以回
天意有不勝靡瞻靡顧者觀於詩可推也夫雨
之愆期農夫之憂也乃公不以爲農夫憂而自
憂非所謂憂民之憂者乎故每時必書志勤也
嘉公之與民同憂也至於六月雨則穀且終播
農庶有秋而用絀民病可蘇矣公也能無樂乎
吾知當雨之及六月也必不以民之沃膏者爲
適然而惟以天之垂貺者爲國幸其懽忻以承
天休有不啻既霑既足者推諸詩可見也夫義
punctuated:
春秋紀天澤之逆順，嘉內君以民事係憂樂也。

甚矣，君當以民心爲心也！僖公閔雨喜雨，無不與民同者，此春秋所以嘉之歟？僖公二年，嘗三時不雨矣，迨六月而雨焉，此亦天不可必之常耳。春秋每書不雨，又特書雨，以爲見僖公與民同憂樂者，何？蓋詩稱僖公儉用愛民，務農重穀，其賢有足徵者。若夫三時不雨，則穀有不滋，農無所賴，而國用民生俱困矣。公也能無憂乎？吾知當不雨之歷三時也，必不以饑之在民者諉諸天，而惟以災之自天者責諸已。其修省以回天意，有不勝靡瞻靡顧者，觀於詩可推也。夫雨之愆期，農夫之憂也，乃公不以爲農夫憂而自憂，非所謂憂民之憂者乎？故每時必書，志勤也，嘉公之與民同憂也。

至於六月雨，則穀且終播，農庶有秋，而用絀民病可蘇矣。公也能無樂乎？吾知當雨之及六月也，必不以民之沃膏者爲適然，而惟以天之垂貺者爲國幸。其懽忻以承天休，有不啻既霑既足者，推諸詩可見也。夫義
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals records whether Heaven’s nourishing rain fails or arrives in due course, commending the ruler of its own state for making the people’s affairs the source of his sorrow and joy.

How imperative it is that a ruler take the people’s heart as his own! Duke Xi shared with the people both anxiety over rain and joy at its arrival. Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him? In Duke Xi’s second year, there were three seasons without rain; only in the sixth month did rain arrive. This was simply another instance of Heaven’s habitual unpredictability. Why, then, is the Annals’ recording of each rainless season, and its special recording of the rain, understood to reveal Duke Xi’s sharing in the people’s sorrow and joy? The Book of Odes praises Duke Xi for frugality in expenditure, love for the people, diligence in agriculture, and esteem for grain. There is sufficient evidence of his worthiness. When three seasons passed without rain, grain could not flourish, farmers had nothing to depend upon, and both state finances and the people’s livelihood fell into distress. Could the duke have been free of sorrow? I know that, during those three rainless seasons, he surely did not blame Heaven for the people’s hunger, but held himself responsible for the calamity sent by Heaven. In cultivating himself and examining his conduct to turn Heaven’s intentions, his anxious searching knew no bounds—there was nowhere he did not look, nowhere he did not turn. This can be inferred from the Odes. Rain’s failure to arrive on time is the farmer’s sorrow; yet the duke regarded it as his own sorrow, rather than merely the farmer’s. Was this not what is meant by grieving over the people’s grief? Thus each season is invariably recorded to mark his diligence and commend his sharing in the people’s sorrow.

When rain arrived in the sixth month, sowing could at last be completed, farmers could hope for a harvest, and straitened finances and the people’s distress could find relief. Could the duke have been without joy? I know that, when rain arrived in the sixth month, he surely did not regard the rich moisture bestowed upon the people as mere chance, but considered Heaven’s gift a blessing for the state. His rejoicing as he received Heaven’s favor went beyond the satisfaction of having been watered and having received enough. This can be seen by inference from the Odes. Now, rain [?] …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之濟旱農夫之慶也乃公不以爲農夫慶而自
慶非所謂樂民之樂者乎故雨必特書志喜也
嘉公之與民同樂也夫與民同憂民斯得以解
其憂與民同樂民斯得以遂其樂僖公之賢其
春秋之僅見者乎雖然同樂又本於同憂也盖
憂所以致其樂未有不同憂而能同樂者僖公
飭過求已理寃放倿庶幾雲漢桑林矣而六月
之雨要自憂勤感召中來也嗚呼春秋豈直爲
魯僖書哉示天下後世以君國子民之道固如
===
此
夏五月公自京師遂會晉侯齊侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯邾人滕人伐秦〔成公十有〕
三年
江有源
同考試官教諭葉　批〔重在書法上發揮甚是而會傳周悉用意深遠尤非淺學可到〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔善發聖人存臣禮意〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔其詞雅其思深〕
punctuated:
之濟旱，農夫之慶也，乃公不以爲農夫慶而自慶，非所謂樂民之樂者乎？故雨必特書，志喜也，嘉公之與民同樂也。夫與民同憂，民斯得以解其憂；與民同樂，民斯得以遂其樂。僖公之賢，其春秋之僅見者乎？雖然，同樂又本於同憂也。盖憂所以致其樂，未有不同憂而能同樂者。僖公飭過求已，理寃放倿，庶幾雲漢、桑林矣，而六月之雨，要自憂勤感召中來也。嗚呼！春秋豈直爲魯僖書哉？示天下後世以君國子民之道，固如此。
夏五月，公自京師，遂會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人、滕人伐秦。〔成公十有〕三年。
江有源。
同考試官教諭葉，批〔重在書法上發揮甚是而會傳周悉用意深遠尤非淺學可到〕。
考試官侍讀陶，批〔善發聖人存臣禮意〕。
考試官洗馬馬，批〔其詞雅其思深〕。
translation_en:
…relieving the drought [?] was cause for the farmers to rejoice. Yet the duke did not regard this as merely the farmers’ joy, but rejoiced himself. Was this not what is meant by taking joy in the people’s joy? Thus the rain is expressly recorded to mark his gladness and commend his sharing the people’s joy. When a ruler shares the people’s anxieties, they can obtain relief from those anxieties; when he shares their joy, they can attain its fulfillment. Was not Duke Xi’s worthiness something rarely seen in the Spring and Autumn Annals? Nevertheless, sharing their joy is rooted in sharing their anxieties. Anxiety is what brings about joy: no one who fails to share their anxieties can share their joy. Duke Xi corrected his faults and examined himself [?], redressed injustices, and dismissed flatterers, approaching the examples of “The Milky Way” and the prayer at Sanglin. The rain in the sixth month ultimately came in response to his anxious diligence. Ah! Were the Spring and Autumn Annals written merely for Duke Xi of Lu? This is indeed how they teach all the world and later generations the way to rule a state and cherish its people as one’s children.
“In summer, in the fifth month, the duke proceeded from the royal capital and thereupon joined the marquises of Jin and Qi, the dukes of Song and Wei, the earls of Zheng and Cao, and men of Zhu and Teng in attacking Qin.” (Thirteenth year of Duke Cheng.)
Jiang Youyuan.
Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “The emphasis on expounding the principles of the Annals’ wording is entirely right. His comprehensive integration of the commentaries and the depth and reach of his interpretation are especially beyond the attainment of shallow scholarship.”
Examiner Tao, Expositor-in-waiting, comments: “He ably brings out the Sage’s intention to preserve the ritual proprieties of a subject.”
Examiner Ma, Librarian, comments: “His language is elegant, and his thought profound.”

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
春秋紀諸侯之用兵而特存尊王之禮焉葢臣
禮以尊王爲重也春秋以伐秦爲遂事者非以
此哉昔魯成及列國將會晉以伐秦因過周而
入覲乃自周往伐焉夫伐秦者其本謀也覲周
者其繼事也春秋乃以伐秦爲繼事者何葢人
臣之禮莫大於尊王尊王之禮莫重於朝覲諸
侯侵伐之出多矣而朝禮則罔修也天王聘使
之遣屢矣而覲禮則弗舉也僅此如京之行又
以過都之便朝覲之典葢幾於廢矣人臣之禮
===
將何能存乎聖人修經至此葢有深爲之懼者
矣使惟據事直書則紀實之信雖傳而苟簡之
儀何以示天下不恭之罪固著而陵替之俗何
以訓方來故書公自京師遂會伐秦若曰車馬
之動本爲周而集干戈之動特自周而行耳葢
意在修怨而不在修禮固其實也去其實以全
名使見者於是而有感焉必以朝禮爲重而叔
世之墜典庶幾其可復興乎先於王事而後於
伯事祇其名耳正其名以統實使聞者因是而
punctuated: 春秋紀諸侯之用兵，而特存尊王之禮焉，葢臣禮以尊王爲重也。春秋以伐秦爲遂事者，非以此哉？昔魯成及列國將會晉以伐秦，因過周而入覲，乃自周往伐焉。夫伐秦者，其本謀也；覲周者，其繼事也。春秋乃以伐秦爲繼事者，何？葢人臣之禮，莫大於尊王；尊王之禮，莫重於朝覲。諸侯侵伐之出多矣，而朝禮則罔修也；天王聘使之遣屢矣，而覲禮則弗舉也。僅此如京之行，又以過都之便，朝覲之典葢幾於廢矣，人臣之禮將何能存乎？聖人修經至此，葢有深爲之懼者矣。使惟據事直書，則紀實之信雖傳，而苟簡之儀何以示天下？不恭之罪固著，而陵替之俗何以訓方來？故書「公自京師遂會伐秦」，若曰車馬之動，本爲周而集；干戈之動，特自周而行耳。葢意在修怨，而不在修禮，固其實也。去其實以全名，使見者於是而有感焉，必以朝禮爲重，而叔世之墜典，庶幾其可復興乎？先於王事而後於伯事，祇其名耳。正其名以統實，使聞者因是而
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the feudal lords’ use of arms, yet takes particular care to preserve the rites of honoring the king. For in the ritual duties of a subject, honoring the king is paramount. Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals treats the campaign against Qin as a subsequent undertaking?

Formerly, Duke Cheng of Lu and the other states were about to join Jin in attacking Qin. Passing through Zhou, he went in for an audience and then proceeded from Zhou to the campaign. Attacking Qin was his original plan; having an audience at Zhou was an additional undertaking. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals treat the attack on Qin as the additional undertaking? Among a subject’s ritual duties, none is greater than honoring the king; among the rites for honoring the king, none is more important than attendance at court. The feudal lords had frequently gone out on invasions and punitive expeditions, yet neglected the rites of court attendance. The Heavenly King had repeatedly dispatched envoys on diplomatic visits, yet the rites of audience were not performed. Even this solitary journey to the capital was merely a matter of taking advantage of passing through it. The prescribed observances of court audience had almost fallen into disuse. How, then, could the ritual duties of a subject survive?

When the Sage reached this point in compiling the Classic, he surely felt profound apprehension. Had he merely written a straightforward account of events, the faithful record of the facts would indeed have been transmitted, but how could such perfunctory observance be presented as an example to the world? The offense of disrespect would certainly have been exposed, but how could customs of declining authority and order instruct future generations? Thus he wrote, “The duke, from the royal capital, thereupon joined in the campaign against Qin.” It is as though he were saying that the chariots and horses had originally assembled for Zhou’s sake, and that the armed expedition merely proceeded from Zhou afterward.

That the intention was to pursue a grievance, rather than to perform the rites, was indeed the reality. By setting aside that reality to preserve the proper designation, he caused readers to be moved by this account and necessarily to attach importance to the rites of court attendance. Might the abandoned observances of a declining age thus perhaps be revived? To put service to the king before service to the hegemon was only the nominal account. By rectifying the designation so that it might govern actual conduct, he caused those who heard it thereby to…

text:

不終廢乎此義行則水木敦本源之懷而侯度
聿修於百辟江漢會朝宗之勢而王靈丕振於
四方天理存人欲消而大倫正矣噫聖人愛禮
之意何至哉抑於是而見周劉子成子之罪焉
禮樂征伐自天子出者也諸侯擅興甲兵而敢
於過都此其罪又不止朝禮之失也而可弗問
乎宣伯禮而獻子賄乃舍其大者而問受脤之
惰則將焉用彼相耶是故二子在會削而不書
===
讀經者宜自得之矣
禮記
知其義而敬守之天子之所以治天下也

translation_en:
…would reflect upon this and necessarily regard service to the king as paramount. Might the surviving rites of a debased age [?] thus escape permanent abandonment? If this principle prevails, the many lords will cultivate the sentiment of honoring their origins—as water has its source and trees their roots—and duly observe the standards governing the feudal lords. Like the Jiang and Han rivers converging toward the sea, they will assemble in allegiance, and royal authority will be greatly strengthened throughout the realm. Heavenly principle will endure, human desires will diminish, and the great human relationships will be set right. Ah! How profound was the Sage’s devotion to ritual!

Here, moreover, we see the culpability of Liuzi and Chengzi of Zhou. Ritual, music, and punitive expeditions issue from the Son of Heaven. The feudal lords mobilized troops on their own authority and dared to pass through the royal capital: their offense went beyond a failure in the rites of court attendance. Could it be left unexamined? Xuanbo observed ritual, while Xianzi offered bribes; yet these ministers disregarded the greater offense and questioned only negligence in receiving sacrificial meat. What use, then, were such ministers? Thus, although the two attended the gathering, their names were excised and left unrecorded. Readers of the Classic should grasp this for themselves.

Book of Rites

“To understand its meaning and reverently uphold it: this is how the Son of Heaven governs all under Heaven.”

Wei Lianggui

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之可以爲國也知義而敬守則禮尊矣而措之
於治有不裕如者乎記禮者之意蓋謂禮之尊
也尊其義也義難知也而不可不知也此固非
祝史之所及矣爲人君者誠能學於古訓於所
以非强世者而悉其精微之藴考諸先王於所
以不相襲者而洞其制作之原有見於天道之
不容不然者禮也而翼翼是持凡其加身而錯
前者一皆不越於率履有見於人情之不可不
然者禮也而兢兢有執凡其體常而盡變者莫
===
不奉之以周旋如此則於禮也可謂尊之矣而
所以治天下者豈外是哉吾知有禮以治躬則
君身端於中正之履而不顯之德以裕有禮以
達分則民志定於上下之辨而不爭之俗由興
義之知也會作述之精而明聖於我備矣天下
之事有知之不明處之不當者乎禮之舉也通
參贊之道而天地將爲昭矣天下之治有推之
不準動之不化者乎蓋禮讓之於爲國也無難
而明義之於天下也甚易耳故曰天子之所以
punctuated: 之可以爲國也！知義而敬守，則禮尊矣，而措之於治，有不裕如者乎？記禮者之意，蓋謂禮之尊也，尊其義也。義難知也，而不可不知也，此固非祝史之所及矣。爲人君者，誠能學於古訓，於所以非强世者而悉其精微之藴；考諸先王，於所以不相襲者而洞其制作之原。有見於天道之不容不然者，禮也，而翼翼是持，凡其加身而錯前者，一皆不越於率履；有見於人情之不可不然者，禮也，而兢兢有執，凡其體常而盡變者，莫不奉之以周旋。如此，則於禮也，可謂尊之矣，而所以治天下者，豈外是哉？吾知有禮以治躬，則君身端於中正之履，而不顯之德以裕；有禮以達分，則民志定於上下之辨，而不爭之俗由興。義之知也，會作述之精，而明聖於我備矣，天下之事，有知之不明、處之不當者乎？禮之舉也，通參贊之道，而天地將爲昭矣，天下之治，有推之不準、動之不化者乎？蓋禮讓之於爲國也無難，而明義之於天下也甚易耳。故曰：「天子之所以
translation_en:
…that ritual can serve to govern a state! When its meaning is understood and it is reverently upheld, ritual is honored. Applied to government, could it fail to afford ample scope for action? The intention of the recorder of ritual was presumably that honoring ritual means honoring its meaning. That meaning is difficult to understand, yet one cannot leave it uncomprehended. This assuredly lies beyond the reach of invocators and scribes.

If a ruler can truly study ancient teachings, fully grasping their subtle profundities in what does not compel the age [?], and examine the former kings, penetrating the origins of their institutions in those respects in which they did not simply follow their predecessors, he will perceive that ritual embodies what the Way of Heaven necessarily requires. He will uphold it with reverent care, and everything that pertains to his person or is set before him will conform to its prescribed conduct. He will perceive that ritual embodies what human feelings necessarily require, and hold fast to it with vigilant care. In embodying enduring norms and responding fully to changing circumstances, he will conduct himself throughout in accordance with it. In this way he may indeed be said to honor ritual. Could the means of governing all under Heaven lie outside this?

I know that, with ritual to regulate his own person, the ruler will be upright in conduct that is centered and correct, and his unseen virtue will abound. With ritual to give effect to distinctions of status, the people's aspirations will be settled through the differentiation of superior and inferior, and customs free of contention will arise. Understanding ritual's meaning brings together the essence of both creating institutions and transmitting them, so that discernment and sagacity are fully present in oneself. Among the affairs of all under Heaven, could there then be anything understood unclearly or handled improperly? Putting ritual into practice opens the way to participating in and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth, whose workings will thereby be made manifest. In governing all under Heaven, could any application then fail to accord with the proper standard, or any action fail to bring about transformation? Thus, with ritual and deference, governing a state presents no difficulty; and with its meaning made clear, ordering all under Heaven is very easy indeed. Hence the statement: “That by which the Son of Heaven…”

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
治天下也夫禮之所關其大如此若之何而不
敬以尊也有天下者其無忽諸大抵禮者聖人
所以為國而樹之坊者也周之興也其坊固也
其衰也大夫僭諸侯諸侯僭天子坊之壞也所
由來漸矣是知禮興則國與興禮衰則國亦因
之人君之尊禮其所以自尊乎然非敬則不獨
數為粗迹而義亦微茫何執乎記者不徒曰知
其義而必曰敬守之其旨深矣
百官得其宜萬事得其序
曹司勳

〔而人君德盛養純意誠然溢於言表必佳士也〕

===
人君德化之成有徵於官正若有徵於事治者
蓋德盛而化斯神也官正事治非至德其孰能
如此乎且天子者百官之表也萬事之綱也君
punctuated:
治天下也。夫禮之所關，其大如此，若之何而不敬以尊也？有天下者，其無忽諸！大抵禮者，聖人所以為國而樹之坊者也。周之興也，其坊固也；其衰也，大夫僭諸侯，諸侯僭天子，坊之壞也，所由來漸矣。是知禮興則國與興，禮衰則國亦因之。人君之尊禮，其所以自尊乎！然非敬，則不獨數為粗迹，而義亦微茫，何執乎？記者不徒曰知其義，而必曰敬守之，其旨深矣。
百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
曹司勳

translation_en:
…governs All-under-Heaven. Since ritual has such far-reaching importance, how could one fail to honor it with reverence? Let those who possess All-under-Heaven never neglect it! Broadly speaking, ritual is the barrier that the sages established to govern the state. When the Zhou rose, its barriers were firm. When it declined, grand masters usurped the prerogatives of the regional lords, and regional lords usurped those of the Son of Heaven. The breakdown of these barriers developed gradually. Thus we know that when ritual flourishes, the state flourishes with it; when ritual declines, the state likewise follows. Is not a ruler’s honoring of ritual the means by which he honors himself? Yet without reverence, not only do ritual prescriptions become mere outward forms, but their meaning also grows obscure: what then can one hold fast to? The author of the Record does not merely say to understand its meaning, but insists on reverently upholding it. The import of this is profound indeed.
“The hundred officials each attain their proper place, and the myriad affairs each attain their proper order.”
Cao Sixun
Associate Examiner Hong, District Magistrate, comments: 〔The two words “proper place” and “order” are expounded almost exhaustively.〕〔Moreover, the idea of the ruler’s abundant virtue and pure self-cultivation truly shines through beyond the words. He must be an excellent scholar.〕 Accept this essay.
Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting, comments: 〔Orderly and clean.〕
Examiner Ma, Librarian, comments: 〔Elegant.〕
The fulfillment of a ruler’s transforming influence through virtue is evidenced in the proper conduct of officials, just as it is evidenced in the orderly management of affairs. For when virtue abounds, its transforming influence becomes wondrous. Without consummate virtue, who could bring officials and affairs into such good order? Moreover, the Son of Heaven is the exemplar for the hundred officials and the guiding cord for the myriad affairs. The ruler’s…

…the Way of the ruler has been attained; thus, through it he illuminates and oversees the hundred officials, who thereby attain their proper fitness. [Illegible character] The hundred officials differ in their capacities, but all receive commands from the ruler; how much more so when an enlightened ruler instructs and guides them! We see that their virtue invariably matches their rank: those at his side are worthy men, all united in purpose to uphold their sovereign. Their abilities invariably match their duties: tireless morning and night, all know to join their efforts in attending reverently to their responsibilities. The great ministers observe the laws; though exalted, they dare not grow arrogant. The lesser ministers maintain their integrity; though lowly, they dare not indulge in extravagance. Although each of the hundred officials has his own proper fitness, what makes them fit is simply this: when the head is enlightened, the arms and legs naturally become capable. Never has there been a ruler under Heaven without ministers. Through this he manages the myriad affairs, which thereby attain their proper order. Affairs are exceedingly intricate, yet all are subject to the ruler’s commands; how much more so when worthy ministers share in their management! We may then see adaptation fully answering every change, so that all achievements flourish, clearly arranged and free of disorder; measures put into practice to achieve complete effectiveness, so that all things assume their proper forms [?], methodically arranged and free of confusion. The main guiding principles are rectified, and the warp and weft of government acquire a clear pattern; the many subsidiary strands are extended, and even the subtlest beginnings become fully apparent. Although each of the myriad affairs has its own natural order, what orders them is simply this: when an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers come together, all affairs naturally become settled. Never has there been anyone capable of governing without methods of government.
Ah! Officials are appointed to accomplish affairs: when they are properly fitted, affairs do not fail. Affairs must be entrusted to officials: when they are ordered, no official duties are neglected. Yet all this is rooted in the ruler’s virtue. How could it be attained by mere good fortune? I have maintained that the ruler’s heart is the source of all transforming influence. If the cultivation of his heart remains incomplete, his employment of men and conduct of government will often depart from what is proper. To desire…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
序且宜也得乎故曰正心以正朝廷而百官而
萬民一於正焉此知本之說也噫昔虞庭賡
歌之日而時幾率作之念尤亟儆焉節已宜已
序可遽足耶是故帝王貴純心也
第貳場
論
堯舜其心至今在
吳汝綸
同考試官教諭崔　批〔一論滾滾數千言發攄胸中無限蘊蓄而縱橫曲折反覆悠揚模寫堯舜之心以道爲體讀之如身遊唐虞之庭面受二帝心法者敬仰敬仰〕
===
同考試官教諭劉　批〔學識淵宏議論精到是必從事心學而上契堯舜之心源者錄以爲式〕
同考試官學正徐　批〔體格宏大而圓詞氣俊逸而古寫出堯舜之心宛然如在殆可以式今傳後者乎〕
punctuated:
序且宜也，得乎？故曰：正心以正朝廷，而百官，而萬民，一於正焉。此知本之說也。噫！昔虞庭賡歌之日，而時幾率作之念尤亟儆焉。節已宜，已序，可遽足耶？是故帝王貴純心也。
第貳場
論
堯舜其心至今在
吳汝綸
同考試官教諭崔批〔一論滾滾數千言，發攄胸中無限蘊蓄，而縱橫曲折，反覆悠揚，模寫堯舜之心，以道爲體。讀之，如身遊唐虞之庭，面受二帝心法者。敬仰！敬仰！〕
同考試官教諭劉批〔學識淵宏，議論精到，是必從事心學而上契堯舜之心源者，錄以爲式。〕
同考試官學正徐批〔體格宏大而圓，詞氣俊逸而古，寫出堯舜之心，宛然如在，殆可以式今傳後者乎！〕
translation_en:
…could order and fitting arrangement be attained? Hence the saying: rectify the heart in order to rectify the court, then the hundred officials, then the myriad people, bringing all alike to rectitude. This is what it means to understand the root. Ah! In ancient times, when ruler and ministers exchanged songs at Shun’s court, they were especially urgent in reminding themselves that every incipient affair must be attended to. Once matters are regulated, fittingly arranged, and ordered [?], can one immediately rest content? Thus emperors and kings prize purity of heart.
Second Session
Discourse
“The Hearts of Yao and Shun Endure to This Day”
Wu Rulun
Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor, comments: 〔This discourse pours forth in several thousand words, giving expression to the limitless store of learning within the author’s breast. Ranging freely, turning through intricate developments, returning repeatedly to its themes with a lingering cadence, it portrays the hearts of Yao and Shun, taking the Way as their substance. Reading it is like personally visiting the courts of Yao and Shun and receiving instruction in the two emperors’ teaching of the heart face to face. I bow in admiration! I bow in admiration!〕
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔His learning and understanding are profound and expansive, and his arguments are precise and penetrating. He must surely have devoted himself to the learning of the heart and thereby attained accord with the very source of Yao’s and Shun’s hearts. Recorded here as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔Its structure is grand and rounded; its language and spirit are gracefully unfettered and antique. It depicts the hearts of Yao and Shun so vividly that they seem present before us. Surely this deserves to serve as a model for the present and to be transmitted to posterity!〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官知縣李　批
〔堯舜之心萬世常存不外一道子獨以此立論而曲折抑揚闡發殆盡且義趣淵深詞調高古有學有養之士也敬服敬服〕
考試官侍讀陶　批
〔立論正大而宏博之學足以發之讀此則堯舜之心眞可見矣當是作家〕
考試官洗馬馬　批
〔議論亹亹似亦能知堯舜之心者〕
聖人之心歷萬世而常存焉其以道爲體者乎
===
蓋聖人之心道之會也非獨聖人之心也所以
爲天地立心者也聖人會道之全體以其心爲
天地立心天地不息道亦不息道不息聖人之
心亦不息夫固不依形而立不待生而存者也
謂聖人旣歿而其心遂與其形之化者同耶是
殆觀聖人之心以形而不知觀聖人之心以道
道不與形爲存亡心亦不隨形而化故後之人
無志乎聖人之心則已有志乎聖人之心有不
思思則得之有不求求則可見由千百載之後
punctuated:
同考試官知縣李批〔堯舜之心，萬世常存，不外一道。子獨以此立論，而曲折抑揚，闡發殆盡。且義趣淵深，詞調高古，有學有養之士也。敬服！敬服！〕
考試官侍讀陶批〔立論正大，而宏博之學足以發之。讀此，則堯舜之心眞可見矣。當是作家。〕
考試官洗馬馬批〔議論亹亹，似亦能知堯舜之心者。〕
聖人之心，歷萬世而常存焉，其以道爲體者乎？
蓋聖人之心，道之會也。非獨聖人之心也，所以爲天地立心者也。聖人會道之全體，以其心爲天地立心。天地不息，道亦不息；道不息，聖人之心亦不息。夫固不依形而立，不待生而存者也。謂聖人旣歿，而其心遂與其形之化者同耶？是殆觀聖人之心以形，而不知觀聖人之心以道。道不與形爲存亡，心亦不隨形而化。故後之人，無志乎聖人之心則已；有志乎聖人之心，有不思，思則得之；有不求，求則可見。由千百載之後
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, District Magistrate: 〔The minds of Yao and Shun endure through all ages and are nothing other than the one Way. You have taken this alone as the basis of your argument, developing it almost exhaustively through its turns and shifts of emphasis. Moreover, the meaning is profound and the diction lofty and antique. You are a man of learning and self-cultivation. Admirable! Admirable!〕
Comment by Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting: 〔The argument is upright and grand, and ample, wide-ranging learning serves to develop it fully. Reading this, one can truly perceive the minds of Yao and Shun. Surely this is an accomplished writer.〕
Comment by Examiner Ma, Librarian of the Heir Apparent: 〔The argument unfolds tirelessly; the author, too, seems capable of understanding the minds of Yao and Shun.〕
The mind of the sage endures through myriad ages. Is this because it takes the Way as its substance?
For the mind of the sage is where the Way converges. It is not merely the sage’s own mind: it is that by which a mind is established for Heaven and Earth. The sage comprehends the Way in its entirety and, through his own mind, establishes a mind for Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth never cease, and neither does the Way; since the Way never ceases, neither does the sage’s mind. It assuredly does not depend upon bodily form to stand, nor upon life to exist. Can one say that, once the sage has died, his mind undergoes the same transformation as his bodily form? This would surely be to regard the sage’s mind in terms of bodily form, without knowing how to regard it in terms of the Way. The Way does not come into being or perish along with bodily form; neither does the mind undergo transformation along with that form. Thus, if people of later ages have no aspiration toward the sage’s mind, there is nothing more to say. But if they do aspire toward it, they may fail to reflect upon it; once they reflect, they attain it. They may fail to seek it; once they seek, it can be perceived. From a vantage point hundreds or thousands of years later…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而可以會聖人之精於千百載之前一道體爲
之感通焉耳程子謂堯舜數千年矣而其心至
今在非心堯舜之心者其能創爲此說乎且聖
人何以爲天地立心也天地生民物凡可以爲
之所者無不欲爲也而其勢不能也於是乎生
聖人而畀之以道而寄之以心聖人以道存之
而爲心又以其心運之而爲治以盡民物之性
以成天地之能是天地無心以聖人之心爲心
聖人有心而實體天地以爲心是心也以道爲
===
體者也至公至正至虛至明至神至大者也蓋
得之天地之本然而又與天地古今相爲流通
者也故能爲天地立心也或曰聖人在以其心
爲天地立心固也聖人不在則與其不可傳者
往矣即二典三謨皆糟䰟也而謂堯舜之心至
今在不幾於玄虛其說而欺天下後世矣乎曰
以形觀聖人則不特虞之時已無堯夏之時已
無舜自穀林蒼梧之既掩而堯舜之跡無一存
者矣而況至於今乎以道求聖人之心則其以
punctuated:
而可以會聖人之精於千百載之前，一道體爲之感通焉耳。程子謂：「堯舜數千年矣，而其心至今在。」非心堯舜之心者，其能創爲此說乎？且聖人何以爲天地立心也？天地生民物，凡可以爲之所者，無不欲爲也，而其勢不能也。於是乎生聖人而畀之以道，而寄之以心。聖人以道存之而爲心，又以其心運之而爲治，以盡民物之性，以成天地之能。是天地無心，以聖人之心爲心；聖人有心，而實體天地以爲心。是心也，以道爲體者也，至公至正、至虛至明、至神至大者也。蓋得之天地之本然，而又與天地古今相爲流通者也，故能爲天地立心也。
或曰：「聖人在，以其心爲天地立心，固也。聖人不在，則與其不可傳者往矣。即二典三謨，皆糟䰟也，而謂堯舜之心至今在，不幾於玄虛其說而欺天下後世矣乎？」曰：「以形觀聖人，則不特虞之時已無堯、夏之時已無舜，自穀林、蒼梧之既掩，而堯舜之跡無一存者矣，而況至於今乎？以道求聖人之心，則其以
translation_en:
…and one can comprehend the essential spirit of sages who lived hundreds or thousands of years before. It is simply the single substance of the Way that enables this sympathetic communion. Master Cheng said, “Yao and Shun lived several thousand years ago, yet their hearts remain to this day.” Could anyone who had not made the hearts of Yao and Shun his own have originated such a statement? Moreover, how do sages establish a heart for Heaven and Earth? Heaven and Earth bring forth people and things; whatever might provide them with a proper place, they wish to do, yet their powers do not permit it. Thus they bring forth sages, endow them with the Way, and entrust it to their hearts. The sages preserve it through the Way, making it their heart; they then put it into operation through their hearts, making it government, so as to fulfill the natures of people and things and bring the capacities of Heaven and Earth to completion. Thus Heaven and Earth have no heart, but take the sages’ hearts as their heart; sages have hearts, but truly embody Heaven and Earth in making them their hearts. This heart takes the Way as its substance. It is supremely impartial and upright, supremely empty and luminous, supremely numinous and vast. It derives from the original nature of Heaven and Earth and flows in mutual communion with them throughout past and present. Hence it can establish a heart for Heaven and Earth.
Someone says: “While sages are alive, they establish a heart for Heaven and Earth through their own hearts—certainly. But when sages are no longer here, they depart together with what cannot be transmitted. Even the Two Canons and Three Counsels are mere dregs [?]. To say that the hearts of Yao and Shun remain to this day—is this not almost to make one’s doctrine abstruse and empty, deceiving the world and later generations?” The reply is: “If one regards sages in terms of bodily form, it is not merely that Yao was already gone in the time of Yu, and Shun in the time of Xia. Once their graves at Gulin and Cangwu had been closed, not a single trace of Yao and Shun remained—how much less could any remain today? But if one seeks the sages’ hearts through the Way, then that which takes as its…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
道爲體者乘天地之正御六氣之變以遊乎無
窮官天地府萬物直寓六骸而未嘗泯者歷萬
世可常存也而何但於今日夫典謨豈盡糟魄
也哉吾嘗卽典謨而窺堯舜之心矣舉元凱誅
四凶舍子而與賢殛鯀而興禹不可以見其心
之至公乎考中星正日同律度量衡封山濬川
類帝禋宗敷教明刑典禮諧音塈讒說殄行不
可以見其心之至正乎稽衆舍己好問好察用
其中於民不可以見其心之至虛乎欽明濬哲
===
闢門明目達聰不可以見其心之至明乎德之
廣運至於被四表治之從欲至於動四方不可
以見其心之至神乎其仁如天其德好生自九
族之睦以至萬邦之雍自三苗之格以至上下
草木鳥獸咸若巍巍蕩蕩而視如浮雲不可以
見其心之至大乎然可以見其心也而非其心
之所在也以爲在典謨也當堯舜存時則何在
也以爲在堯舜也比堯舜旣歿則又何在也蓋
以道爲體者也得之天地之本然而流行於天
punctuated: 道爲體者，乘天地之正，御六氣之變，以遊乎無窮，官天地，府萬物，直寓六骸而未嘗泯者，歷萬世可常存也，而何但於今日？夫典謨豈盡糟魄也哉？吾嘗卽典謨而窺堯舜之心矣。舉元凱，誅四凶，舍子而與賢，殛鯀而興禹，不可以見其心之至公乎？考中星，正日，同律度量衡，封山濬川，類帝禋宗，敷教明刑，典禮諧音，塈讒說殄行，不可以見其心之至正乎？稽衆舍己，好問好察，用其中於民，不可以見其心之至虛乎？欽明濬哲，闢門明目達聰，不可以見其心之至明乎？德之廣運，至於被四表；治之從欲，至於動四方，不可以見其心之至神乎？其仁如天，其德好生，自九族之睦以至萬邦之雍，自三苗之格以至上下草木鳥獸咸若，巍巍蕩蕩而視如浮雲，不可以見其心之至大乎？然可以見其心也，而非其心之所在也。以爲在典謨也，當堯舜存時則何在也？以爲在堯舜也，比堯舜旣歿則又何在也？蓋以道爲體者也，得之天地之本然而流行於天
translation_en: …that which takes the Way as its substance rides upon the proper course of Heaven and Earth, harnesses the transformations of the six vital energies, and roams the limitless. It makes Heaven and Earth its offices and the myriad things its storehouse. Merely lodging in the six parts of the body, it has never been extinguished and can endure through ten thousand generations. Why should it endure only until today? Can the Canons and Counsels really be nothing but dregs? I have sought through the Canons and Counsels to glimpse the hearts of Yao and Shun. They promoted the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai, punished the Four Miscreants, passed over their sons to confer rule upon worthy men, put Gun to death, and raised up Yu. Can we not see in these acts the utmost impartiality of their hearts? They observed the stars culminating at dusk and dawn, regulated the calendar, standardized pitch pipes, measures, and weights, established sacrifices to the mountains and dredged the rivers, offered the lei sacrifice to the Supreme Lord and pure sacrifices to the honored powers, spread instruction and clarified punishments, regulated rites and harmonized music, and rejected slanderous speech and ruinous conduct [?]. Can we not see in these acts the utmost rectitude of their hearts? They consulted the multitude and set aside their own views, delighted in asking questions and examining matters, and applied the mean in governing the people. Can we not see in these acts the utmost openness of their hearts? Reverent, enlightened, profound, and wise, they opened their gates and made their sight keen and their hearing receptive. Can we not see in these acts the utmost illumination of their hearts? Their virtue spread widely, reaching beyond the four boundaries; their government fulfilled their wishes, moving all four quarters. Can we not see in this the utmost spiritual efficacy of their hearts? Their benevolence was like Heaven, and their virtue cherished life. From harmony among the nine degrees of kinship they extended concord to the myriad states; from bringing the Sanmiao to submission they brought all above and below, the plants and trees, birds and beasts, into accord. Lofty and boundless were their achievements, yet they regarded them as floating clouds. Can we not see in this the utmost greatness of their hearts? Yet although these things allow us to see their hearts, they are not where their hearts reside. If we suppose their hearts reside in the Canons and Counsels, where were they when Yao and Shun were alive? If we suppose they reside in Yao and Shun, where, then, were they after Yao and Shun had died? For their hearts take the Way as their substance, deriving it from the inherent nature of Heaven and Earth and flowing through Heaven …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
地古今者也是故堯舜在則存其至公至正至
虛至明至神至大者以運天下之治而爲唐爲
虞堯舜殁則其至公至正至虛至明至神至大
者常在天地間有能繼之者可以爲萬世之唐
虞而無能繼者亦不絶於世之非唐非虞何者
以道爲體者也道無所謂息也心亦無所謂息
也論道統者有自源而達流謂堯舜以是傳之
禹湯文武周公孔子孟子者矣所傳者何傳此
心也又有遡流而窮源謂孟子孔子周公文武
===
禹湯得統於堯舜者矣所得者何得此心也夫
曠世而前可以傳後可以得是堯舜之心流行
於天地古今寓於禹湯文武周公孔孟之間而
亦不盡於禹湯文武周公孔孟之間是故自禹
得之以治夏謂禹之心爲禹之心可也謂禹之
心爲堯舜之心亦可也堯舜之心不在於夏乎
自湯得之以治殷謂湯之心爲湯之心可也謂
湯之心爲堯舜之心亦可也堯舜之心不在於
殷乎自文武周公得之以治周謂文武周公之
punctuated: 地古今者也。是故堯舜在，則存其至公至正至虛至明至神至大者，以運天下之治，而爲唐爲虞；堯舜殁，則其至公至正至虛至明至神至大者常在天地間。有能繼之者，可以爲萬世之唐虞；而無能繼者，亦不絶於世之非唐非虞。何者？以道爲體者也。道無所謂息也，心亦無所謂息也。論道統者，有自源而達流，謂堯舜以是傳之禹湯文武周公孔子孟子者矣。所傳者何？傳此心也。又有遡流而窮源，謂孟子孔子周公文武禹湯得統於堯舜者矣。所得者何？得此心也。夫曠世而前可以傳，後可以得，是堯舜之心流行於天地古今，寓於禹湯文武周公孔孟之間，而亦不盡於禹湯文武周公孔孟之間。是故自禹得之以治夏，謂禹之心爲禹之心可也，謂禹之心爲堯舜之心亦可也。堯舜之心不在於夏乎？自湯得之以治殷，謂湯之心爲湯之心可也，謂湯之心爲堯舜之心亦可也。堯舜之心不在於殷乎？自文武周公得之以治周，謂文武周公之
translation_en:
…earth, throughout past and present. Thus, while Yao and Shun lived, they preserved that which was supremely impartial, upright, empty, luminous, numinous, and great, using it to bring order to all under Heaven and establish the rule of Tang and Yu. After Yao and Shun died, that which was supremely impartial, upright, empty, luminous, numinous, and great remained ever present between Heaven and earth. If anyone could carry it forward, they could bring about the rule of Tang and Yu for ten thousand generations. Even if none could carry it forward, it would not cease to exist in an age unlike Tang or Yu. Why? Because it takes the Way as its substance. The Way cannot be said to cease; neither can this mind.

Among those who discuss the succession of the Way, some proceed from the source downstream, saying that Yao and Shun transmitted this to Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, Kongzi, and Mengzi. What did they transmit? They transmitted this mind. Others trace the stream back to its source, saying that Mengzi, Kongzi, the Duke of Zhou, Wen, Wu, Yu, and Tang received their succession from Yao and Shun. What did they receive? They received this mind. Across widely separated ages, those who came before could transmit it, and those who came after could receive it. Thus the mind of Yao and Shun flows throughout Heaven and earth, past and present. It finds a dwelling in Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, Kongzi, and Mengzi, yet is not exhausted by them.

Thus, when Yu received it and used it to govern Xia, one could call Yu’s mind his own mind, and one could equally call Yu’s mind the mind of Yao and Shun. Was not the mind of Yao and Shun present in Xia? When Tang received it and used it to govern Yin, one could call Tang’s mind his own mind, and one could equally call Tang’s mind the mind of Yao and Shun. Was not the mind of Yao and Shun present in Yin? When Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou received it and used it to govern Zhou, to speak of the mind of Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
心爲文武周公之心可也謂文武周公之心爲
堯舜之心亦可也堯舜之心不在於周乎自孔
孟得之以教於春秋戰國謂孔孟之心爲孔孟
之心可也謂孔孟之心爲堯舜之心亦可也堯
舜之心不在於春秋戰國乎而何間於漢耶唐
耶宋耶是故東海有聖人出焉此心同也西海
南海北海有聖人出焉此心同也前乎千萬世
之既往後乎千萬世之方來有聖人出焉此心
同也何者千聖一心也千聖一心者何萬古一
===
道也萬古一道者何道之大原出於天天一而
已矣而道有二乎哉道一而已矣而心有二乎
哉道在天下萬世故堯舜之心亦常在天下萬
世也此豈依形而立者耶待生而存者耶若夫
桀紂之心與物相刃相靡即其生之日而心已
亡矣矧既歿之後而可以語存乎是心也堯舜
與桀紂與衆人同具者也但堯舜得之而爲堯
舜桀紂喪之而爲桀紂衆人失之而爲衆人耳
禹稱堯舜之民皆以堯舜之心爲心夫民何以
punctuated: 心爲文武周公之心可也，謂文武周公之心爲堯舜之心亦可也，堯舜之心不在於周乎？自孔孟得之以教於春秋戰國，謂孔孟之心爲孔孟之心可也，謂孔孟之心爲堯舜之心亦可也，堯舜之心不在於春秋戰國乎？而何間於漢耶、唐耶、宋耶？是故東海有聖人出焉，此心同也；西海南海北海有聖人出焉，此心同也；前乎千萬世之既往，後乎千萬世之方來，有聖人出焉，此心同也。何者？千聖一心也。千聖一心者何？萬古一道也。萬古一道者何？道之大原出於天，天一而已矣，而道有二乎哉？道一而已矣，而心有二乎哉？道在天下萬世，故堯舜之心亦常在天下萬世也。此豈依形而立者耶？待生而存者耶？若夫桀紂之心，與物相刃相靡，即其生之日而心已亡矣，矧既歿之後而可以語存乎？是心也，堯舜與桀紂與衆人同具者也。但堯舜得之而爲堯舜，桀紂喪之而爲桀紂，衆人失之而爲衆人耳。禹稱堯舜之民皆以堯舜之心爲心。夫民何以
translation_en: …heart as the heart of Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou is acceptable; to call the heart of Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou the heart of Yao and Shun is also acceptable. Was not the heart of Yao and Shun present in the Zhou? When Kongzi and Mengzi obtained it and taught in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, to call their heart the heart of Kongzi and Mengzi is acceptable; to call their heart the heart of Yao and Shun is also acceptable. Was not the heart of Yao and Shun present in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods? What distinction, then, could there be in the Han, Tang, or Song? Thus, if a sage arises by the eastern sea, this heart is the same; if sages arise by the western, southern, or northern seas, this heart is the same. If sages arise in the countless generations already past or the countless generations yet to come, this heart is the same. Why? A thousand sages share one heart. Why do a thousand sages share one heart? Throughout all ages there is one Way. Why is there one Way throughout all ages? The great source of the Way comes from Heaven. Heaven is one: could there be two Ways? The Way is one: could there be two hearts? The Way exists throughout the world and through all generations; hence the heart of Yao and Shun likewise always exists throughout the world and through all generations. Could it depend upon bodily form to be established, or upon life to exist? As for the hearts of Jie and Zhou, clashing with things and wearing themselves away, their hearts were already lost while they lived. How much less could one speak of their continued existence after death? This heart is something Yao and Shun, Jie and Zhou, and ordinary people all alike possess. Yet Yao and Shun attained it and thereby became Yao and Shun; Jie and Zhou forfeited it and thereby became Jie and Zhou; ordinary people lost it and thereby became ordinary people. Yu said that the people of Yao and Shun all took the heart of Yao and Shun as their own heart. Now, how could the people…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
能心堯舜之心也以其所具者同也同具而不
能自盡得堯舜於變而其本體可槩見也此可
見堯舜之心在當時卽無所不在也何獨至後
世而疑之民且能以其心爲心也而況遠過於
民者乎而後世卒鮮能爲堯舜者皆失其同具
之眞心也眞心之失機心害之也故曰機心存
則純白不備純白不備則神生不定神生不定
者道之所不載也堯舜之心則純白備者也純
白備故其神定也神定故其道載也道載故其
存久也蓋堯舜爲天地所立之心以道爲體而
流行於天下後世天下後世有能存堯舜以道
爲體之心卽可以其心繼堯舜而復爲天地立
心是故其心能無一毫之私焉則堯舜之心之
公者在我也能無一毫之邪焉則堯舜之心之
正者在我也能無一毫之壅蔽滯椹焉則堯舜
之心之虛之明之神之大者在我也而純白備
矣純白備而神定而道載矣道體所在原無所
爲異也又安得不同也以道體而存之爲堯舜
punctuated: 能心堯舜之心也？以其所具者同也。同具而不能自盡，得堯舜於變，而其本體可槩見也。此可見堯舜之心在當時卽無所不在也，何獨至後世而疑之？民且能以其心爲心也，而況遠過於民者乎？而後世卒鮮能爲堯舜者，皆失其同具之眞心也。眞心之失，機心害之也。故曰：「機心存則純白不備，純白不備則神生不定，神生不定者，道之所不載也。」堯舜之心則純白備者也。純白備，故其神定也；神定，故其道載也；道載，故其存久也。蓋堯舜爲天地所立之心，以道爲體，而流行於天下後世。天下後世有能存堯舜以道爲體之心，卽可以其心繼堯舜，而復爲天地立心。是故其心能無一毫之私焉，則堯舜之心之公者在我也；能無一毫之邪焉，則堯舜之心之正者在我也；能無一毫之壅蔽滯椹焉，則堯舜之心之虛之明之神之大者在我也，而純白備矣。純白備而神定，而道載矣。道體所在，原無所爲異也，又安得不同也？以道體而存之，爲堯舜
translation_en: …be able to make the heart of Yao and Shun their own? Because what they inherently possess is the same. Though they possess it in common, they cannot fully realize it on their own; through the transforming influence of Yao and Shun, its fundamental substance becomes broadly apparent. From this we can see that the heart of Yao and Shun was already present everywhere in their own time. Why doubt its presence only when we come to later ages? Even the common people could make that heart their own; how much more could those who far surpass the common people! Yet in later ages, few ultimately succeeded in becoming like Yao and Shun, because they had all lost the true heart they possessed in common. The loss of the true heart comes from the harm inflicted by the calculating heart. Thus it is said: “When a calculating heart exists, pristine purity is incomplete. When pristine purity is incomplete, the life of the spirit is unsettled. Those whose spiritual life is unsettled are not sustained by the Way.” The heart of Yao and Shun possesses pristine purity in full. Because that purity is complete, their spirit is settled; because their spirit is settled, the Way sustains them; because the Way sustains them, their heart endures. The heart that Yao and Shun established for Heaven and Earth takes the Way as its substance and flows throughout the world and into later ages. Anyone in the world in later ages who can preserve this heart of Yao and Shun, whose substance is the Way, can thereby succeed Yao and Shun with their own heart and once again establish a heart for Heaven and Earth. Thus, if my heart can be free of the slightest selfishness, the impartiality of Yao and Shun’s heart is present in me. If it can be free of the slightest perversity, the uprightness of their heart is present in me. If it can be free of the slightest obstruction, obscurity, or impediment [?], the openness, clarity, spiritual efficacy, and greatness of their heart are present in me, and pristine purity is complete. When pristine purity is complete, the spirit is settled and the Way sustains it. Wherever the substance of the Way resides, there is fundamentally no difference; how, then, could it fail to be the same? Preserving it through the substance of the Way makes it the heart of Yao and Shun…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之心以堯舜之心而措之爲堯舜之治由是出
其心之公則舉罔弗當罪罔弗服矣出其心之
正則執度典章靡弗齊一而百工允釐庶績其
凝矣出其心之虛則納天下之善以爲善而善
與人同矣出其心之明則不必徧物而百志惟
熈矣出其心之神則廣運之德從欲之治無遠
弗屆矣出其心之大則彌綸造化博濟羣生而
有天下而不與矣而唐虞不再見於今日乎至
是則不惟堯舜之心在雖謂堯舜至今存可也
===
雖然先堯舜而聖者有矣後堯舜而聖者亦有
矣而何獨堯舜之心至今在乎心學之源自堯
舜啓也堯之告舜曰允執厥中舜之告禹曰人
心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中是萬世
心學之源也堯舜開萬世心學之源故堯舜之
心在萬世尤章章著也况羣聖之心即堯舜之
心舉堯舜而羣聖在其中矣然則吾人求見堯
舜之心於何處見之曰舜嘗見堯於羹墻矣夫
羹墻安得有堯也是舜之心有堯耳舜之心有
punctuated:
之心，以堯舜之心而措之，爲堯舜之治。由是出其心之公，則舉罔弗當，罪罔弗服矣；出其心之正，則執度典章靡弗齊一，而百工允釐，庶績其凝矣；出其心之虛，則納天下之善以爲善，而善與人同矣；出其心之明，則不必徧物，而百志惟熈矣；出其心之神，則廣運之德、從欲之治，無遠弗屆矣；出其心之大，則彌綸造化，博濟羣生，而有天下而不與矣。而唐虞不再見於今日乎？至是，則不惟堯舜之心在，雖謂堯舜至今存，可也。
雖然，先堯舜而聖者有矣，後堯舜而聖者亦有矣，而何獨堯舜之心至今在乎？心學之源，自堯舜啓也。堯之告舜曰：「允執厥中。」舜之告禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」是萬世心學之源也。堯舜開萬世心學之源，故堯舜之心在萬世，尤章章著也。况羣聖之心，即堯舜之心，舉堯舜而羣聖在其中矣。然則吾人求見堯舜之心，於何處見之？曰：「舜嘗見堯於羹墻矣。」夫羹墻安得有堯也？是舜之心有堯耳。舜之心有
translation_en:
…the heart of Yao and Shun; putting the heart of Yao and Shun into practice produces the government of Yao and Shun. Thus, when its impartiality is expressed, no appointment is inappropriate, and no punishment fails to win acceptance. When its rectitude is expressed, the observance of measures and statutes is entirely consistent, all officials duly perform their duties, and every undertaking achieves completion. When its openness is expressed, it takes the goodness of all under Heaven as its own and shares goodness with others. When its illumination is expressed, there is no need to examine every matter, yet the manifold purposes all flourish. When its spiritual efficacy is expressed, its far-reaching virtue and its government, which accords with its wishes, reach even the remotest places. When its greatness is expressed, it embraces the workings of creation and extends aid broadly to all living beings; it possesses all under Heaven yet remains uninvolved. Would not the age of Tang and Yu—Yao and Shun—appear again today? At this point, not only would the heart of Yao and Shun remain: one could even say that Yao and Shun themselves still live today.
Even so, there were sages before Yao and Shun, and there were sages after them. Why, then, speak only of the heart of Yao and Shun as remaining to this day? Because the learning of the heart originated with Yao and Shun. Yao told Shun: “Sincerely hold fast to the mean.” Shun told Yu: “The human heart is precarious; the heart of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.” This is the source of the learning of the heart for all ages. Because Yao and Shun opened this source for all ages, the enduring presence of their heart through all ages is particularly manifest. Moreover, the heart of all the sages is precisely the heart of Yao and Shun: in naming Yao and Shun, one includes all the sages. Where, then, should we look if we seek to behold the heart of Yao and Shun? The answer is: “Shun once saw Yao in his broth and upon the wall.” How could Yao have been in the broth or on the wall? It was simply that Yao was present in Shun’s heart. In Shun’s heart there was…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
堯故食則見堯於羹坐則見堯於墻豈惟羹墻
將無往而非堯之所在亦無在而非舜之所見
矣卽舜之見堯而後舜者之見堯與舜不可知
耶故爲之說曰堯舜之心至今在何在曰在天
地間天地之間何在曰在吾人之心有精一之
學則其心可見無精一之學則其心不可見程
子涵養須用敬進學在致知得精一之傳者也
其爲此言非空言也誠有見於堯舜之心今眞
在也顧窮而在下者得堯舜之心而惟其道明
===
必達而在上者得堯舜之心而後其道行有天
下者其念之哉
表
擬唐幸國子監觀釋奠命祭酒孔頴達講
孝經廷臣賀表〔貞觀十四年〕
陸檄
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔粹而融麗而則大雅〕
〔之音也宜錄以式多士〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔場中作者頗多浮泛〕
punctuated:
堯，故食則見堯於羹，坐則見堯於墻。豈惟羹墻？將無往而非堯之所在，亦無在而非舜之所見矣。卽舜之見堯，而後舜者之見堯與舜，不可知耶？故爲之說曰：「堯舜之心至今在。」何在？曰：「在天地間。」天地之間何在？曰：「在吾人之心。」有精一之學，則其心可見；無精一之學，則其心不可見。程子「涵養須用敬，進學在致知」，得精一之傳者也。其爲此言，非空言也，誠有見於堯舜之心今眞在也。顧窮而在下者得堯舜之心，而惟其道明；必達而在上者得堯舜之心，而後其道行。有天下者，其念之哉！

表
擬唐幸國子監觀釋奠，命祭酒孔頴達講《孝經》，廷臣賀表〔貞觀十四年〕
陸檄

同考試官教諭蔡，批〔粹而融，麗而則，大雅〕〔之音也。宜錄以式多士。〕

同考試官教諭張，批〔場中作者頗多浮泛，〕
translation_en:
…Yao in his heart; thus, when eating, he saw Yao in his broth, and when seated, he saw Yao upon the wall. Yet why only in broth and walls? Wherever he went, Yao would be present, and wherever he was, Shun would see him. From Shun’s seeing Yao, can we not understand how those who came after Shun might see both Yao and Shun? Hence the saying: “The heart of Yao and Shun remains to this day.” Where does it remain? “Between Heaven and Earth.” Where between Heaven and Earth? “In our own hearts.” Through the learning of refinement and single-mindedness, their heart can be seen; without this learning, it cannot be seen. Master Cheng said, “In nurturing oneself, one must employ reverent attentiveness; advancing in learning lies in extending knowledge.” He had received the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness. These were no empty words: he truly perceived that the heart of Yao and Shun remains present even now. Yet when those in obscurity and lowly stations attain the heart of Yao and Shun, their Way is merely made clear; only when those who have risen to high stations attain it can their Way be put into practice. Let those who possess All-under-Heaven ponder this!

Memorial
