Be strict in rejecting the unworthy, without allowing them to remain through indulgence: then the purpose of the methods of banishment and confinement beyond the city [?] can be achieved without restoring those methods. When the rhythmic movements of paired swords are prized, a fashion for flying-white calligraphy develops [?]; when guests bearing zithers are honored, the accompanying harmonies that follow their tunes…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
作由是黌序之間積之數年當必多業成
通經之士應蒸髦之選屢持正秉義之操
預充庭之貢者矣而成均之間又從而甄
別之至於
廟堂之上舉措之際尤加意焉使卓然經明
行修之士參錯立
朝而不然者無得溷廁於其間則李復所謂
取士之法劉光祖所謂封殖人才之策畢
舉矣其倡愈大其化愈遠不庶幾乎道德
===
一風俗同布之庶位緩急有賴邁漢匹周
而無愧於前修矣乎或曰士亦貴自養也
獨上之倡也乎哉曰成周尚德教士無不
趨德教矣西漢尚經術士無不趨經術矣
東漢尚節義士無不趨節義矣此前事之
已效者也且中才之士未可一朝而遽化
爲君子也乃其心猶趨進之心也彼見傅
綜者進而淺陋者退也即反其所爲淺陋
者而務傅綜其傅綜也又待於責乎乃其
punctuated:
作。由是黌序之間，積之數年，當必多業成通經之士應蒸髦之選，屢持正秉義之操預充庭之貢者矣。而成均之間，又從而甄別之。至於廟堂之上、舉措之際，尤加意焉，使卓然經明行修之士參錯立朝，而不然者無得溷廁於其間，則李復所謂取士之法、劉光祖所謂封殖人才之策畢舉矣。其倡愈大，其化愈遠，不庶幾乎道德一、風俗同，布之庶位，緩急有賴，邁漢匹周，而無愧於前修矣乎？
或曰：「士亦貴自養也，獨上之倡也乎哉？」曰：「成周尚德教，士無不趨德教矣；西漢尚經術，士無不趨經術矣；東漢尚節義，士無不趨節義矣。此前事之已效者也。且中才之士，未可一朝而遽化爲君子也，乃其心猶趨進之心也。彼見傅綜者進而淺陋者退也，即反其所爲淺陋者而務傅綜，其傅綜也，又待於責乎？乃其
translation_en:
…arise. Thus, after several years of sustained effort in the schools, there will surely be many scholars whose studies are accomplished and who comprehend the Classics, answering the call to select outstanding talent; time and again, those who uphold rectitude and righteousness will be included among the candidates presented at court. The Imperial University will then further distinguish among them. At the highest levels of government, particular care must be taken in appointments and dismissals, so that men outstanding in their understanding of the Classics and cultivation of conduct stand together at court, while those who lack these qualities cannot slip into their company. Then what Li Fu called the method of selecting scholars, and what Liu Guangzu called the policy of nurturing talent, will both be fully implemented. The stronger the encouragement, the farther its transforming influence will reach. Might we not then approach unity in morality and uniformity in customs, placing such men in the various offices, dependable in ordinary times and emergencies alike, surpassing the Han and matching the Zhou, without falling short of the worthies of old?
Someone asks: “For scholars, self-cultivation is also important. Can it depend solely on encouragement from above?” I reply: “When the Zhou esteemed moral instruction, every scholar pursued moral instruction. When the Western Han esteemed classical learning, every scholar pursued classical learning. When the Eastern Han esteemed integrity and righteousness, every scholar pursued integrity and righteousness. These are precedents whose efficacy has already been demonstrated. Moreover, scholars of middling ability cannot suddenly be transformed into gentlemen in a single morning. Yet their hearts still seek advancement. When they see those of comprehensive learning [?] promoted and the shallow and ignorant rejected, they turn away from their own shallowness and ignorance and strive for comprehensive learning [?]. Must their pursuit of such learning still await demands from above? Moreover, their…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
心猶慕名之心也彼見耿介者榮而萎靡
者辱也則毀其所爲萎靡者而務耿介其
耿介也又俟於勸乎夫上智不待倡而養
中人可以善可以不善而必待於倡倡則
養不倡則不養故愚生主於倡之說竊有
見於風草之喻盂水之譬舜與湯舉皐陶
伊尹以遠天下之不仁其道蓋如此也
第四問
陳有則
===
同考試官教諭葉 批〔明體適用之學場中類能言之獨此作衍繹詳明議論正大而歸諸〕〔實德實行蓋知務學之要者是可以薦矣〕
考試官侍讀陶 批〔古人進德修業皆有實用其力處子能懇懇言之似非空言相眩者錄之〕
考試官洗馬馬 批〔學問本體用一源子能據古人之德業究析明盡可以占所養矣〕
君子之學所以成已也而成物者已具君
子之用所以成物也而成已者始全啟知
punctuated:
心猶慕名之心也。彼見耿介者榮而萎靡者辱也，則毀其所爲萎靡者而務耿介，其耿介也又俟於勸乎？夫上智不待倡而養，中人可以善，可以不善，而必待於倡。倡則養，不倡則不養。故愚生主於倡之說，竊有見於風草之喻、盂水之譬。舜與湯舉皐陶、伊尹，以遠天下之不仁，其道蓋如此也。

第四問
陳有則

同考試官教諭葉批〔明體適用之學，場中類能言之。獨此作衍繹詳明，議論正大，而歸諸〕〔實德實行，蓋知務學之要者，是可以薦矣。〕
考試官侍讀陶批〔古人進德修業，皆有實用其力處。子能懇懇言之，似非空言相眩者，錄之。〕
考試官洗馬馬批〔學問本體用一源，子能據古人之德業，究析明盡，可以占所養矣。〕

君子之學，所以成已也，而成物者已具；君子之用，所以成物也，而成已者始全。啟知
translation_en:
…their hearts still yearn for distinction. When they see the upright honored and the dispirited disgraced, they cast off their dispirited ways and strive for uprightness. Must their uprightness then await further encouragement? Those of the highest wisdom cultivate themselves without awaiting encouragement from above. People of middling capacity, however, may become good or may fail to become good, and necessarily depend upon such encouragement. With encouragement they cultivate themselves; without it they do not. Thus, in advocating encouragement from above, I, an unworthy student, have drawn insight from the analogy of wind and grass and the comparison with water in a basin. Shun and Tang promoted Gao Yao and Yi Yin, thereby keeping the inhumane far away throughout the realm. Their method was surely like this.

Fourth Question
Chen Youze

Comment by Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor: 〔Most candidates in the examination can discuss learning that comprehends fundamental principles and applies them appropriately. This composition alone develops the subject fully and clearly, offers upright and substantial arguments, and brings everything back to〕〔actual virtue and actual conduct. Its author evidently understands the essentials of pursuing learning and may therefore be recommended.〕

Comment by Examiner Tao, Reader-in-waiting: 〔In advancing their virtue and cultivating their undertakings, the ancients all had concrete matters to which they devoted their efforts. You discuss these with earnest conviction and seem not to be one who dazzles others with empty words. Accept this composition.〕

Comment by Examiner Ma, Librarian to the Heir Apparent: 〔In learning, substance and function fundamentally share a single source. Drawing upon the virtue and achievements of the ancients, you investigate and analyze them clearly and thoroughly. From this we can discern the cultivation you have attained.〕

The gentleman’s learning is the means by which he perfects himself, yet within it the means of perfecting others are already present. The gentleman’s practical activity is the means by which he perfects others, yet only through it does his self-perfection become complete. To open understanding [?] …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
所以學而用在是矣知所以用而學在是
矣然非實德是務則何以盡成已之功而
非實行是勵又何以基及物之化哉則古
人之學與用當必有要而不可以泛求矣
執事以古人學術事功為問且以諭諸士
所實用其力者愚生何足以語此哉然竊
有聞焉而未能也敢無辭以復今夫天之
生人也賦之形賦之性矣則踐形盡性固
吾分也而凡同有是形同有是性者皆吾
===
同胞而不可恝然視也是故大學語明德
必繼之新民而釋新民必本之明德無二
道也易大傳曰精義入神以致用也利用
安身以崇德也又曰藏器于身待時而動
非謂是耶柰之何此義之不明也於是有
果於獨善而忘世者焉彼其孤蹤長往獨
行高蹈將自謂於俗無累也而一體者乖
矣則成已之分固未盡也於是有期於彝
善而忘已者焉彼其乘時遘會趨事赴功
punctuated:
所以學，而用在是矣；知所以用，而學在是矣。然非實德是務，則何以盡成已之功？而非實行是勵，又何以基及物之化哉？則古人之學與用，當必有要，而不可以泛求矣。
執事以古人學術事功為問，且以諭諸士所實用其力者，愚生何足以語此哉？然竊有聞焉而未能也，敢無辭以復？今夫天之生人也，賦之形，賦之性矣，則踐形盡性，固吾分也。而凡同有是形、同有是性者，皆吾同胞，而不可恝然視也。是故《大學》語明德，必繼之新民；而釋新民，必本之明德，無二道也。《易大傳》曰：「精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。」又曰：「藏器于身，待時而動。」非謂是耶？柰之何此義之不明也？於是有果於獨善而忘世者焉。彼其孤蹤長往，獨行高蹈，將自謂於俗無累也，而一體者乖矣，則成已之分固未盡也。於是有期於彝善而忘已者焉。彼其乘時遘會，趨事赴功，
translation_en:
…how to learn, and practical application lies therein; know how to put learning into practice, and learning lies therein. Yet unless one devotes oneself to genuine virtue, how can one fully accomplish the perfection of oneself? And unless one strives to act in earnest, how can one lay the foundation for a transforming influence extending to others? The learning and practical application of the ancients must therefore have had an essential principle, which cannot be sought indiscriminately.
Your Honor asks about the ancients’ learning and achievements in affairs, and further instructs the candidates concerning where they actually applied their efforts. How could an ignorant student such as I be qualified to speak of this? Nevertheless, I have heard something of it, though I have not yet been able to put it into practice. Dare I fail to offer a response? When Heaven brings human beings into existence, it endows them with bodily form and moral nature. To fulfill that form and fully realize that nature is assuredly our duty. All who share this form and this nature are our siblings, and we cannot regard them with indifference. Thus, when the Great Learning speaks of illuminating virtue, it invariably follows this with renewing the people; and when it explains renewing the people, it invariably grounds this in illuminating virtue. These are not two separate Ways. The Great Commentary on the Changes says: “Refining one’s understanding of what is right until one penetrates the numinous serves to bring it into practical application; making application beneficial and securing oneself serves to exalt virtue.” It also says: “Store one’s capacities within oneself, and await the proper time to act.” Does this not express precisely this point? How is it, then, that this principle remains obscure? Consequently, there are those who resolutely pursue their own moral perfection and forget the world. They withdraw far away in solitude, following a lofty path alone, imagining themselves unburdened by worldly ties. Yet they have broken their unity with others, and thus have not fully discharged even their duty to perfect themselves. Then there are those who aspire to constant goodness [?] and forget themselves. Seizing the moment and encountering favorable opportunities, they hasten to undertake affairs and pursue achievements…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
將自謂於世有補也而立本者鮮矣則成
物之用又曷施耶周子蓋憂之故示人曰
志伊尹之所志學顏子之所學夫伊尹之
志紀於書傳人能言之矣堯舜其君堯舜
其民也一夫不獲引以爲辜也先知覺後
知先覺覺後覺也斯其志誠偉矣然非徒
任以天下而不先其本也蓋元聖之德既
著矣不然耕野之夫成湯何遽加以三聘
之禮哉觀其自重以堯舜之道其學不可
===
知耶顏子之學稱於孔子人能言之矣怒
則不遷過則不貳也三月不違仁也屢空
而不憂簞瓢而能樂也其學誠純矣然非
徒自善其身而無與於世也蓋王佐之才
既具矣不然爲邦之問夫子何遽語以四
代禮樂哉觀夫孟子擬諸禹稷之事其用
又不可知耶蓋考伊尹之未聘其所自樂
即顏子之樂使顏子而遇即伊尹矣故黃
直卿氏曰聖賢無一偏之學顏子是明德
punctuated: 將自謂於世有補也，而立本者鮮矣，則成物之用又曷施耶？周子蓋憂之，故示人曰：「志伊尹之所志，學顏子之所學。」夫伊尹之志，紀於書傳，人能言之矣：堯舜其君，堯舜其民也；一夫不獲，引以爲辜也；先知覺後知，先覺覺後覺也。斯其志誠偉矣，然非徒任以天下而不先其本也。蓋元聖之德既著矣，不然，耕野之夫，成湯何遽加以三聘之禮哉？觀其自重以堯舜之道，其學不可知耶？顏子之學，稱於孔子，人能言之矣：怒則不遷，過則不貳也；三月不違仁也；屢空而不憂，簞瓢而能樂也。其學誠純矣，然非徒自善其身而無與於世也。蓋王佐之才既具矣，不然，爲邦之問，夫子何遽語以四代禮樂哉？觀夫孟子擬諸禹稷之事，其用又不可知耶？蓋考伊尹之未聘，其所自樂，即顏子之樂；使顏子而遇，即伊尹矣。故黃直卿氏曰：「聖賢無一偏之學，顏子是明德
translation_en:
…they will claim to have benefited the world, yet few establish the foundation. How, then, can their capacity to bring others to fulfillment be put into practice? Master Zhou was concerned about this and therefore instructed people: “Aspire to what Yi Yin aspired to; learn what Master Yan learned.” Yi Yin’s aspirations are recorded in the Documents and other transmitted writings, and people can recount them: to make his ruler a Yao or Shun and his people like the people of Yao and Shun; to regard any single person’s failure to find his proper place as his own fault; and, as one who knew and awakened first, to awaken those who would know and awaken later. His aspirations were indeed great. Yet he did not merely take responsibility for all under Heaven without first attending to the foundation. His virtue as the foremost sage was already manifest. Otherwise, why would Cheng Tang have accorded a man plowing in the fields the ceremonial honor of three invitations to serve? When we observe how he valued himself through the Way of Yao and Shun, can we not understand his learning?

Master Yan’s learning was praised by Confucius, and people can recount it: he did not transfer his anger to others or repeat a fault; for three months he did not depart from benevolence; though frequently destitute, he was untroubled, and with only a basket of food and a gourd of drink he could remain joyful. His learning was indeed pure. Yet he did not merely perfect himself and take no part in the world. He already possessed the talent to assist a true king. Otherwise, when he asked about governing a state, why would the Master have immediately told him about the rites and music of the four dynasties? When we observe how Mengzi compared him with Yu and Ji in their undertakings, can we not also understand how his abilities could be put to use? If we examine Yi Yin before he was invited to serve, what he delighted in was precisely what Master Yan delighted in. Had Master Yan met with the opportunity, he would have been another Yi Yin. Thus Huang Zhiqing said: “The sages and worthies had no one-sided learning. Master Yan represents manifesting luminous virtue…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
伊尹是新民言之若岐而其道曷常不一
也於乎幡然一出而造有商表正之業不
違如愚而三千之徒莫得擬焉伊之志顏
之學可多見耶後世有志於事功者以天
下爲巳任日夜興致太平則有若范文正
仲淹再決大策以安社稷則有若韓忠獻
琦萬口一詞稱爲賢相則有若富文忠弼
田夫野老皆知姓氏則有若司馬文正光
之數君子者固不得上擬伊尹然志存社
===
稷身係重輕植偉節於當時流芳聞於後
世伊尹而下此非其卓犖者乎有潛心理
學者會道有元上接洙泗則有若周元公
敦頤闡道甚早明物察倫則有若程明道
顥學本至誠動不爲矯則有若程伊川頤
窮神知化精思力踐則有若張橫渠載窮
理以致知反躬以踐實則有若朱文公熹
之數君子者雖未必盡如顏子然窮極藴
奥闡發性靈明聖學於將湮綿道脉於不
punctuated:
伊尹是新民。言之若岐，而其道曷常不一也？於乎！幡然一出，而造有商表正之業；不違如愚，而三千之徒莫得擬焉。伊之志、顏之學，可多見耶？後世有志於事功者，以天下爲巳任，日夜興致太平，則有若范文正仲淹；再決大策，以安社稷，則有若韓忠獻琦；萬口一詞，稱爲賢相，則有若富文忠弼；田夫野老皆知姓氏，則有若司馬文正光。之數君子者，固不得上擬伊尹，然志存社稷，身係重輕，植偉節於當時，流芳聞於後世。伊尹而下，此非其卓犖者乎？
有潛心理學者，會道有元，上接洙泗，則有若周元公敦頤；闡道甚早，明物察倫，則有若程明道顥；學本至誠，動不爲矯，則有若程伊川頤；窮神知化，精思力踐，則有若張橫渠載；窮理以致知，反躬以踐實，則有若朱文公熹。之數君子者，雖未必盡如顏子，然窮極藴奥，闡發性靈，明聖學於將湮，綿道脉於不
translation_en:
…Yi Yin represents renewing the people. Though these descriptions seem divergent, when were their ways ever anything but one? Ah! Resolutely coming forth to serve, one established for the Shang the achievement of setting others right by example; offering no dissent and seeming foolish, the other had no equal among the three thousand disciples. Can such resolve as Yi Yin’s and such learning as Master Yan’s often be found?
Among those in later ages intent upon practical achievement, Fan Zhongyan, posthumously titled Wenzheng, took responsibility for all under Heaven and worked day and night to bring about great peace. Han Qi, posthumously titled Zhongxian, twice settled great questions of state policy to secure the altars of soil and grain. Fu Bi, posthumously titled Wenzhong, was acclaimed with one voice by everyone as a worthy chief councilor. Sima Guang, posthumously titled Wenzheng, was known by name even to farmers and village elders. These gentlemen certainly cannot be ranked alongside Yi Yin. Yet their ambitions centered on the state, and its fortunes depended upon them; they established examples of magnificent integrity in their own time and left an honored reputation to posterity. Among those who followed Yi Yin, were these not outstanding figures?
Among those who devoted themselves to the Learning of Principle, Zhou Dunyi, honored as Duke Yuan, comprehended the Way at its source [?] and reached back to the tradition of the Zhu and Si rivers. Cheng Hao, known as Mingdao, elucidated the Way very early, understanding things and discerning human relationships. Cheng Yi, known as Yichuan, grounded his learning in utmost sincerity, acting without affectation. Zhang Zai, known as Hengqu, fathomed the spiritual and understood transformation, reflecting deeply and practicing diligently. Zhu Xi, honored as Duke Wen, investigated principle to extend knowledge and examined himself to put it into practice. Though these gentlemen may not have equaled Master Yan in every respect, they fully explored the deepest mysteries, elucidated human nature and its spiritual capacities, illuminated the learning of the sages when it was about to fall into oblivion, and sustained the transmission of the Way so that it would not …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
絶顏子而下此非其流亞矣乎夫韓范諸
人樹立偉矣而不以理學稱者非無得於
學也蓋嘗考其素矣富貴貧賤處之若一
而毀譽忻戚不以動心者文正之所本也
事君盡力知無不爲而成敗利鈍一聽之
天者魏公之所本也惻怛至誠充溢內外
慷慨大節莫之屈撓非富公之所本乎自
少至老未嘗妄語平生所作咸可對人非
司馬公之所本乎則韓范諸公之所學可
知矣不然諸公之所值其足以動吾中而
===
移吾守者多矣豈能始終一節若此耶夫
周程諸儒造詣深矣而不以功業顯者非
不適於用也蓋嘗考其故矣淸獻之薦未
上而廬山之跡已虛濂溪之所遭也宗正
之召未行而士夫之望已缺明道之所遭
也伊川才堪大事指顧可集矣經幃憚其
方嚴而簾中慮其不靖將能行乎橫渠政
先善俗召對且用矣新政拒於求助而宿
punctuated:
絶。顏子而下，此非其流亞矣乎？夫韓范諸人樹立偉矣，而不以理學稱者，非無得於學也。蓋嘗考其素矣：富貴貧賤，處之若一，而毀譽忻戚不以動心者，文正之所本也；事君盡力，知無不爲，而成敗利鈍一聽之天者，魏公之所本也；惻怛至誠，充溢內外，慷慨大節，莫之屈撓，非富公之所本乎？自少至老，未嘗妄語，平生所作，咸可對人，非司馬公之所本乎？則韓范諸公之所學可知矣。不然，諸公之所值，其足以動吾中而移吾守者多矣，豈能始終一節若此耶？
夫周程諸儒造詣深矣，而不以功業顯者，非不適於用也。蓋嘗考其故矣：淸獻之薦未上，而廬山之跡已虛，濂溪之所遭也；宗正之召未行，而士夫之望已缺，明道之所遭也。伊川才堪大事，指顧可集矣，經幃憚其方嚴，而簾中慮其不靖，將能行乎？橫渠政先善俗，召對且用矣，新政拒於求助，而宿
translation_en:
…without interruption. Among those who came after Master Yan, were these not his peers and successors? The achievements of Han, Fan, and the others were great; that they were not renowned for their learning of principle does not mean that they gained nothing from learning. Let us examine their habitual conduct. To treat wealth and rank, poverty and low station alike, allowing neither praise nor blame, joy nor sorrow to stir the heart—this was the foundation of Fan Wenzheng’s conduct. To serve his ruler with all his strength, doing whatever he knew ought to be done, while leaving success or failure, favorable or adverse circumstances, entirely to Heaven—this was the foundation of the Duke of Wei’s conduct. Compassion and utmost sincerity filled his being and manifested themselves outwardly; in matters of high principle he was resolute and could neither be bent nor shaken—was this not the foundation of Lord Fu’s conduct? From youth to old age he never spoke falsely, and everything he did throughout his life could be openly acknowledged before others—was this not the foundation of Lord Sima’s conduct? Thus we can understand the learning of Han, Fan, and the other gentlemen. Otherwise, among the circumstances they encountered, many could have disturbed their inner resolve and altered their commitments. How could they have maintained such unwavering integrity from beginning to end?
The attainments of the Confucian scholars Zhou, Cheng, and the others were profound; that they were not distinguished by public achievements does not mean that their learning was unsuited to practical application. Let us examine the reasons. Before Qingxian’s recommendation had been submitted, his presence at Mount Lu was already gone: this was Lianxi’s fate. Before the summons to serve in the Court of the Imperial Clan could be acted upon, the hopes of the scholar-officials had already been dashed: this was Mingdao’s fate. Yichuan possessed the ability to undertake great affairs and could have accomplished them with a mere gesture. Yet those at the imperial lectures feared his upright severity, while the ruler behind the curtain worried that he would disturb the peace. How could he have put his learning into practice? In government, Hengqu gave priority to improving popular customs; he had been summoned for an audience and was about to be employed. Yet those promoting the new policies rejected him when seeking assistance, and the venerable…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
德疏於獻凶能無歸乎若夫筮仕歷五十
年而立朝僅四十日又文公所以終塞也
則周程諸儒之不究可知矣不然諸儒之
所具其足以濟斯世而澤斯民者豫矣豈
其施用弗究若此耶合而觀之可以見用
之必資於學學之必適於用矣夫用不可
必也學可自致也孟子論伊尹自萬鍾千
駟之辭受以至一介之取予非道義不苟
也然後其節完其心足以自信而天下事
===
惟其所任業之所由建也韓范諸公其卓
行固不可殫述蓋亦有去任貧至徒步行
已不受微塵者矣諸君子之砥厲若此又
非其植立之要乎夫工師之爲室也其制
不必同乃其址必固垣必堅則靡弗同也
不然雖崇構麗飾其傾也速矣夫君子之
業亦若是也人見夫弛弛之士或不羈而
致功名遂以爲細行不必拘也甚至目謹
恪爲苟曲謂不足以任事然則一介之愼
punctuated:
德疏於獻凶，能無歸乎？若夫筮仕歷五十年，而立朝僅四十日，又文公所以終塞也。則周程諸儒之不究可知矣。不然，諸儒之所具，其足以濟斯世而澤斯民者豫矣，豈其施用弗究若此耶？合而觀之，可以見用之必資於學，學之必適於用矣。
夫用不可必也，學可自致也。孟子論伊尹，自萬鍾千駟之辭受，以至一介之取予，非道義不苟也。然後其節完，其心足以自信，而天下事惟其所任，業之所由建也。韓范諸公，其卓行固不可殫述，蓋亦有去任貧至徒步，行已不受微塵者矣。諸君子之砥厲若此，又非其植立之要乎？
夫工師之爲室也，其制不必同，乃其址必固，垣必堅，則靡弗同也。不然，雖崇構麗飾，其傾也速矣。夫君子之業亦若是也。人見夫弛弛之士或不羈而致功名，遂以爲細行不必拘也，甚至目謹恪爲苟曲，謂不足以任事。然則一介之愼
translation_en:
…and senior men of virtue were estranged over the presentation of ill omens [?]; could he avoid returning home? As for having entered official service fifty years earlier, yet having served at court for only forty days, this, too, explains why Master Wengong (Zhu Xi) remained thwarted to the end. Thus we can understand why the Confucian scholars Zhou and the Cheng brothers never fully realized their aims. Otherwise, they already possessed all that was needed to aid their age and benefit its people: how could the exercise of their abilities have remained so unfulfilled? Considered together, these cases show that practical service must draw upon learning, and that learning must be suited to practical service.
Whether one is employed cannot be assured; learning, however, lies within one’s own power to attain. In discussing Yi Yin, Mencius describes how, from declining or accepting ten thousand measures of grain and a thousand teams of four horses, down to taking or giving the smallest thing, he never acted carelessly where the Way and righteousness were concerned. Only then was his integrity complete and his heart sufficiently assured of itself to undertake the affairs of the realm. This is how great achievements are established. The outstanding conduct of such men as Han and Fan certainly cannot be recounted exhaustively. Among them were those who, on leaving office, were so poor that they traveled on foot, and who in their conduct would not accept so much as a speck of dust. Was not such rigorous self-discipline also essential to establishing their moral foundations?
When a master builder constructs a house, its design need not be the same as others’, but its foundations must be firm and its walls strong: in these respects all houses must alike conform. Otherwise, however lofty the structure and splendid its ornament, it will soon collapse. The gentleman’s achievements are likewise. People see that lax and careless men [?] sometimes attain merit and fame despite their unrestrained conduct, and consequently suppose that one need not be scrupulous about minor matters of conduct. They even regard conscientious care as petty punctiliousness, saying that such men are unfit to undertake affairs. If so, then scrupulousness over even the smallest thing…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
非耶噫此業之所以鮮植也孔子語顔淵
以爲仁之要必克己復禮其目必非禮勿
視聽言動也然後其功密其力得有所施
而外誘不得以投其隙學之所由純也周
程諸儒其格言固不可殫述盖莫非嚴畏
以直其内省察以防其間者矣諸大儒之
精密若此又非其造詣之要乎夫農夫之
力田也其種不必同乃若耕必深耨必易
則靡弗同也不然雖沃壤奥區其獲也鮮
===
矣夫君子之學亦若是也人見夫才辯之
士或過高而似超脱遂以爲問學不必事
也甚至目防檢爲沾滯謂不足以入道然
則四勿之訓非耶噫此學之所以罕造也
田斯以觀而實用其力者可知矣必自一
介之微以至於無所不慎而其守斯固非
以逐於小也立其大固兼乎小矜其細所以
全其大也必由四勿之旨以至於無所不
察而其養斯純非事於外也由乎中以應
punctuated:
非耶？噫！此業之所以鮮植也。孔子語顔淵，以爲仁之要，必克己復禮；其目，必非禮勿視聽言動也。然後其功密，其力得有所施，而外誘不得以投其隙，學之所由純也。周程諸儒，其格言固不可殫述，盖莫非嚴畏以直其内、省察以防其間者矣。諸大儒之精密若此，又非其造詣之要乎？夫農夫之力田也，其種不必同，乃若耕必深，耨必易，則靡弗同也。不然，雖沃壤奥區，其獲也鮮矣。夫君子之學亦若是也。人見夫才辯之士，或過高而似超脱，遂以爲問學不必事也，甚至目防檢爲沾滯，謂不足以入道。然則四勿之訓非耶？噫！此學之所以罕造也。
田斯以觀，而實用其力者可知矣。必自一介之微，以至於無所不慎，而其守斯固，非以逐於小也；立其大，固兼乎小，矜其細，所以全其大也。必由四勿之旨，以至於無所不察，而其養斯純，非事於外也；由乎中以應
translation_en:
…is it wrong? Alas! This is why so few establish themselves in their endeavors. Confucius told Yan Yuan that the essential requirement for practicing humaneness was to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety. Its specific requirements were neither to look, listen, speak, nor act contrary to ritual propriety. Only then would one’s efforts be thorough and one’s strength find a proper application, while external temptations could find no opening through which to enter. This is how learning becomes pure. The exemplary sayings of the Confucian scholars Zhou and Cheng and their fellows certainly cannot be exhaustively recounted, but all concern maintaining seriousness and reverence to make the inner self upright, and examining oneself to guard against lapses. These great Confucian scholars were so exacting and meticulous: was this not also essential to their attainment? When farmers work their fields, they need not plant the same crops, but all alike must plow deeply and weed thoroughly. Otherwise, even on fertile soil in rich districts, their harvests will be scant. The gentleman’s learning is just like this. People see men of talent and eloquence whose excessively lofty stance seems to place them beyond ordinary constraints, and consequently suppose that inquiry and study need not be pursued. They even regard vigilance and restraint as impediments, saying that these are insufficient for entering the Way. Does this mean that the teaching of the Four Prohibitions is wrong? Alas! This is why so few attain mastery in learning.
Viewed in this way [?], we can recognize those who truly exert themselves. One must begin with the slightest scruple and proceed until there is nothing about which one is not careful; only then will one’s resolve be firm. This does not mean pursuing petty matters. Establishing what is great necessarily encompasses what is small; taking care over details is how one preserves the greater whole. One must follow the purport of the Four Prohibitions until there is nothing one does not scrutinize; only then will one’s self-cultivation become pure. This does not mean attending merely to externals: one proceeds from within to respond…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乎外制乎外所以養其中也遇則以之立
業而非無本不遇則以明道而非無用學
術事功隨所卷舒而明德新民之學可幾
矣此固儒生之常談也惟以爲常而弗談
而用力者鮮矣乃求所以用其力則舍此
不可也故不敢以爲常而弗談也不識執
事以爲何如
第五問
魏良靜
===
同考試官知縣洪　批〔以六事論馭將之失切中今時之弊而末復以不御馭能將又深得將將之道者經略如斯其胷中眞有數萬甲兵矣豈但可以經生目之耶敬羡敬羡〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔援古証今高文卓識將將之術宜無出此子其有文事武備者歟可爲得人慶矣〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔天下未嘗無將顧無以馭之耳子能以往事明之其留心時務者耶〕
punctuated:
乎外，制乎外所以養其中也。遇則以之立業而非無本，不遇則以明道而非無用。學術事功，隨所卷舒，而明德新民之學可幾矣。此固儒生之常談也，惟以爲常而弗談，而用力者鮮矣。乃求所以用其力，則舍此不可也。故不敢以爲常而弗談也。不識執事以爲何如？

第五問
魏良靜

同考試官知縣洪　批〔以六事論馭將之失，切中今時之弊，而末復以不御馭能將，又深得將將之道者。經略如斯，其胷中眞有數萬甲兵矣，豈但可以經生目之耶？敬羡，敬羡！〕
考試官侍讀陶　批〔援古証今，高文卓識，將將之術宜無出此。子其有文事武備者歟？可爲得人慶矣！〕
考試官洗馬馬　批〔天下未嘗無將，顧無以馭之耳。子能以往事明之，其留心時務者耶？〕
translation_en:
…to the outward; regulating outward conduct is how one nurtures what lies within. When afforded an opportunity, one uses this learning to accomplish deeds, which thus have a foundation; without such an opportunity, one uses it to illuminate the Way, and it is thus not without usefulness. Learning and practical achievement unfold or withdraw as circumstances permit, and the learning of manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people may thereby be approached. These are indeed commonplace sayings among Confucian scholars. Yet precisely because people regard them as commonplace and leave them unspoken, few exert themselves in this learning. If one seeks the means of applying one's efforts, however, one cannot dispense with this. Therefore I dare not leave it unspoken on the grounds that it is commonplace. I wonder what you, sir, think of this.

Fifth Policy Question
Wei Liangjing

Comment by Associate Examiner Hong, District Magistrate: 〔By discussing failures in managing generals under six headings, you strike directly at the abuses of our own time. At the end, you further propose managing capable generals by refraining from controlling them, profoundly grasping the Way of commanding commanders. With strategic understanding like this, you truly have tens of thousands of armored troops within your breast. How could one regard you merely as a student of the Classics? My respectful admiration, my respectful admiration!〕

Comment by Examiner Tao, Reader-in-Waiting: 〔You invoke antiquity to substantiate your account of the present: distinguished writing and outstanding insight. Surely no method of commanding commanders surpasses this. Are you perhaps one who combines civil accomplishments with military preparedness? We may celebrate having found a worthy man!〕

Comment by Examiner Ma, Librarian to the Heir Apparent: 〔The realm has never lacked generals; it has merely lacked the means to manage them. You can illuminate this through past events. Are you one who devotes close attention to current affairs?〕

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
方今爲中國患者北則有胡寇時窺亭障
犯封畧南則閩廣之賊苦於倭擾山海萑
蒲之孽因而延蔓以天下全勝之力經營
之歷歲矣厚屯集廣召募峙芻糧穀器械
凡威敵制勝之策亦旣悉舉而烽燧猶驚
膚功未奏議者謂患在於無將昔趙以李
牧守代邊匈奴遠徙吳以步騭守交州百
蠻震服彼皆區區偏安一隅猶有人焉若
此矧
===
國家兼統覆載受鉞分閫旌壘相望豈翳無
人將由任用不重措置失理責成弗專文
法太煩恩信未孚聲實莫辨凡此六者皆
足以解豪傑之體窒立功之路陸敬輿云
勝敵之要在乎將得其人馭將之方在乎
操得其柄今日之患不在無將正坐不得
馭將之方而已其方安在則執事所詢往
古之事備具之矣請得而繹陳之昔晉蒐
於被廬以謀中軍之帥郤縠以悅禮樂而
punctuated:
方今爲中國患者，北則有胡寇時窺亭障，犯封畧；南則閩廣之賊苦於倭擾，山海萑蒲之孽因而延蔓。以天下全勝之力經營之，歷歲矣。厚屯集，廣召募，峙芻糧穀器械，凡威敵制勝之策，亦旣悉舉，而烽燧猶驚，膚功未奏。議者謂患在於無將。昔趙以李牧守代邊，匈奴遠徙；吳以步騭守交州，百蠻震服。彼皆區區偏安一隅，猶有人焉若此，矧國家兼統覆載，受鉞分閫，旌壘相望，豈翳無人？將由任用不重，措置失理，責成弗專，文法太煩，恩信未孚，聲實莫辨？凡此六者，皆足以解豪傑之體，窒立功之路。陸敬輿云：「勝敵之要，在乎將得其人；馭將之方，在乎操得其柄。」今日之患，不在無將，正坐不得馭將之方而已。其方安在？則執事所詢往古之事，備具之矣。請得而繹陳之。
昔晉蒐於被廬，以謀中軍之帥，郤縠以悅禮樂而
translation_en:
At present, among the threats to the Central Realm, in the north there are Hu raiders who repeatedly spy upon our watchposts and fortifications and violate our borders; in the south, the bandits of Fujian and Guangdong suffer from the depredations of the wokou [?], while bands of outlaws in the mountains and along the coast consequently spread and multiply. The empire has devoted its full, overwhelmingly superior strength to dealing with them for years. Garrisons have been reinforced, recruits widely enlisted, and fodder, provisions, grain, and military equipment stockpiled. Every means of overawing the enemy and securing victory has already been employed. Yet the beacon fires still signal alarms, and no substantial success has been achieved. Those discussing the matter say that the trouble lies in a lack of generals.
Formerly, Zhao employed Li Mu to defend the frontier of Dai, and the Xiongnu withdrew far away; Wu employed Bu Zhi to defend Jiaozhou, and the many Man peoples submitted in awe. These were merely small states maintaining themselves in one corner of the realm, yet even they had men of such ability. How much more should our dynasty, which rules all beneath Heaven and upon Earth! Generals receive the battle-axe of command and take charge of regional military affairs; their banners and fortified camps stand within sight of one another. Can it really be that there are no capable men? Or does the problem arise because appointments carry insufficient authority, arrangements are ill-conceived, responsibility for results is divided, administrative regulations are too burdensome, imperial favor and trust have failed to inspire confidence, and reputation cannot be distinguished from actual ability? Each of these six failings is sufficient to sap the energies of outstanding men and block their path to achievement.
Lu Jingyu said: “The key to defeating the enemy lies in obtaining the right man as general; the way to direct generals lies in holding the proper means of control.” Today’s trouble is not a lack of generals: it arises precisely from failing to find the proper way to direct them. Where is that way to be found? It is fully embodied in the events of antiquity about which you have inquired. Allow me to expound and set them forth.
Formerly, Jin held a military review at Beilu to deliberate on the choice of a commander for the central army. Xi Hu, because he delighted in ritual and music and …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
敦詩書見舉荀卿與臨武君論將亦拳拳
乎六術五權三至之目而歸本於仁義蓋
其時雖列國兵爭去古未遠呂伐遺矩猶
有存者將之所重可知矣後世若祭征虜
之雅歌臨戎羊叔子之輕裘布信庶幾有
仁義禮樂餘風者然安可多得而王翦白
起之流夷都邑坑巳降則不可語仁義周
勃樊噲之輩起身吹簫販繒問又安覩所
謂禮樂而或拓地千里擅料敵之神橫身
===
百戰佐炎興之業彼足以辦吾事者又安
得不用之也執事謂王在得人不能盡如
晉楚所云是矣而今日之將豈無其人乎
惟是古者推轂授鉞跪而遣將使無天於
上無地於下振起其慷慨自效之氣然後
可以暢耿烈而集大勳而用之遲速稍間
則未足以遇不遇言也韓信亡於治粟都
尉高帝素未之奇矣當蕭何之追還乃人
心欲散之時也漢中片語即與登壇帝諒
punctuated:
敦詩書見舉。荀卿與臨武君論將，亦拳拳乎六術、五權、三至之目，而歸本於仁義。蓋其時雖列國兵爭，去古未遠，呂伐遺矩猶有存者，將之所重可知矣。後世若祭征虜之雅歌臨戎，羊叔子之輕裘布信，庶幾有仁義禮樂餘風者，然安可多得？而王翦、白起之流，夷都邑，坑巳降，則不可語仁義；周勃、樊噲之輩，起身吹簫販繒問，又安覩所謂禮樂？而或拓地千里，擅料敵之神，橫身百戰，佐炎興之業，彼足以辦吾事者，又安得不用之也？執事謂王在得人，不能盡如晉楚所云，是矣。而今日之將，豈無其人乎？
惟是古者推轂授鉞，跪而遣將，使無天於上，無地於下，振起其慷慨自效之氣，然後可以暢耿烈而集大勳。而用之遲速稍間，則未足以遇不遇言也。韓信亡於治粟都尉，高帝素未之奇矣。當蕭何之追還，乃人心欲散之時也。漢中片語，即與登壇，帝諒
translation_en:
…and was recommended for his devotion to the Poetry and Documents. When Xun Qing discussed generalship with Lord Linwu, he likewise dwelt earnestly upon the six methods, five considerations, and three ultimate principles, grounding them in benevolence and righteousness. Although the various states were then contending in war, antiquity was not yet distant, and some inherited standards of Lü’s campaigns [?] still survived. From this we may understand what was valued in a general. In later ages, General Ji, the General Who Conquers the Caitiffs, sang refined songs while confronting the enemy, and Yang Shuzi wore a light fur robe and established trust. They came close to preserving the lingering influence of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music. Yet how could such men be found in abundance? Men such as Wang Jian and Bai Qi razed cities and buried surrendered soldiers alive; one cannot speak of them in terms of benevolence and righteousness. Men such as Zhou Bo and Fan Kuai rose from among flute players and silk sellers [?]; where could one discern in them what is called ritual and music? Yet some expanded the territory by a thousand li and displayed extraordinary skill in judging the enemy; others exposed themselves in a hundred battles and assisted the rise of the Han. Since they were capable of accomplishing our purposes, how could we fail to employ them? You say that the essential thing is to obtain suitable men [?], and that they cannot all measure up to what was said in Jin and Chu. This is correct. And among today’s generals, can there truly be no suitable men?
The crucial point is that in antiquity rulers pushed the chariot wheel, bestowed the battle-axe, and knelt to send their generals forth, allowing them to acknowledge neither Heaven above nor Earth below. This stirred their fervent resolve to prove themselves in service; only then could they fully display their shining valor and achieve great merit. A slight difference in how early or late a man was employed, however, is insufficient grounds for saying whether he received recognition. Han Xin fled while serving as Commandant for Grain Management; Emperor Gao had never previously regarded him as exceptional. When Xiao He pursued him and brought him back, men’s allegiance was on the verge of dissolving. A few words at Hanzhong immediately secured his elevation upon the ceremonial platform. The emperor understood…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
何非輕許可者未見其謀而壇巳登其僣
此以聳觀聽乎耿弇稱爲北道主人世祖
久加恩慰矣當更始之敉罷兵則人心危
疑之際也床下數言乃與佩印帝知弇足
任大事者必見其謀而印始佩其因此以
服偏裨乎此畀才柄用之凖也今也握鈴
仗鉞尊矣練技與偏校分行閭譬與鄰遊
並鶩分殊也而禮猶卑名異也而事猶等
身莫使臂手不應心以致徒擁空銜難成
===
偉績其無乃任用不重矣乎選甲簡卒誓
而出師使心有進死志無退生以齊其奮
迅直前之勇然後可以固巳勢而燄堅敵
而兵之勝負互見則又當以幸不幸論也
楚誅子玉於一敗以謝申息之老說者以
再敗咎楚成矣然剛而無禮違命僨師此
而不誅何以爲國耶秦宥孟明於再衂以
啓西戎之霸論者以采蘩美秦穆矣然勞
師襲遠不聽蹇叔穆實尸之孟明何罪耶
punctuated: 何非輕許可者，未見其謀而壇巳登，其僣此以聳觀聽乎？耿弇稱爲北道主人，世祖久加恩慰矣。當更始之敉罷兵，則人心危疑之際也。床下數言，乃與佩印。帝知弇足任大事者，必見其謀而印始佩，其因此以服偏裨乎？此畀才柄用之凖也。今也，握鈴仗鉞，尊矣；練技與偏校分行，閭譬與鄰遊並鶩。分殊也，而禮猶卑；名異也，而事猶等。身莫使臂，手不應心，以致徒擁空銜，難成偉績，其無乃任用不重矣乎？選甲簡卒，誓而出師，使心有進死，志無退生，以齊其奮迅直前之勇，然後可以固巳勢而燄堅敵。而兵之勝負互見，則又當以幸不幸論也。楚誅子玉於一敗，以謝申息之老，說者以再敗咎楚成矣。然剛而無禮，違命僨師，此而不誅，何以爲國耶？秦宥孟明於再衂，以啓西戎之霸，論者以采蘩美秦穆矣。然勞師襲遠，不聽蹇叔，穆實尸之，孟明何罪耶？
translation_en:
…that [Xiao] He was not one to give his endorsement lightly. Before seeing Han Xin’s plans, the emperor had already had him ascend the platform of appointment: was he using this to impress those who watched and listened [?]? Geng Yan declared that he would be master of the northern route, and Emperor Shizu had long shown him favor and reassurance. When the Gengshi Emperor sought to disband the troops [?], people were fearful and uncertain. After a few words at the foot of the couch, Geng Yan was given a seal to wear. The emperor knew that Yan could be entrusted with great affairs; only after hearing his plans did he have him wear the seal. Was he thereby securing the submission of the subordinate commanders? These are standards for entrusting authority to talented men and employing them.

Today, those who hold the command bell [?] and wield the battle-axe occupy an exalted position. Yet in practicing military skills they take their places alongside subordinate officers, and in village activities [?] they compete alongside neighborhood companions. Their station is distinct, yet the courtesies accorded them remain lowly; their designation differs, yet their duties remain the same. The body cannot direct the arms, and the hands do not respond to the mind. Thus they merely possess empty titles and find it difficult to achieve great deeds. Is this not because insufficient weight is given to their appointment and employment?

Select armored warriors and choose soldiers; administer an oath and send the army forth. Make their hearts intent on advancing even unto death, with no thought of retreating to preserve their lives, thereby unifying their courage to surge swiftly and directly forward. Only then can one secure one’s own position and overawe a powerful enemy. Yet victory and defeat alternate in warfare, and these must also be judged in terms of good or ill fortune.

Chu put Ziyu to death after a single defeat, to make amends to the elders of Shen and Xi. Commentators blame King Cheng of Chu for this second defeat. Yet Ziyu was headstrong and lacked propriety; he disobeyed orders and brought disaster upon the army. If such a man were not executed, how could the state be governed? Qin pardoned Mengming after two defeats, thereby laying the foundations of its hegemony over the Western Rong. Commentators praise Duke Mu of Qin by invoking Gathering Southernwood. Yet it was Mu himself who was responsible for exhausting the army on a distant surprise attack and refusing to heed Jian Shu. What fault lay with Mengming?

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
此討罪宥過之準也今也列城屯戍均矣
守國不分夷險當虜不分强弱情異也而
迹則同罪一也而罰則異異庸正典奸黠
逃誅以致法紀弗彰遇敵輙潰其無乃措
置失理矣乎衛青出高闕走右賢俘裨王
𠫤人畜功固偉矣漢帝命使者持大將印
卽軍中拜之曹彬總舟師下江南降李煜
封府庫功亦不細矣宋祖初以使相見命
終復靳之以宋祖視漢帝雖若少吝然漢
===
帝以滅胡之事爲青期而宋祖以太原之
下爲彬望故一則施大恩以寵之於立功
之始一則留峻階以俟之於成功之後緩
急異用而責成之意均也今也左右推遷
前後踵繼謀方立而權任忽分事未究而
業已見代十羊九牧去徒興嗟又安得永
肩一心有遠計以裨
社稷乎此責成不專之弊也李光弼之代郭
子儀也張用濟謀以精銳入東都光弼執
punctuated: 此討罪宥過之準也。今也列城屯戍均矣，守國不分夷險，當虜不分强弱，情異也而迹則同，罪一也而罰則異，異庸正典，奸黠逃誅，以致法紀弗彰，遇敵輙潰，其無乃措置失理矣乎？衛青出高闕，走右賢，俘裨王，𠫤人畜，功固偉矣。漢帝命使者持大將印，卽軍中拜之。曹彬總舟師下江南，降李煜，封府庫，功亦不細矣。宋祖初以使相見命，終復靳之。以宋祖視漢帝，雖若少吝，然漢帝以滅胡之事爲青期，而宋祖以太原之下爲彬望，故一則施大恩以寵之於立功之始，一則留峻階以俟之於成功之後，緩急異用，而責成之意均也。今也左右推遷，前後踵繼，謀方立而權任忽分，事未究而業已見代，十羊九牧，去徒興嗟，又安得永肩一心，有遠計以裨社稷乎？此責成不專之弊也。李光弼之代郭子儀也，張用濟謀以精銳入東都，光弼執
translation_en:
This is the standard for punishing crimes and pardoning errors. Today, garrisons are stationed throughout the cities alike. In defending the state, no distinction is made between easy and difficult terrain; in confronting the enemy, none is made between strong and weak forces. Circumstances differ, yet outward conduct is treated as identical; offenses are the same, yet punishments differ. The established statutes are applied differently [?], and the crafty escape punishment. Consequently, military law and discipline fail to command respect, and troops collapse whenever they meet the enemy. Does this not suggest that the arrangements are ill conceived?

Wei Qing marched out through Gaoque, routed the King of the Right Worthies, captured subordinate kings, and seized people and livestock [?]. His achievement was certainly great. The Han emperor ordered an envoy to take the seal of General-in-Chief and confer the appointment upon him in the army’s camp. Cao Bin commanded the fleet that conquered Jiangnan, secured Li Yu’s surrender, and sealed the government storehouses and treasuries. His achievement, too, was considerable. The founding emperor of the Song initially promised him appointment as an honorary Chief Councillor, but ultimately withheld it. Compared with the Han emperor, the Song founder might seem somewhat grudging. Yet the Han emperor expected Wei Qing to destroy the northern peoples, while the Song founder hoped that Cao Bin would capture Taiyuan. Thus, the one bestowed great favor to honor his commander at the outset of his achievements; the other reserved an exalted rank to await the completion of his commander’s task. Though they differed in whether they acted promptly or delayed, their intention to hold their commanders responsible for success was the same.

Today, men are shifted from one post to another, successors following one upon another. A plan has barely been established when authority and responsibility are suddenly divided; an undertaking has not yet been carried through when its commander is already replaced. There are nine shepherds for ten sheep, and departures merely occasion sighs [?]. How, then, can men long shoulder their responsibilities with a united purpose and devise far-reaching plans to benefit the altars of soil and grain? This is the harm caused by failing to vest responsibility for success in one person.

When Li Guangbi replaced Guo Ziyi, Zhang Yongji planned to enter the Eastern Capital with elite troops. Li Guangbi arrested him…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而斬之以部將代領其衆王猛之伐慕容
暐也鄧羌堅臥請司隷景略馳往許之然
後運矛赴敵以景略視光弼雖若少徇然
光弼以用濟不斬令不肅而景略以鄧羌
不往燕不平故一則旌旗改色而思明䘐
一則奮兵長驅而鄴城破剛柔異用而應
變之機一也今也檄符旁午奏牒絡繹首
功繩於幕府之法軍租制於守藏之吏一
室卒尖動疑有觸又安能展布四體有遂
===
事以利
國家乎此文法太煩之弊也李漢超在關南
民有訟强娶其女不償其錢者然關南賴
超故陽責其人遣之以安其心而陰諭之
改不然長惡不悛當如後患何法固寓於
愛之中矣此漢超之所以感泣而修政焉
郭進守西山軍校有訟進不法者然其事
誣進故執其人送進令殺之以快其意然
天子所賜豈有竟殺者仁固行乎法之外
punctuated:
而斬之，以部將代領其衆。王猛之伐慕容暐也，鄧羌堅臥請司隷，景略馳往許之，然後運矛赴敵。以景略視光弼，雖若少徇，然光弼以用濟不斬令不肅，而景略以鄧羌不往燕不平。故一則旌旗改色而思明䘐，一則奮兵長驅而鄴城破。剛柔異用，而應變之機一也。今也檄符旁午，奏牒絡繹，首功繩於幕府之法，軍租制於守藏之吏，一室卒尖，動疑有觸，又安能展布四體，有遂事以利國家乎？此文法太煩之弊也。
李漢超在關南，民有訟强娶其女、不償其錢者。然關南賴超，故陽責其人遣之，以安其心，而陰諭之改。不然，長惡不悛，當如後患何？法固寓於愛之中矣。此漢超之所以感泣而修政焉。郭進守西山，軍校有訟進不法者。然其事誣進，故執其人送進，令殺之，以快其意。然天子所賜，豈有竟殺者？仁固行乎法之外
translation_en:
…and beheaded him, appointing a subordinate commander to lead his troops in his place. When Wang Meng attacked Murong Wei, Deng Qiang remained obstinately in bed and demanded appointment as Metropolitan Commandant. Jinglue [Wang Meng] hurried to him and agreed; only then did Deng take up his spear and charge the enemy. Compared with Li Guangbi, Jinglue might seem somewhat indulgent. Yet Guangbi judged that unless Zhang Yongji was executed, military discipline could not be maintained; Jinglue judged that unless Deng Qiang advanced, Yan could not be subdued. Thus, in the one case, the banners took on a changed aspect and Shi Siming suffered defeat; in the other, the troops surged forward in a long advance and the city of Ye fell. Firmness and flexibility were employed differently, but the capacity to respond to circumstances was the same. Nowadays, military dispatches and warrants fly in every direction, and memorials and official documents follow in an unending stream. Credit for enemy heads taken is constrained by the regulations of the military headquarters, and military revenues are controlled by treasury clerks. [The phrase 一室卒尖 is garbled; its meaning is uncertain.] At every move, commanders fear transgressing some rule. How, then, can they freely exercise their abilities and accomplish deeds that benefit the state? This is the harm caused by excessively complicated administrative rules.
When Li Hanchao was stationed in Guannan, a commoner brought a complaint that he had forcibly taken the man's daughter as a wife and failed to repay his money. But Guannan depended on Hanchao, so the emperor publicly rebuked and dismissed the complainant to reassure Hanchao, while privately instructing Hanchao to mend his ways. Otherwise, if he persisted unrepentantly in wrongdoing, how could the ensuing troubles be dealt with? Law was thus embodied within benevolence. This was why Hanchao wept with gratitude and improved his administration. When Guo Jin defended Xishan, a military officer accused him of unlawful conduct. But the accusation against Jin was false, so the emperor had the man arrested and sent to Jin, ordering Jin to kill him to gratify his feelings. Yet how could one actually kill someone bestowed by the Son of Heaven? Benevolence was thus exercised beyond the law…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣此其人所以踴躍而立功焉宋祖之待
二將皆厚之以誠也不然因人言而稍存
其迹則漢超將以有罪自疑而進亦以不
自懷慮矣何以慰爲將之心而鼓其敵愾
之勇哉今日之待將大率類此故曰恩信
未孚也李廣爲未央衛尉其屯邊也無部
伍行陣不擊刁斗不事文籍就善水草屯
止軍中有簡易之稱矣然廣之略遠常運
於紀律之外勇且以飛將畏之况敢犯乎
===
有將如此簡何嫌耶程不識爲長樂衛尉
其屯邊也正部伍行陣擊刁斗治軍簿至
明不得休息軍中有煩擾之苦矣然不識
之慮周常嚴乎紀律之中自言勇不得犯
我况遇害乎有將如此嚴何嫌耶漢武之
用二將皆察乎其實也不然聽虛聲而不
究其實則廣嘗以不遵兵法棄而不識且
以不知大體黜矣何以盡爲將之才而收
其折衝之效哉今日之論將大率類此故
punctuated:
矣。此其人所以踴躍而立功焉。宋祖之待二將，皆厚之以誠也。不然，因人言而稍存其迹，則漢超將以有罪自疑，而進亦以不自懷慮矣。何以慰爲將之心，而鼓其敵愾之勇哉？今日之待將，大率類此，故曰恩信未孚也。
李廣爲未央衛尉，其屯邊也，無部伍行陣，不擊刁斗，不事文籍，就善水草屯止，軍中有簡易之稱矣。然廣之略遠，常運於紀律之外，勇且以飛將畏之，况敢犯乎？有將如此，簡何嫌耶？程不識爲長樂衛尉，其屯邊也，正部伍行陣，擊刁斗，治軍簿至明，不得休息，軍中有煩擾之苦矣。然不識之慮周，常嚴乎紀律之中，自言勇不得犯我，况遇害乎？有將如此，嚴何嫌耶？漢武之用二將，皆察乎其實也。不然，聽虛聲而不究其實，則廣嘗以不遵兵法棄，而不識且以不知大體黜矣。何以盡爲將之才，而收其折衝之效哉？今日之論將，大率類此，故
translation_en:
…Thus this man eagerly rendered meritorious service. In his treatment of these two generals, Song Taizu showed both generosity and sincerity. Otherwise, had he allowed others’ accusations to leave even a slight trace of suspicion, Li Hanchao would have doubted his own standing as one deemed guilty, while Guo Jin too would have harbored fears for his security [?]. How could this have reassured his generals and stirred their courage against the enemy? The treatment of generals today largely resembles this latter course; hence I say that favor and trust have yet to inspire confidence.
Li Guang served as Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison at Weiyang Palace. When stationed on the frontier, he dispensed with organized units and battle formations, did not have the watch kettles struck, and did not concern himself with written records. He encamped wherever water and pasture were good, and his army was known for its simplicity and ease. Yet Guang’s strategy was far-reaching, often operating beyond formal military regulations. Even the brave [?] feared him as the “Flying General”; how would they dare attack him? With such a general, what objection could there be to simplicity? Cheng Bushi served as Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison at Changle Palace. When stationed on the frontier, he kept units and battle formations in proper order, had the watch kettles struck, and worked on military registers until dawn, allowing no rest. His army suffered from troublesome demands. Yet Bushi’s deliberations were comprehensive, and he consistently maintained strict military discipline. He himself said that the brave [?] could not attack him; how much less would he suffer harm? With such a general, what objection could there be to strictness? Emperor Wu of Han employed both generals with an understanding of their actual capabilities. Otherwise, had he listened to empty reports without investigating the realities, Guang would have been rejected for failing to observe military methods, and Bushi dismissed for failing to grasp the larger essentials. How could he then have fully drawn upon their talents as generals and secured their success in repelling the enemy? Assessments of generals today largely resemble this latter course; hence…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
曰聲實莫辨也夫以古人勉敵馭將之機
班班若彼而今時之弊動與古人相反又
往往若此則夫邊烽所以未熄海波所以
不靖信非無將之患而不得馭將之方之
爲患矣誠能按古人之成法參時事之通
變破拘攣之陋談振因循之積弊權不分
於衆則任用重罰必麗於情則措置當專
責成以致卓犖之用寬文法以容跅弛之
才厚恩信以感其心辨聲實以作其效將
===
見精神折衝風聲鼓舞四方負奇不羈之
士必望風景從思自表見立功名於疆場
之上古今人不甚相遠安知無昔時桀老
上之庭係尉陀之頸者出其間乎故愚謂
今南北之寇舉不足患所可患者馭將不
得其方而已雖然此因執事之問而論馭
將之方也抑猶有不御之說焉蓋兵機天
下之至速者也岐路躊躇坐失千里矣變
生呼吸間不一髮矣而可從中覆乎且既
punctuated:
曰：聲實莫辨也。夫以古人勉敵馭將之機，班班若彼，而今時之弊，動與古人相反，又往往若此，則夫邊烽所以未熄，海波所以不靖，信非無將之患，而不得馭將之方之爲患矣。誠能按古人之成法，參時事之通變，破拘攣之陋談，振因循之積弊，權不分於衆，則任用重；罰必麗於情，則措置當。專責成以致卓犖之用，寬文法以容跅弛之才，厚恩信以感其心，辨聲實以作其效，將見精神折衝，風聲鼓舞，四方負奇不羈之士，必望風景從，思自表見，立功名於疆場之上。古今人不甚相遠，安知無昔時桀老上之庭、係尉陀之頸者出其間乎？故愚謂今南北之寇，舉不足患，所可患者，馭將不得其方而已。
雖然，此因執事之問而論馭將之方也，抑猶有不御之說焉。蓋兵機，天下之至速者也，岐路躊躇，坐失千里矣；變生呼吸，間不一髮矣，而可從中覆乎？且既
translation_en:
…I say: reputation and reality cannot be distinguished. The ancients’ methods of confronting the enemy [?] and directing generals were so clearly evident, yet present abuses repeatedly run counter to their practices, occurring again and again as described above. Thus, the reason the frontier beacon fires have not died out and the seas remain unsettled is truly not a lack of generals: the trouble lies in failing to find the proper way to direct them. If we could indeed examine the established methods of the ancients, adapt them to changing circumstances today, dispel narrow and blinkered arguments, and remedy the accumulated abuses of habitual inaction, then authority would not be divided among many, and appointments would carry weight; punishments would accord with the actual circumstances, and measures would be appropriate. Give generals sole responsibility for achieving results, so that their exceptional abilities may be put to use; relax formal regulations to accommodate unrestrained talent; extend generous favor and trust to move their hearts; and distinguish reputation from reality to bring forth their accomplishments. Then we would see their spirit repel aggression and their reputation inspire others. Men of extraordinary ability and independent spirit throughout the realm would surely respond to this example, following like shadows, eager to distinguish themselves and win merit and renown on the frontier. People of ancient and modern times are not so very different. How can we know that among them none will emerge to match those of former times who humbled Laoshang’s court [?] and bound Wei Tuo by the neck? Thus, in my humble opinion, none of the invaders now troubling north and south need cause anxiety. What should cause anxiety is merely the failure to direct generals properly.
Nevertheless, this discussion of how to direct generals responds to your question; there is also an argument for refraining from controlling them. Opportunities in warfare are the most fleeting things under Heaven. Hesitate at a fork in the road, and a thousand miles are lost through inaction. A change arises within a single breath, with not a hair’s breadth of time to spare: can decisions then be referred back to the court for review? Moreover, once…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以爲能而用之矣又恐其不足以濟吾事
是不推心而置腹也既以重權畀之矣又
令其受制於人是欲掣肘而學書也故兵
法曰將能而君不御者勝蓋謂此也夫馭
御一也而言者之意則微有辨陸贄之所
謂馭者駕馭之謂也是鼓舞豪傑者也兵
法之所謂不御者覊御之謂也是束縛若
牛馬者也是故可以馭可以無御而中持
衡焉其斯爲人君之善將將乎愚生不知
兵姑掇拾所聞如此惟執事進而教之幸
甚
punctuated: 以爲能而用之矣，又恐其不足以濟吾事，是不推心而置腹也。既以重權畀之矣，又令其受制於人，是欲掣肘而學書也。故兵法曰：「將能而君不御者勝。」蓋謂此也。夫馭、御一也，而言者之意則微有辨。陸贄之所謂馭者，駕馭之謂也，是鼓舞豪傑者也；兵法之所謂不御者，覊御之謂也，是束縛若牛馬者也。是故可以馭，可以無御，而中持衡焉，其斯爲人君之善將將乎？愚生不知兵，姑掇拾所聞如此，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…having judged him capable and employed him, yet still fearing that he cannot accomplish one’s purposes: this is failing to open one’s heart and place trust in him. Having entrusted him with great authority, yet making him subject to others’ control: this is like wishing to learn calligraphy while having one’s elbow restrained. Thus the Art of War says: “He whose general is capable and whose ruler does not interfere will win.” This, surely, is what it means.

The words yu 馭 and yu 御 mean the same thing, but the intentions of those using them differ subtly. What Lu Zhi calls “guiding” means directing and leading: it inspires men of outstanding ability. The “control” rejected by the Art of War means bridling and restraining: it binds men like oxen and horses. Thus one may guide while refraining from restraint, maintaining a proper balance between the two. Is this not what it means for a ruler to be skilled at commanding commanders?

I, an ignorant student, know nothing of warfare and have merely gathered together what I have heard, as set out here. If you, honored sir, would offer me further instruction, I would be most fortunate.

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
我
皇上御曆之四年爲隆慶庚午天下
當再試士于鄉〔臣自强 臣大臨〕
奉
欽命來典應天府試事臣竊伏自
念臣學術淺陋濫塵侍從竊祿
===
有年愧未能效萬分一乃今承
乏校文賢才所由進厥惟重任
大懼不敏或甄別弗當無能稱
任使罪盆滋甚蓋自聞
命以迄于兹日夜兢惕若有神焉
鑒臨于上于左右不容頃刻懈
也事竣錄成臣大臨猥以職事
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序

我皇上御曆之四年，爲隆慶庚午，天下當再試士于鄉。〔臣自强 臣大臨〕奉欽命來典應天府試事。臣竊伏自念：臣學術淺陋，濫塵侍從，竊祿有年，愧未能效萬分一。乃今承乏校文，賢才所由進，厥惟重任。大懼不敏，或甄別弗當，無能稱任使，罪盆滋甚。蓋自聞命以迄于兹，日夜兢惕，若有神焉，鑒臨于上、于左右，不容頃刻懈也。事竣錄成，臣大臨猥以職事
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

The fourth year of our emperor’s reign was the gengwu year of Longqing (1570), when scholars throughout the realm were again due to sit the Provincial Examination. 〔Your servants Ziqiang and Dalin〕 received an imperial command to come and preside over the examination in Yingtian Prefecture. Your servant humbly reflects: my learning is shallow and meager; undeservedly occupying a place among the imperial attendants, I have drawn a salary for years, ashamed that I have been unable to render even one ten-thousandth of the service owed. Now I have been called upon, for want of someone better, to evaluate examination essays. Since this is the means by which worthy talent advances, the responsibility is indeed weighty. I greatly feared that, lacking discernment, I might judge candidates improperly and fail to fulfill my commission, thereby aggravating my culpability [?]. From the time I received the command until now, I have been vigilant and apprehensive day and night, as though spirits were watching over me from above and on either side, permitting not a moment’s slackness. With the examination concluded and the record completed, your servant Dalin, unworthily charged with these official duties …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
謹中言于簡末曰自昔世道關
於人才人才係於學術故學術
不可不慎也我
聖祖奮起淮右甫入金陵遂建禮賢
之館聘劉基宋濂輩論經史訪
治道當是時疆宇未拓也而辨
學術審好尚已先衆務舉矣比
===
定制取士一本於聖賢之學而
又拳拳以文質得中名實相稱
為
諭焉誠見夫士非此不可以學而
用人圖治者非此不可以用也
列聖相承率由斯道名卿碩輔焜耀
後先用能裨翼洪庥流澤無際
punctuated: 謹中言于簡末曰：「自昔世道關於人才，人才係於學術，故學術不可不慎也。我聖祖奮起淮右，甫入金陵，遂建禮賢之館，聘劉基、宋濂輩論經史，訪治道。當是時，疆宇未拓也，而辨學術、審好尚，已先衆務舉矣。比定制取士，一本於聖賢之學，而又拳拳以文質得中、名實相稱為諭焉。誠見夫士非此不可以學，而用人圖治者非此不可以用也。列聖相承，率由斯道，名卿碩輔焜耀後先，用能裨翼洪庥，流澤無際。
translation_en: …respectfully sets forth these words [?] at the end of the record: “From antiquity, the condition of the world has depended upon men of talent, and men of talent upon learning. Thus learning must be approached with care. Our Sagely Founder rose in Huaiyou. As soon as he entered Jinling, he established a hall for honoring worthy men and summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, and others to discuss the classics and histories and to inquire into the way of governing. At that time, his territory had not yet expanded, yet distinguishing sound learning and carefully judging what should be esteemed already took precedence over all other affairs. When regulations for selecting officials through examinations were established, they were grounded entirely in the learning of the sages and worthies. He also earnestly instructed that literary refinement and substance should attain a proper balance, and that reputation and reality should correspond. He clearly perceived that scholars could not properly pursue learning without this, and that those who employed men to achieve good government could not properly appoint them without it. Successive sage sovereigns followed this same path. Distinguished ministers and eminent chief councillors shone in generation after generation; thus they were able to sustain the dynasty’s great blessings and spread its beneficence without limit…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
非學術正而得人盛之明效歟
比年以來文盛勝質士習稍漓
有識者深用爲慮蓋自
先帝晚禩已欲挽其敝而歸之中矣
肆我
皇上潛心聖學興起斯文
登極之歲卽
===
幸太學祀孔子
以身示天下且申飭有司端士習
正文體益諄諄加意焉夫上之
所向下之所趨也卽疏遐阻僻
凡聲教所可暨罔不忻忻嚮風
祇若
彝訓矧茲
punctuated: 非學術正而得人盛之明效歟？比年以來，文盛勝質，士習稍漓，有識者深用爲慮。蓋自先帝晚禩，已欲挽其敝而歸之中矣。肆我皇上潛心聖學，興起斯文，登極之歲卽幸太學，祀孔子，以身示天下，且申飭有司，端士習，正文體，益諄諄加意焉。夫上之所向，下之所趨也。卽疏遐阻僻，凡聲教所可暨，罔不忻忻嚮風，祇若彝訓。矧茲
translation_en: …Is this not clear proof of the efficacy of sound learning and the abundant recruitment of worthy men? In recent years, literary embellishment has flourished at the expense of substance, and scholars’ habits have grown somewhat lax. Discerning men have been deeply concerned about this. Indeed, already in the late years of the previous emperor’s reign, he wished to remedy these failings and restore a proper balance. Thus our present Emperor has devoted himself to the learning of the sages and fostered this cultural tradition. In the year of his accession, he visited the Imperial University and offered sacrifice to Confucius, setting an example for all under Heaven through his own conduct. He further admonished the responsible officials to rectify scholars’ habits and correct literary style, giving these matters ever more earnest attention. For whatever those above favor, those below pursue. Even in distant, inaccessible, and secluded places, wherever imperial instruction and civilizing influence can reach, all gladly turn toward that influence and reverently follow the enduring precepts. How much more so here…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
畿甸重地我
聖祖開先文敎化所由始者乎又剏
茲六館諸曹皆四方豐庠之彥
旣承我
皇上恩意掄選而至者乎故今觀其
所爲文雖神采異齊裁致各別
類皆原本經傳闡發性眞崇雅
黜浮敷華茂實體要得而粹美
備矣以臣心目所寓合式者誠
===
衆郎
恩制所增廣弗能盡錄也於戲盛
哉此非所謂文質得中名實相
稱者耶非士習端而文體正耶
非夫
punctuated: 畿甸重地，我聖祖開先文敎化所由始者乎？又剏茲六館，諸曹皆四方豐庠之彥，旣承我皇上恩意掄選而至者乎？故今觀其所爲文，雖神采異齊，裁致各別，類皆原本經傳，闡發性眞，崇雅黜浮，敷華茂實，體要得而粹美備矣。以臣心目所寓，合式者誠衆，郎恩制所增廣，弗能盡錄也。於戲，盛哉！此非所謂文質得中，名實相稱者耶？非士習端而文體正耶？非夫
translation_en:
…this important metropolitan region, where our sagely founder first established literary instruction and moral transformation [?]? Moreover, he founded these Six Colleges; are not all these men outstanding scholars from flourishing schools throughout the realm, who have come here through selection under our Emperor’s gracious intentions?

Thus, examining their writings now, although their spirit and brilliance differ in degree and their composition and expression vary, they generally take the Classics and their commentaries as their foundation, elucidate the truth of human nature, esteem refinement and reject superficiality, and combine flowering expression with abundant substance. They grasp the essentials and possess purity and beauty in full. Among those that I, your servant, have considered, truly many meet the prescribed standards. Even with the expansion graciously decreed [?], it is impossible to include them all.

Ah, how splendid! Is this not what is meant by achieving a proper balance between refinement and substance, and making reputation correspond to reality? Does it not show that scholars’ habits are upright and their literary style correct? Is it not that …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
王國之禛與夫四方之彥培養滲
而蘊藉厚者能然耶庶幾哉可
藉是以復
主上矣雖然〔臣〕尤不能無懼也夫士
今日之爲言也弁包廣博究析
精微其文固彬彬然正矣然所
以務此者其幾有二又不可不
===
辨也以求道爲務則弁包究析
入於目會於心者皆道也亦文
也得其本而該其末也聖賢之
學也以�η文爲務則入於目會
於心者皆文也非道也狥其末
而遺其本也舉子之業也今諸
士果皆聖賢之學乎〔臣〕李敢必
punctuated:
王國之禛與夫四方之彥，培養滲而蘊藉厚者，能然耶？庶幾哉，可藉是以復主上矣。雖然，〔臣〕尤不能無懼也。夫士今日之爲言也，弁包廣博，究析精微，其文固彬彬然正矣。然所以務此者，其幾有二，又不可不辨也。
以求道爲務，則弁包究析，入於目、會於心者，皆道也，亦文也，得其本而該其末也，聖賢之學也。以�η文爲務，則入於目、會於心者，皆文也，非道也，狥其末而遺其本也，舉子之業也。今諸士果皆聖賢之學乎？〔臣〕李敢必
translation_en:
…could the auspicious talents [?] of the royal realm and the outstanding men of the four quarters achieve this through deeply permeating nurture [?] and richly accumulated learning? We may indeed hope so: on this basis we can report back to His Majesty. Nevertheless, your servant cannot help feeling apprehensive. In what these scholars write today, their coverage is broad and comprehensive, their investigation and analysis subtle and precise. Their compositions are certainly refined and proper. Yet there are two possible motives for pursuing this, and these must be distinguished.
If they devote themselves to seeking the Way, then, in their comprehensive treatment and searching analysis, everything that enters their eyes and is grasped by their minds is the Way, and is also literary expression. They grasp the root and encompass the branches: this is the learning of sages and worthies. If they devote themselves to literary composition [?], then everything that enters their eyes and is grasped by their minds is literary expression, but not the Way. They pursue the branches and abandon the root: this is the occupation of examination candidates. Do all these scholars now truly pursue the learning of sages and worthies? Your servant would not dare to affirm [?]…

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也抑舉子之業已乎則其言固
聖賢也爲其言之聖賢也而取
之而或不以聖賢之學自務非
欺乎取士而或售其欺是臣所
大懼也臣願諸士無忘今日之
言而實以聖賢之學自務也士
實以聖賢自務業不必改習也
===
卽今日之言一反諸身心焉而
聖賢在是矣而或不然者有以
移之也卑者悅紛華逐聲利知
耻者所弗屑無足深論高者搜
奇衒異以翰墨爲勳業而無與
於身心或從事身心矣又脫略
於存養省察謂可頓造而卒乖
punctuated: 也。抑舉子之業已乎？則其言固聖賢也。爲其言之聖賢也而取之，而或不以聖賢之學自務，非欺乎？取士而或售其欺，是臣所大懼也。臣願諸士無忘今日之言，而實以聖賢之學自務也。士實以聖賢自務，業不必改習也。卽今日之言，一反諸身心焉，而聖賢在是矣。而或不然者，有以移之也。卑者悅紛華，逐聲利，知耻者所弗屑，無足深論。高者搜奇衒異，以翰墨爲勳業，而無與於身心；或從事身心矣，又脫略於存養省察，謂可頓造，而卒乖
translation_en:
… Or is theirs merely the work of examination candidates? Their words are certainly those of the sages and worthies. If we select them because their words are those of the sages and worthies, yet some do not devote themselves to the learning of the sages and worthies, is this not deception? That, in selecting men for office, we might allow their deception to succeed is what your servant greatly fears. Your servant hopes that all these scholars will remember what they have said today and truly devote themselves to the learning of the sages and worthies. If scholars truly devote themselves to becoming sages and worthies, they need not change the studies they pursue. They need only take the words they have written today and turn them back upon their own persons and minds: the way of the sages and worthies lies right here.

If some fail to do so, it is because something diverts them. Those of a lower sort delight in dazzling splendor and pursue reputation and gain—things that anyone with a sense of shame would disdain, and that do not merit extended discussion. Those of a higher sort seek out the extraordinary and flaunt the unusual, treating literary composition as meritorious achievement while leaving their own persons and minds untouched. Some do apply themselves to their persons and minds, yet neglect the work of preserving and nurturing the mind and of examining themselves, claiming that they can attain the goal at once, only in the end to depart from …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
於實用才知之士或往往然也
而聖賢之學湮矣則士習何如
耶是〔臣〕之所大懼也〔臣〕故願諸
士無忘今日之言而一反諸身
心也昔伊尹之出也有幡然之
數語傅說之出也則對揚之三
篇言於前而信於後若符契不
爽也今諸士出矣行將試南宮
===
對
大廷布列有位乃先資自獻之言
固在異日者執是以律諸士誠
聖賢之學自務誠見之實用則
習誠端名實誠稱無忝我
聖朝所崇尚無負我
punctuated: 於實用。才知之士，或往往然也，而聖賢之學湮矣，則士習何如耶？是〔臣〕之所大懼也。〔臣〕故願諸士無忘今日之言，而一反諸身心也。昔伊尹之出也，有幡然之數語；傅說之出也，則對揚之三篇。言於前而信於後，若符契不爽也。今諸士出矣，行將試南宮，對大廷，布列有位。乃先資自獻之言，固在異日者，執是以律諸士。誠聖賢之學自務，誠見之實用，則習誠端，名實誠稱，無忝我聖朝所崇尚，無負我
translation_en: …in practical application. Men of talent and intelligence often act in this way, and the learning of the sages and worthies falls into obscurity. What, then, becomes of scholars’ habits? This is what your servant greatly fears. Your servant therefore hopes that you gentlemen will not forget what you have said today, but will turn it all back upon your own persons and minds. When Yi Yin emerged to serve, there were those few words about his decisive change of resolve; when Fu Yue emerged to serve, there were the three chapters in which he responded to and extolled his ruler’s charge. What they said beforehand was borne out afterward, matching as precisely as the two halves of a tally. Now you gentlemen have emerged. Soon you will sit the Metropolitan Examination, respond at the Palace Examination, and take your places in official posts. We therefore draw beforehand upon the words with which you present yourselves, intending to use them in the future as the standard by which to judge you [?]. If you truly make the learning of the sages and worthies your own endeavor, and truly manifest it in practical application, then your habits will indeed be upright, and your reputation will indeed accord with your substance. You will bring no dishonor upon what our sagely dynasty esteems, nor disappoint our …

title: 隆慶四年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上興起申飭至意則豈惟諸士有
休聞哉而臣之懼始釋矣諸士
其勉哉諸士其勉哉
翰林院侍讀陶大臨謹序
punctuated:
皇上興起申飭至意，則豈惟諸士有休聞哉？而臣之懼始釋矣。諸士其勉哉！諸士其勉哉！
翰林院侍讀陶大臨謹序。
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s earnest intention to inspire and admonish them—then would it be only the candidates who gain an honorable reputation? Only then would your servant’s apprehension be dispelled. Candidates, strive diligently! Candidates, strive diligently!
Preface respectfully written by Tao Dalin, Reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
